-Imagine a game titled ''Sniper Elite'' but you use melee, pistol and smg 90% of the time. Yeah. Most encounters are close range, you rarely get to use your sniper. This was the biggest let down about the game.

-DLCs. My god. Curse whoever invented this ''DLC'' nonsense. If you buy the standard version of this game you only get access to like a quarter of the actual existing content. Most of the missions are behind a MASSIVE paywall. DLCs are like x3 times the price of the base game when combined. They took it way too far with this game.

-Broken AI. It seems to me the germans share a telepathic connection because soon as you make the slightest disturbance you will be swarmed from all sides. Oh and they will aimbot you with a pistol from a hundred meters away. They never seem to miss. On any difficulty. 

-Unclear missions. On three seperate occasions I had to look up on youtube where to go because some missions are really obscure. No indicators or anything just wasting my time running around not finding it.

-Mission 9 is a joke. It takes literally 10 seconds to complete. You just shoot one high profile target from afar and it's over. They should've just included that in the end of mission 8 after a cutscene. Are they trying to boost up the number of missions by doing this? 10 SECONDS for the whole mission. How is this justified?

-Shallow characters and weak story ruins the immersion.

-Invasion. They apparently added this multiplayer system like in dark souls where you invade other players worlds and try to kill them. No thank you. I turned it off after my first encounter. Game is already hard enough for you to get invaded by some sweat with hundreds of hours to hop in and grief your game. I'm good. Plus you can't save/load or even pause the game while he's in your world for obvious reasons. Just an inconvenience I'd rather avoid and instead play my own little solo dolo stealth action game.

Extremely overpriced. Not a bad game per se but completely forgettable and average passtime.

I'll preface this short review by stating, as someone who exhaustively played Sniper Elite 4, that your experience with Sniper Elite 5 will greatly depend on your appreciation of SE4. That's not to say that Sniper Elite 5 isn't enjoyable, but it does feel like Rebellion have taken a couple of baby steps forward, and a big leap backwards.

I really appreciated the inclusion of the weapon modification system and surprisingly loved the new campaign invasion mode; but outside these two additions, I found a lot of issues which really need to be addressed. The most frustrating of these problems has been the size of game updates, with single campaign or multiplayer map updates often requiring 30GB downloads, whether you've got access to the content or not. A fix was attempted, which failed miserably and stopped some players being able to launch the game at all. With the last campaign map of Season Pass 2 now out, it seems these updates won't be as frequent, but it simply hasn't been handled well.

The campaign is also strewn with issues: the story is generic, the threat the enemy poses is never well explained, Karl's commentary of situations and enemy intel is laughably poor, many of the maps feel rigid or restrictive, which in turn limits sniping opportunities, enemy AI is confusingly inept at the best of times, and the list goes on.

The game still has many positives which have carried over from Sniper Elite 4, but it should have been so much better. Rebellion had an absolute masterpiece to build on and haven't executed it well. I'm putting a thumbs up here, but with a caveat. Do not purchase this if you're looking for a successor to SE4, because this is a clear downgrade. Pick it up on sale if you love the franchise, otherwise, spend your money elsewhere.

Coop - Play story missions with other players
Invasions - Invade another player and try to take them out, or the other way around
Survival - Defend command posts with other players against waves of enemies
PVP multiplayer - Various modes of standard multiplayer with levels and stuff to unlock

It's just good enough to pass. But barely. Still good enough to keep me playing, slowly, for dozens of hours, so it's doing something right...

- The story is bland (solo agent singlehandedly penetrates Nazi strongholds and disables a WMD).
But... It holds things together.

- The freedom is annoyingly restricted - maps are just patches of gameplay in a LARGE map, but connected by narrow paths that artificially confine player movement. It's annoying that a small hedge holds you back, and you can't climb in/out trenches, and you cannot jump... Not at all. So many things look entirely traversable but aren't.
But... You get used to it, and at least you can *shoot* all across the map. Which you sometimes need to do, and albeit artificial, it keeps you from too much running & gunning (at least on higher levels because you die easily).

- They say the sniping is "authentic"... But you just press "space" and a useful diamond comes up that assists in headshot after headshot even at extremely long distances. And there is x-ray vision for enemies you saw once, which makes it incredibly easy to plan a route and stay undetected, just as long as you have patience.
But... Yeah, shooting is fun.

- The enemy AI is one of the most braindead AI's ever in a game like this. They see five of their buddies getting headshotted in a building doorway, and they think "hey, maybe if I walk through the door as well, I catch the sniper, hey you know what? let me LOUDLY yell ahead that I'm coming through as well". It's ridiculous. They are alone, and they loudly yell to their imaginary friend or to me, the sniper, just to let me know they're there, so I can take them down with great ease. They don't listen, they don't look around, they don't work together, they don't take cover, they don't change weapons, they don't take strategic positions, they don't create funnels, they don't draw me out of a hiding place (except from the odd grenade), they don't cover each other, they don't care at all about their wounded buddies, they glitch and look/shoot through doors and walls...
But... No, there's no but for this one. The insanely terrible AI is, for me, by far the hardest hit on the immersion, and made me ragequit often.

But the maps are gorgeous and large, and the environments (especially the indoors) are detailed, chaotic and very well done. Even if traversing chokepoints is often extremely artificial and limiting. It's fun mowing down countless numbers of bad guys in a combination of slowly scouting from the edges of the map, and then barging in and having hectic firefights in maze-like indoors quarters, churches, science stations, armories etc..

I'm not military, so I have no idea if this is is anything like sniping at all, but "authentic sniping"? Nah, absolutely, definitely not even close.

Survivor mode is challenging and really tests your skills. I have not played invasion mode or multi-player yet - long overdue! There are much less bugs since first release. There are still some bugs but they're minimal and don't ruin the game. DLC campaigns are much too small and need considerable expansion (compared to SE4).  I play SE5 on a dedicated PC that exceeds recommended spec, without other game software or commercial software running on it - as a result I've had no technical or functional issues.

2. You can adjust your zero, but the increments are shoddy beyond 300m with big gaps between the different ranges on most scopes, making it basically nearly useless to engage beyond 300m regardless of how much magnification you have (that's fine, but it could've been better).

Loved playing SE5. 

Have been a fan of the series since SE V2. (Never played the original SE1.)

It's expected that each game in the series somehow improves upon the last. SE5 does continue with that ethos. 

Possibly the strongest element of SE5 is that the graphics have taken a strong upturn. Everywhere in this game looks completely authentic. Authentic to the point where I regularly stopped in my tracks and look at what's going on around me. I was fully admiring the graphics generally anyway, but sometimes the graphics stop you dead. Not only do places look real, and the art direction gorgeous, but textures stand up to seriously close inspection. 

To relate to SE4 which looked gorgeous, SE5 is a step up. It all looks and feels 100% like real places. This is no coincidence, as the developers in their own words, 'took thousands of photographs'. It his however testament to their dedication to gaming, and artistic skill of reproducing photos of real places.

Right from the moment you see the loading screens the game looks crisp. The maps look crisp. One slight issue is that I saw occasional aliasing. However I got around this by upping my native resolution from 1440p, using Nvidia DSR. Running the game at 4K almost 100% eliminated aliasing. Even then though, running SE5 at native resolution was fine and the aliasing not bad. Aliasing was not everywhere - just the usual suspects like metal gridwork.

There have been tweaks to the game-play too I think. I could not tell you what they are, but game-play feels more rounded. I have heard Youtube reviewers mention game-play tweaks.

----

It took me 40 hours to play the campaign. (I searched the map over, and used a guide to get the odd collectable I missed.) Once the season passes are at a reasonable price, I will buy them:  they have two levels each. Plus I mean to get any other campaign material. 

I will for sure be replaying SE5. I am tempted to jump right in and replay, just to be back in those worlds. However I have had System Shock since pre-order, and will be playing that next.

First of all, no it's not just sniper elite 4 but more, they improved A LOT.

It can be a bit short with it's to few missions, but the ones we get are still very fun and varied, with interesting paths to take and positions to snipe from, so just for campaign this game would be worth to buy on sale.

Where it truly shines tough is the invasion mechanic. It gives you tools and is balanced in such a fun, asymetrical way, that actual irl sniper tactics really work and are worth using in PVP, like never staying in the same place to make it harder for the enemy to stop you, predicting enemy movement and laying traps, etc. 

And unlike most online games, there is no real meta here, this is primarily a battle of wits between two players, and smarter one will usually win regardless of gear. Good invader can track down and hunt the invaded and hunt them like an animal, but the good invaded can turn the whole round into a horror game for the invader. I love this game, you won't find anything quite like it anywhere else.

Also if you're just interested in it for the PVE or coop experience, the survival mode is also very entertaining, and let's you not only blindly shoot at enemies, but also set traps, find good defensive position and manage your resources, so even if pvp hunts are not your thing, you will still find enough content for yourself.

Sniper elite is the best sniper game series (or probably because I don't play many fps games). The install size is huge 93gb for deluxe version, but I think a lot of it goes to assets, mainly for graphics because the game world looks really good and there are many objects and buildings and they look different even though of course they're also reused in other places.

The most important thing is improvement from previous series, it can be a good and a bad thing because that way the latest will ofc be the best and there is no urge to get the previous installments. It's like they're competing with their own existing games and replace it with the latest. 

The one improvement I like the most is Enemy AI. In SE4 if I snipe someone, enemies will be alerted and the second shot will always reveal my position. So it kinda beats the main feature of the game as a sniper, the game has melee, pistol, submachine gun and rifle so I can use any of those to defend myself while the enemies are alerted . In SE5 enemies have better status (I think SE4 also has it but simpler). In SE5 the statuses are Clear, Investigating, Searching, Combat. If it ever reaches combat status but I manage to kill the enemies engaged fast enough, it will go back to clear status. That is the biggest improvement because then I can snipe again. Esp if I use rifle with the lowest noise range. So far I managed to stay in stealth all the time in all missions that I have played (1 and 2), while still be able to kill any enemy as I please. I still have to wait a bit to cool down depending on situation, but not too long.

The whole experience is very atmospheric, the music, the sound effect, the chatter, the graphics, this is the only game/genre that I'm comfortable walking slowly in stealth most of the time without needing to rush to go somewhere (unless I know I already clear the area). The game world is big but not too overwhelmingly big. It's the right size for each mission.

There are also rpg elements (I forgot whether it's already there since the previous series but I think it's new or already in se4), for skills. Not too important though but it helps.

As with other sniper elite series, bullet time showing slow motion kill when the bullet penetrates enemy body part never gets old. Especially when it's a difficult shot from great distance (enemy has helmet and micro movements). And loading a save file is really fast like in seconds. There is also quick save and quick load buttons, it feels like savestate in emulator games, can just load when messed up and back in action in just seconds.

Price is a bit steep as others also mentioned. So wait for a discount. It's still too expensive to buy all even at discount though, but the deluxe version should be enough for a while, and buy the rest at later discount event.

SE5 is a good game with some flaws. I was a huge fan of SE4, so naturally I'm going to be comparing the two games.

The Good:

-Options for days for configuring your guns and loadouts
-Interesting new take on survival mode, once you beat one there are different base options
-Longer and more involved single player missions than the base SE4 missions, feels more like some of the dlc missions from SE4
-Elite snipers no longer have heat seeking laser point accuracy like in SE4
-I really like that if you pick up an enemy weapon, you get what's left in the clip and then discard it.
-Tanks can no longer be shot and destroyed with a simple sniper round.

The expected:

-Allied characters are wooden cutouts with no personality just like in SE4. This time they just amped up the diversity. At least you can skip the cutscenes.
-AI can be janky: enemies can magnetic snap to cover 10ft away sometimes. Enemy soldiers stupidly exit their sidecar despite having a mounted machinegun they are leaving behind.

The Bad:

-While the gun options are cool, the progression system is completely tied to the single player missions, for a game with 3 distinct game modes, why always force players into one mode to progress?
-Despite these choices, it almost feels like there is always one correct upgrade path for each weapon.
-Base game guns are quite limited, I think there are only 5 non-dlc weapons
-Elite enemy types running with MG42s seems a bit over the top and cartoonish. Why not go back to the FG42?
-The speed at which wounded enemies instantly pull out their pistols is cartoonish as well
-When finishing up the third wave at a base, the instant spawn mechanic is kind of lame, really should've just let you run to the new base like in SE4
-DLC prices are insane. Seriously, twice the base game cost for both season passes?

I think that's everything. Overall a good game but not as good as the fourth game!

Okay, I loved SE3 and 4 and played through them several times on the hardest difficulty. They're some of my favorite games ever. This one's just weird.

1. Instead of gauging how much you have to compensate for gravity and wind, the game just outright tells you, even on authentic difficulty. This makes shooting itself trivial, and long-range kills unsatisfying.
2. Map design is simply atrocious. Lack of helpful verticality, plenty of occasions that force you out into the open, frequent risk of getting surrounded. You're constantly switching between claustrophobically tight spaces and 360-I-could-get-shot-from-any-angle-right-now open vastness, with trees blocking your (but of course not the enemies') view. Rarely, if ever, will you be able to line up in a way where enemies will funnel down a path towards you that doesn't involve getting shot in the rear.
3. Enemies are silent. Like, there's no grunts alerting you of their position. I suspect the new "focus" mechanic was supposed to balance this out, but for one, that's just in no way better than how it worked previously, and moreover, it's disabled on authentic.
4. Maps are empty as hell. It's hard to find a vantage point to actually snipe more than a handful of guys. Ironically, and I've had this happen more than once, at times you see no one from a vantage point, by virtue of all the frustrating shrubbery littering the levels, but once you engage someone nearby and screw up, there's like 10 dudes right around the corner. I had several situations where I closed in on a location where I had previously killed what I assumed was everyone at said location, only to find that there were still some oblivious npcs left roaming the area, conveniently out of sight, and apparently deaf, ready to blow your cover when you least expect it. AI is simply all over the place, too unreliable for stealth, thus ruining the entire premise of the game.

All in all, this game seems to borrow a lot of superficial game design from Hitman and Metal Gear Solid, but without any understanding of why those games work the way they do on a deeper level. I'll probably finish it, but man, this is a serious step back. This game simply doesn't satisfy me in any way. If you succeed, you don't feel accomplished, and if you fail, it doesn't feel like it was your fault, the exact opposite of why I fell in love with the series.

Edit: Finished the game and played through it once more on normal difficulty. I still stand by everything I said. If you're looking for a lackluster action game, sure, go ahead. If you want more Sniper Elite 4, this is absolutely, unequivocally not it.

Third Person Stealth games, or stealth games in general have always been some of my favourite genres in video games and by all intents and purposes, I should've really enjoyed Sniper Elite 5 but for some reason I never had that itch to keep playing it.

Sniper Elite 5 is a game where you assume the role of Karl Fairburne, an American-German Sniper on the side of the allies who helps turn the tide of the war in France 1944 through the games own inner plot set around the events of the historical D-Day.

The gameplay is what you'd expect, sneak around, line up your shots, hide bodies and collect intel. You are truly a commando in every sense of the word.

One of the best aspects of the game are the level design and missions. The maps are not massive but they're not small either, they are packed with things to do and each level feels meticulously crafted by the developers to an astonishing level. Although you have your main objective every mission there are an abundance of side missions as well as a few different difficulties, I imagine the replayability of this game is great and you could definitely get your moneys worth. 
There are 9 missions in total and each can take between 60 and 150 minutes to complete. Definitely bang for your buck.

There are multiple ways you can complete each mission, sometimes its just blowing something up, sometimes its breaking a production line, there are several ways to do things as well as multiple enemy types and loadouts that can suit your playstyle. 

If I'm being honest with myself, I genuinely don't know why I didn't enjoy this game. I was the same with SE2 and SE4. For me something just feels off and I would like to make a disclaimer that it is just the way I [i] personally [/i] feel about the game. I just never clicked with it. I felt no urge to hit launch and when I was playing it I wasn't getting any enjoyment out of it. It felt like a chore just so I could get a review out and be done with it.

I got halfway through mission 6 before I said to myself. "I'm just not enjoying this and I don't know why." I genuinely don't. The game ticks every single last box but I guess I can just say that I'm not in the mood for this game right now, that's the only thing I can think of.

I will not be giving this game a rating as I feel that it is unfair but I will be bold enough to say that I do recommend this game to people who enjoy the stealth-shooter genre.

I will come back to this game when I'm in the mood for it and see if I can complete it.

OK, right off the bat I feel like mentioning that I'm only covering the base game in this review, because most of the DLC's deserve their own review entirely, so please keep that in mind.

Sniper Elite 5 has it's flaws and drawbacks, don't get me wrong. Yes, the map design is on average subpar to that in Sniper Elite 4, with some of the levels being particularly frustrating to get through (*Cough* Level 6 *Cough*). Yes, it was odd for Rebellion to remove the trip mine and S-mine from the main game, and yet keep them inside Multiplayer. And yes, this game doesn't give you as much of an opportunity to snipe as much as the previous games, which is a little weird. But with that said, it's still a pretty good game in my mind.

1. Story
First things first, this game has much better characters, and a better story compared to anything that came before. Karl is a little bit more interesting than he was in Sniper Elite 4, and actually has pretty decent chemistry with all the main characters. Speaking of them, Charlie is a decent enough buddy for Karl, but be warned because she might have the single most aggressive Scottish accent in any character from anything ever.

Other than them, Marie is a pretty good character who ties them to the resistance and sometimes helps provide transport, although not being super interesting. And Moller is a good villain who bears a likeness to the douche bags in charge of the Nazi Regime.

For the story, Operation Kraken might just seem like another evil Nazi super weapon, and it is. But what really sets it apart from what has come before is just how insane the actual plan is. I wont spoil anything, but the whole game is worth playing through just to find out the awesome conclusion of exactly what it is.

2. Gameplay

Sniper Elite 5 might not have as good levels as Sniper Elite 4, but it does make up for it in the new things it added. For one thing, this game added Invasion mode, which is a wonderful way to play through the game if you don't feel challenged enough. The game adds plenty of new weapons like the SREM-1, Welgun, and RSC 1918. I for one think that it's an interesting idea to add non-lethal kill methods, since it's a really good way to get XP. Some of the levels are pretty well designed, such as levels #2 and #7. \

There are several different ammo types, all of which are useful for different situations. And of course, weapon customization might not be realistic to the period but it is a really cool factor. 

3. Conclusion

So, in the end Sniper Elite 5 might not be an amazing game, but I do believe that it has many strong parts. I would recommend to get it on sale, since I'm not sure that it's worth the $50 (but to be fair, I'm not sure that Sniper Elite 4 is worth $60).

8.2/10

This game is terrific. Don't be fooled by the title. While it does include various rifles and plenty of open areas for shooting, this isn't really just a sniper game. Karl is a commando, through and through. You'll be sneaking around hostile territory conducting guerrilla warfare against the Germans, sabotaging enemy equipment (coastal gun batteries, AA guns, comm equipment, etc), gathering intelligence and assassinating officers. There are a bunch of different ways to complete each mission, including both ends of the spectrum. It is a lot like Splinter Cell in that way. You can sneak around without touching anyone, you can just knock them out (why not kill those nazis?) or you can ventilate them with your blade. Naturally, you can also engage at all ranges with various firearms. If sniping isn't your thing, there are submachine guns and pistols that are perfectly viable in combat, especially now that you can aim down the sights. CQB with a Thompson is definitely a treat. 

A lot of care was put into making Karl shoot and scoot in a realistic and period accurate way, including his usage of the fighting knife melee kills and the way he reloads his weapons. 

It's a cool game, and definitely nails that espionage vibe. The Axis Invasion mode is a lot of fun, too. Definitely give this game a shot. If not here on steam, then try Gamepass. 

Also, set your AA to medium and increase the render scale instead of just maxing out the graphics. You'll thank me later.

I bought this late, but I've played through the campaign twice, once on medium and once on hard. It's pretty simple really:

- In a vacuum, sniper elite 5 is a "decent" game.
- Compared to Sniper Elite 4, it's a bad game.

Why?

- Map's are prettier but not open world. Way too many invisible walls or things you cant't jump over, each map really only offers two or maybe 3 direct paths to follow. This makes the best part of the game (Sniping from long distance) naturally harder because you can't get on that hill over there that you want to, no you have to climb this specific building they put right here. SE 4 gave you WAY more freedom and options for long distance sniping.

- Weapon upgrades are a cool idea, but don't make a big enough difference really, I always end up just going for muzzle velocity, and as quiet as possible. Even then most of the rifles are just too loud. Now this would be fine if the maps were like SE4 because you can almost always go over 100-200m away from the enemies but in SE5 you are semi guided on a path, there is FAR less room for long distance sniping. This felt more like Splinter Cell where the majority of kills were either stealth take downs or pistol shots. Why not call it Pistol Elite 1 instead.

Main Point : Sniper Elite 4 was awesome because you could CHOOSE to be a up close pistol man, or that guy that finds the furthest possible point and then sits there and takes out 1/4th of the map, then moves to another great natural spot. SE5 does not give you that same freedom. It has a tiny bit of it, but it's just way more forced and ultimately that's the complete wrong direction they should have gone in. 

I still enjoyed the game, I like the B movie campaigns they are silly. I didn't personally find this game woke, I think adding non lethal options is good. Choice is good. Unfortunately overall SE4 had more choice than SE5, and ultimately that's why you should buy that one and play that one instead.

I really hope SE6 goes back to the more open world design. It's the difference between a just okay game and a great one.

This is my introduction into the Sniper Elite series and prior to starting this one I had heard a variety of negative reviews and complaints about this one compared to previous iterations. 

Levels are massive and are able to be taken in multiple directions from multiple starting locations. If you mess up stealth in one location, usually not all is lost because of how expansive the maps are. There's a few unlocks and collectibles in each level which rewards players for curiosity and exploring. 

The game takes weapon suppression seriously and putting a silencer on doesn't make your gun totally impervious from being heard like other games. You have to take into account what type of gun you're using, how far away enemies are, are there enemies above 47 meters away? No? Then they probably heard that shot. There's a variety of different gun unlocks and choices for rifles that even differ. One of my favorite rifle is meant for close to moderate range shots and likely won't kill someone if it's a body shot, but there's other rifles that could easily shoot 300 meters.

One of the main complaints I've heard about this game are invaders. Originally, I was agreeing with some of the negative reviews. Thinking that an invader completely messes up stealth, I have to play different, but I was wrong. Yes, you do have to play differently because invaders are not AI. Invaders get the advantage of being able to walk along enemies, explore the map, but the player has traps, map awareness, and phones to call and determine an approximate location of the invader. The invaders also have far less items than the player to make it more in the player's favor. The game does not become a "battle royale" as some have said unless the player is playing like a loud buffoon. There's been quite a few times where I've even seen invaders killed from melee stealth. I've seen some reviews complaining that invasions can take upwards of 10 whole minutes as if there's an obtuse amount of time. For those who don't like invaders or any PvP there's an option to turn them off like previous Sniper Elite games. Personally, I think leaving them on is fine as long as the difficulty isn't on authentic and adds additional variety to already well designed levels and the longevity of the game. The only real issue I've had with invaders is coming across two very clear cheaters (in my almost 40 hours of playtime as of writing) which is miniscule thankfully.

As for one of the my only issues with the game, there's aren't too many missions. The additional starts, playstyles, invaders all help this, but I just wish there were more. Each mission is likely to take a player at least an hour each time or more with invasions and co op which helps. There's also other game modes for survival which add a more action-loud game mode for those who aren't great at stealth, which is also fun.

Co op is great and there's a lot of hilarious situations both you and your friends can get into. For kill cams, the game will stop both players to see one whoever got the kill shot. The kill cam is gruesome, hilarious, and seeing Nazis lose their eyes, teeth, and testicles in different situations is satisfying.

It's a fun as hell stealth game with satisfying kill cams and works great either single player or co op. It's worth the buy.

Finished my first playthrough (Normal) and wanted to share my first impressions. 

I enjoyed the game and would recommend it if you enjoyed previous Sniper Elite and Zombie Army games. Dropped down to Normal on my first playthrough because for some reason I couldn't shoot straight at first. Only played the campaign, haven't played any Season Pass content yet. 

The main campaign was shorter than I expected but the missions and side objectives were what you'd expect from a Sniper Elite game. AA guns, lots of them. Nazis too.

Sniper Elite 5 reintroduces armour piercing ammo which makes dealing with armoured vehicles a lot quicker. There's also non-lethal, subsonic and match grade ammo. Can't say much about the new ammo types as I haven't really used them enough. Takedowns now offer a lethal or non-lethal option. 

Each map has 3 different starting locations, the default locations and two other locations that you have to find and unlock. A nice feature that allows you to mix things up a bit.

Rocks are replaced with empty bottles. No longer an infinite supply but you can find empty bottles all over the map. Throwing a bottle at an enemy's head will knock them unconscious which is handy and neat.

Truck engines can now also be used for sound cover, just like generators. Alarms are also new-ish. Once the alarm is triggered, sirens will call for reinforcements. Alarms can be disabled and booby trapped as well, so that's fun.

Zip lines to travel across larger distances relatively fast. I suppose they're handy but I'm not sure if they really add anything. 

A crowbar and bolt cutters are new tools. They can be used to open doors and supply crates, some can be opened by picking the lock or brute force, others only by brute force. You can also use them to cut holes in fences or sabotage mission objectives. 

The Kill List is a nice addition. Every mission has an optional objective to kill the target in a specific way. Some are easy, others are a bit trickier but they were fun to do and I'm sure I'll have fun with them in the next few playthroughs. 

I do have some issues with the game, though. Nothing that made me regret buying this game but I still want to mention them.

First of all, it is set in France. Not one French person to be shot, though. Not even civilians. In Italy we got to shoot Italians on both sides but in France the best we get are NPCs slipping in and out of their stupid French accents. Very disappointing.

The graphics are really nice, the fabric of Karl's sweater looks pretty realistic but at the same time the player models look a bit more plasticky. The facial animations are more detailed but look off, especially in the cut scenes. Corpses often have wide open, contorted mouths [strike] and for some reason a lot of them also end up sticking their asses in the air as if to say "Fick mich hart, Karl, du heißer Scharfschütze" [/strike] which is more comical than anything else.

I always found the Zombie Army games to a bit a jankier than the Sniper Elite games when it comes to the controls in general. Weapon handling was the most noticeable difference to me and  Sniper Elite 5 feels more in line with Zombie Army 4 than Sniper Elite 4.

Gun handling feels different, more Zombie Army than Sniper Elite but I can't quite explain what that means. The balancing of weapons and other decisions don't make sense to me. They added the Drilling shotgun but it doesn't have a rifle barrel, which is the defining feature of the Drilling. Also, Mosin, poor thing. 

Maps are big just like in SE4 but feel emptier, first few maps have a lot of open fields and hedges. Villages and military structures are smaller. Feels a bit more open world compared to SE4, if that makes sense. Maybe it's the difference in design, I think SE4 had better level design with elevation differences and pathing. Traversing the terrain in 5 is a lot jankier. Lots of invisible walls, hills you can't climb, obstacles you can't mount or vault.

Getting interaction prompts to appear can be a pain. Especially picking up items from safes was quite iffy. I point directly at the documents but no prompt, have to do a little dance to get the prompt and then I still have to pick up the TNT or ammo or whatever before the documents even register. Don't know why that is but it is annoying. 

Enemies are spread thin,  I first thought that was due to Normal difficulty but apparently it's no different on higher difficulties. Will find out for myself soon enough.

Not a big fan of locating work benches to unlock weapon upgrades. I suppose it's nice to change or upgrade your rifle on the go but adding three, one for pistol, SMG and rifle each is a bit much. I very much would have prefered individual weapon challenges like in SE4 to upgrade instead of unlocking them across the board.

And last, but not least, there sadly is no Overwatch mode. I'm sure Invasion can be fun but Overwatch was really good in SE4. A huge improvement on SE3 and I would've loved some DLC missions for Overwatch. 
I prefer co-op, don't really touch multiplayer so the removal of co-op Overwatch means a game with less content.

Or sneak through long grass whilst the infantry yak in German either about their personal lives or even better about what the bosses are up to. Maps are well drawn with objectives clearly marked. Tutorial hints are really useful when you're learning the mechanics and you can turn them off in options when you've got the hang of them.
   All in all, a very satisfying experience.

Yes, I know, it is long time, but I like to explore everything and find what is there to find.
So what's new since Sniper Elite 4?

Workbenches in every map (3 per map), where you can unlock/modify your weapons while in mission.

Various weapons (usually slightly better in first missions) lying around to pick up and use while they has ammo. That is modified general weapons you can unlock by progressing thtough the game - silenced versions, stronger versions or with larger magazines etc. Plus there are weapons falling from every dead enemy, you can pick these weapons and use while they has ammo, or simply take ammo from them (need to unlock certain skill for that).

"Parkour". Yes, some climbing elements from Tomb Raider - ledges, ladders, vines, sliding down the slopes, ziplines. Interesting, useful.

I'm not sure if it is new since 4th game, but there are crowbars and bolt cutters in every map as well as locked doors, crates, walled with planks holes that needs these tools to open new paths.

Also the game still has safes with secret materials or secondary objectives. Safes can be opened with found keys or explosives.

As 4th game it has beautiful graphics and sound, retain hiding in tall grass, sound mask options where player can create them by himself where applicable or use those in the world (fight sounds, plane sounds etc)

One little personal disappointment I have to notice. Even with most difficult custom setting set to lowest amount of ammo found/dropped, there are still plenty of ammo to use. One minor bug I found where killed vehicles retained working engine sounds. And that is it from negative things.

In summary, if you liked 4th game, you'll also like the 5th one. Plus there are additional DLC missions, weapons and skins to unlock.

Oh, and now you can slow down or fast forward the flying bullet scene, I think it is also new feature.

So yeah, thanks for reading.

Compared to Sniper Elite 4, this game doesn't play well at all. I don't know what happened, but this feels like a downgrade to the franchise. It's hard to explain, but there were a lot of little things about the game that killed my experience playing it. Player movement was janky at times, and often wouldn't allow you to perform the action you wanted. Stealth could be ruined because of a glitched texture or object you thought you were safely hidden behind. And sometimes the enemies would just.. break ...and not move anymore, especially when you raised suspicion. 

These sorts of things were very smooth and well executed in SE4 but for some reason it's terrible in this game and it really killed my enjoyment of it. Things felt less intuitive and more forced and there were times where I thought I could get creative in my approach, but the game basically said I couldn't for no real reason. 

On top of that there were new mechanics implemented that felt unnecessary. Gun customizations instead of simple upgrades, non-lethal options for bullets and explosives that do nothing for overall gameplay or story, and character upgrades that didn't really change much in how you performed, and were too easy to level up.

The story was also all over the place. Without giving away too much, the game starts with you stuck behind enemy lines for the longest time, all by yourself aside from a few french revolutionists. And all of a sudden, after 3 or 4 of the levels going like that, you're then back with the allies invading Normandy?? There was no real flow to it after that because it felt like we skipped 3 or 4 chapters in a book. In the past, Sniper Elite games have had stories but it never really focused on them aside from providing backstory to the mission you were doing  and setting up the big bosses and their evil scheme that was supposed to turn the tide of war for Germany. It never needed to go further than that, but for some reason it's starting to and it's almost to Sniper Elite's detriment.

Overall while I really wanted to like this game, it just has too many issues for it to be worthwhile. It really felt like I was forcing myself to finish the game towards the end because I was fed up with it. If you've read this far, GO PLAY SNIPER ELITE 4!! I promise you that game is much more polished and very satisfying to play. I hope that future installments of Sniper Elite really try and smooth over these issues. Very disappointed to say "no" in my recommendation of this game.

Neither of the two things that made SE4 stand out to me are present in this game. Sniper Elite 5 has been released for many months now, and in my own opinion, it's one of the best games of the franchise.  However, it does have its flaws.  Despite being released as a sniping game, it is fairly easy to complete each mission with an assault style playthrough, utilizing unscoped rifles and the various secondary weapons.  If its a more realistic take you desire, a pure stealth sniping route could easily land you 60+ hours of gameplay, and it is worth just about every hour.  Observing patrol routes, calculating the trajectories, pacifying or killing lone sentries, every action demands your utmost attention and ability to plan out the next move.  For example, it takes me about 6 to 7 hours of gameplay just to complete each mission undetected.  The option for just simple run-and-gun DOOM style fighting can also work if that's more your speed.

Moving on from basic gameplay, the visuals are stunning, the levels are large and feature various zones to either blitz or sneak through, and the ability to pick up weapons from fallen enemies and supply crates is a plus, in my mind.  Each level has a hidden cache with at least one MG42 and a belt of 100 rounds to neutralize large groups of soldiers, while Panzerfausts and Panzerbusche anti-tank rifles can deliver stand-off attacks on armored vehicles and troop transports.  Every encounter can be dealt with in a variety of ways, and while that's not a new feature in the series, it's the best implementation of it so far.

The AI can be rather smart at times, but is still rather easy to fool.  Soldiers will take cover when shot at, and if you're using a suppressor on your rifle, this can lead to them actually retreating and falling farther and farther back, but this only works if you are outside of their detection range, which is another very well-implemented gameplay mechanic.  I've played way too many games that feature the Hollywood-esque suppressor where your weapon is silent at all ranges.  The suppressors in this game though work exactly as they should, and while they significantly reduce the range at which your shots can be heard, they don't completely remove them either.

The various types of ammunition you can unlock during the game is another great feature, although the less said about the nonlethal rounds, the better.  Subsonic ammunition though is a game changer, and combine that with a customised Welrod, and you can complete missions with just that sidearm.  And speaking of unlocks, it just feels reminiscent of Call of Duty and Battlefield, where you have to meet the prerequisites to obtain them, from attachments to weapons and gear.  I did enjoy having to find the workbenches to mount the new attachments or utilize the new kit, but it does get a bit ridiculous.  Have you seen a Tarkov-inspired Luger?  Some of the attachments just don't work like that at all.

Moving on to weapons, the selection was pretty decent, but I wish there was more!  The SREM-1 is a nifty little rifle that I actually did not know anything about.  I'd never even heard of it, and thought Rebellion was pulling my leg, until I watched Saint Jonathon at the Royal Armouries actually talk about it and show off the only surviving example.  Speaking of which, Rebellion, would you please complete it's model, it's missing a scope ring, and the point where that can be attached is easily seen on the handguard.  Moving on from that, for a game based in France, there's not a lot of French weapons available.  I was expecting to see a Lebel or a Berthier, maybe even a MAS-36, but maybe that's for a later DLC package, I'm not sure.  I wasn't expecting to see Japanese weapons and equipment, so that was a little weird despite being central to the campaign.

And that leads to a new issue, the campaign is basically the same: the Nazis have a new superweapon, you have to follow all the leads to find said superweapon, then you blow it up and kill the man in charge.  That was V2 with a V2 rocket loaded with Tabun gas, that was 3 with the P.1000 Ratte superheavy tank, that was 4 with an upgraded radio-guided rocket, and now we have stealth-plated submarines with V2 rockets.  The formula is getting tired at this point.  Same for the Hitler assassination missions.  Don't get me wrong, there is nothing wrong with killing Hitler.  It's just, when are we going to be able to target other senior Nazi officials?  I've shot Hitler's testicle off in four separate games now.  I no longer have that juvenile chuckle.

And now we get to the major issue I've been having.  Sniper Elite 5 is still acting like its out of Alpha and into Beta.  I'm having game-crashing bugs practically every level, more often 2 to 3 times per level.  I don't know if that's because the code is still a little iffy or if it's because my hard drive isn't capable of running it, all I do know is that this issue still needs worked on.  If you've read this far, good for you, make sure your PC is up to the minimum requirements, but I highly recommend going as far beyond that as you financially can.  Maybe it's just me, but I don't have the money to throw at it right now.  I will say that it is very frustrating having to restart my PC multiple times just to finish a single mission.

Well, that's all I've got.  Make sure you get your free DLC downloads when they come out, because hey, they're free even if they don't do much of anything gameplay wise.  I can't say much for the rest of the DLC, I don't have them yet.  Sniper Elite 5 is another solid addition to the franchise, but what's next?  We've gone to Berlin, to North Africa, to Italy, and now France.  There's only so much more Karl Fairburne can do before V2 begins, so will we see him again in the Netherlands as part of Market Garden, or maybe in Belgium for the Battle of the Bulge?  All I know is, his story is almost done, if not done already.  That's up to Rebellion, but I think they might still have one more installment before calling it quits.

This is a good game to play if you've got time to kill, and if you can handle the game-ending bugs and hope they get patched, then this game could be a good entry into your library.  If you want to snipe, look no further.  If you want to run-and-gun, you can do that here.  If you want to be the SOE-equivalent of James Bond, that's here too.  If you have the previous entries, then you know Karl's story so far, but now you have to help him liberate France. If you've enjoyed the Sniper Elite games this is certainly a step forward. The levels are a little bigger and mostly better, with a couple of exceptions. The system of "how far a shot can be heard" is more complex now and there are new techniques and tactics you can use. Graphics are excellent.

--- PROS:

+ Great gear customizability. Plenty of different types of muzzles, suppresors, scopes, receivers, etc. You can tailor your guns to your personal playstyle. For each weapon configuration you're given the exact distance at which the shot will be inaudible (suppressors only make it a little quieter, even on lower difficulties). Suppressors can now be used independently of ammo type, allowing for many different levels of gunshot audibility (most quiet of course being suppressor plus subsonic ammo).

+ Increased ammo variety. Vehicles are now immune to regular ammo, even at weak points. Only armor-piercing bullets can hurt them. Subsonic ammo is quieter but has greater bullet drop. Match ammo has reduced bullet drop but is louder. Soft-point ammo deals more damage to human targets but can't penetrate armor or helmets. Additionally there's non-lethal ammo - quieter and doesn't kill (in case you suddenly feel sorry for those poor low-ranking nazis).

+ Music - somewhat better and more noticable than in SE4, at least in my opinion.

+ NPC dialogue. In SE4 nazis sounded like cartoonish villains. Now they sound more like human beings.

--- PROS/CONS (depending on personal preferences):

+/- In addition to the wind indicator in scoped view which allows for horizontal adjustments, there's now also a similar indicator for gravity. This makes sniping less reliant on luck, but also probably a bit easier. Some people will like it, some won't.

+/- When aiming at an enemy with any weapon, there's now an icon above his head if he's within audible range of your gunshot. Same as with sniping, this makes stealth less reliant on luck, but also easier. Again, a matter of taste.

+/- No more "authentic plus" difficulty. "Authentic" is now the highest. Hardcore fans and realism nuts will probably be dissapointed.

--- CONS:

- Map design could be slightly better, with more vantage points and sniping opportunities (except "Spy Academy" - this one is a masterpiece).

- Fairburne is now wearing some lousy sweater, which makes him look significantly less badass.

+VE: gorgeous graphics.  immersive sound.  manual save and load - very few games have this.  
-VE: faulty bots that do silly things, initially tricky to deal with but weaknesses become obvious.

So I just wrapped up the base game with the goal of killing every soldier in every level. Took about 47 hours and lots of patience. Out of SE3, SE4, and SE5, this was my favorite, and I thoroughly enjoyed the other games. 

I took a firm stealth approach to the entire game, which worked out very well. If you like that sort of playstyle, you will enjoy this. If analyzing troop movements and finding short strike windows is your thing, this game has it in spades. 

What I liked...

- The weapon customization is detailed enough to be fun, although a few of the items are a little silly. I'm looking at you, weirdly-crossed grip tape.

- The visuals are fantastic.

- Soldier bios - This was a nice touch. It allows you to get to know your quarry before you put a bullet through its skull. Not sure why they added this feature, but it was kind of funny.

- The suppressed rifle sounds actually sound fairly realistic. As someone who spends a good deal of time on the range and spent seven years in the Army, it's nice to hear a game get this right.

What I didn't like...

- I'm not a fan of "weapon/item unlock" mechanics in games. I'm not even sure why developers put these in games any more. It would be great if you started with the ability to build your loadout however you wanted. The pros and cons of each weapon/item should be enough on their own to prevent any particular loadout from being overpowered.

- I'm not a fan of the way the player icon displays on the map. I know, it's a small thing, but when you are trying to orient yourself on maps this size, the direction of the character icon should reflect the way the camera is facing instead of the character's body. This is a minor annoyance when you are in cover, which is a lot of the time. 

- Constant kill cams get old. Look, I loved this game. Thought it was great, but if I smoke 150+ dudes on one map, I have to watch 150 kill cams. Each one runs about seven seconds. That's 17+ minutes of kill cams. Bruh, that's a bit much. I know you can turn them off completely, but what about a happy medium or some way to modify the kill cam frequency? This is just one bald dude's opinion.

Overall, this was a great game. Definitely took top spot for me for the SE series of games. I'll be buying the DLC so I can go smoke the dude with the bad haircut and the toothbrush mustache next. Have fun dropping bodies. I certainly did.

[u][b]TL;DR[/b][/u]
I can't recommend a game that claims to be Sniper Elite but feels more like Hitman in WWII,and fails to execute either properly. This experience taught me the value of not preordering.

First of all, it's not a bad game and looks very good. However, I've played all the earlier Sniper Elite games and most of the Hitman franchise (which is more relevant than it might seem), and I find this one to be the least enjoyable among modern games.

[u]What I like:[/u]
In this installment, compared to the previous ones, I particularly like the [b]weapon customization[/b]. It allows you to dramatically alter how a weapon performs in some cases, and enables specialization of weapons for certain tasks or playstyles. Additionally, I also like the [b]graphics.[/b] While not necessarily better, the grittier atmosphere it creates suits the game quite well in my opinion.

[u]What I don't like:[/u]
Let's address the big issue first: [b]map design and the Hitman-like feel[/b]. The maps are expansive but, unlike Hitman, all paths feel constrained (sometimes oddly so). For three-quarters of the game, you're so close to the enemy that an SMG or a knife is more useful than a scoped rifle. The game introduces new options for killing like poisoning, and to top it off, it features the same hitman-o-vision from the Hitman series. The only difference is that it feels even more out of place here. All of this contributes to the game feeling more like a poorly executed Hitman set in WW2 rather than a proper Sniper Elite game.

[b]Grinding[/b]: If you want everything, be prepared to do a lot of grinding. If you want to do it in multiplayer, you'll have to do it all over again against other players who most likely already have the upgrades.

Speaking of [b]multiplayer[/b], the old-style multiplayer has been replaced with gameplay similar to CoD and Battlefield, but with everyone equipped with sniper rifles. I find that this style challenges less thinking and sniping, and leans more toward reflexes and bunny hopping.

[b]Multiple DLC seasons[/b]. call me old fashioned but i think this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, certainly at €30 for 2 maps, 2 guns, and some skins.

P.S. The best anti-tank weapon is an SMG with AP bullets.

What made me to feel good in this, is that Sniper Elite finally came to France, 1944. That is what I like about it. That is a proof you can make WW2 game still with very modern and solid gameplay, that won't be totally generic.
Surprisingly D-Day doesn't felt like before in this title.  It used to have in call of duty series but, here, SE 5 is one and only a non-multiplayer game like (Post-Scriptum, HLL) that allows you to explore open maps based on Normandy locations. Still having their own and new flavour.
And some maps are enough big to let you enjoy the Normandy from open perspective. What is enjoying too, the number of WW2 guns and their customization is beyond satisfying, and it isnt over-looked nor overdone. If you're a WW2 enthusiasts you can love this series, I'm glad the Normandy came to this series with fresh look. Possibly next game will head towards the Pacific as some hints can be found in the game or into the Ardennes, Belgium, but we will see...

[u] What game offers? [/u]

- large maps and long missions 
- good and fresh looking Normandy and D-Day setting
- replayability e.g. exploring map=unlocking new start locations ,or unlocking new objectives
- use of different paths and fight methods
- good gun customization
- plenty of weapons and attachments to use (smgs, assault rifles, sniper rifles)
- invasion mode in campaign - the enemy player, playing as Wehrmacht's sniper tries to eliminate and stop you, or you can play to stop someone's missions
- multiplayer - with no run'gun cod like, just sniping , no crossing to run, very nice like in Ghost Warrior Games.

[u] What it doesn't offer? [/u]

- not all maps are that super big, half of them is in standard size
- only a couple missions where u play with other squad members or protect squads 
- still lone wolf game, doesn't involve you in that 'large' battle feeling

[u] Issues? [/u]

Game is very well optimized. As the minimum requirements are presented, you can still have 3gb or even less of VRAM, to enjoy the game. Tested on Gtx 750 ti, gtx 760 and finally on 1050ti. Graphics are really nice. Sometimes but much rarely, u can spot dead bodies to glitch in textures and not properly collide with some terrain objects. Not too often.
Sniper Elite 5 is really great game from the series. Though I spent good hours in this game, I feel it should have more missions as there are 8 (basic edition)- however pretty long to complete them 100%.

[u] Any improvements? [/u] 

- new possibilities of enemies AI, they aren't that stupid like before in SE Afrika (what I have heard before) or  you have to respect enemies in open engagement even on easy difficulty and plan your tactic.
- new movement and shot animations, 
- new audio effects: gun shots are extremely good, it's well made that silenced rifles are still loud, which is correct in real life.
- longer missions and more items to use, as well plenty explore and to find in loot.

[u] Conclusion: [/u]

Though I spent good hours in this game, I feel it should have more missions as there are 8- however very long to complete, and each location looks completely different. Apparently SE5 is the best from the series, still it is being updated with new content. The best game to grab from the series. If they make next part in the Pacific Theater it would be total epicness.

The exceptions are the second map, Occupied Residence, and the third map, Spy Academy, which were interesting and had a fun mix of gameplay styles, Spy Academy in particular. 

A tip is to do a bit of scouting before entering areas and immediately starting to stealth kill enemies. A lot of the time you'll kill everyone and miss a good sniping spot where you could have nested yourself and taken them on from there, creating a sound mask by sabotaging a nearby generator. 

Another tip is to put FSR onto Ultra (if you can) and turn off anti-aliasing. The game is quite jaggy and has quite a bit of shimmering, particularly in the foliage, and FSR smooths it out while looking a lot like your native res. Turning anti-aliasing off makes the image sharper while in FSR Ultra mode, so in the end you end up getting a free 10-20fps while making the game look better (I play in 1080p by the way). Play the game on high settings instead of Ultra as well. 

To conclude, the maps are interesting, unique, large, and are lengthy to complete; the gameplay loop is fun; and a bunch of other things they added like weapon customisation and achievements etc. Have fun sniping!

I've played the earlier iterations through, and I've played SE5 through. This latest iteration (SE5) introduces some maddening gotchas that make it feel badly-designed and poorly-conceived compared to the earlier iterations. Especially as a AAA game at around $50 USD, it's a rip-off. I got it on a half-price sale and still don't feel like it was worth the cost. If you can pick it up for under $20, you might get your money's worth, but maybe not. It depends upon your willingness to endure the badness. Personally, I find the wonky glitches to be problematical enough that I cannot recommend it.

MANY of the other negative reviews mention my same points, so I would urge you to take the negative reviews seriously! But I'll reiterate just some of the problems for special emphasis.

* Rebellion totally broke body-looting compared to previous iterations! WHY? WHY redesign a system that worked just fine before. In SE5 you have to be perfectly lined-up with a body and looking "down" at it to even get the option to "Search." That's maddening enough, because it's often ridiculously time-consuming to try to get lined up just right to be able to "Search." But....

* MUCH worse is that even when you are lined up just right, you hold "E" to "Search," and instead the dumb interface immediately grabs the nearest weapon (that might even be behind you!) that the body dropped onto the ground! I don't WANT that weapon! I did everything possible to NOT pick it up! But, noooo. This dumb game is just determined that if I hit "E" (even as a "hold" of the key) I MUST want that weapon. It's flat-out ridiculous, and by the time you finish the game, you'll be raging at the number of times you are FORCED to pick up and then drop a weapon you did NOT want to pick up. So, in summary, the looting system is ABSURDLY broken!

* The armored vehicles are stupid-hard to deal with. In previous iterations, you could take them out with Teller mine and/or TNT, which is legit! The 40s-era armor couldn't withstand a Teller/TNT combo, but in SE5 NO amount of explosives can one-shot an armored vehicle. Instead, you must deal explosives damage and then position yourself behind the vehicle and start pumping armor-piercing rounds into the exposed (after the initial explosives) "weak spots" until the thing blows up. It's just time-consuming, inaccurate artificial difficulty. Complete waste of time/effort that does the opposite of adding to the "realism" of the game.

* This is NOT a "sniper" game, like previous iterations were. You are often forced by terrain, buildings, etc. into close-quarters combat. I've actually killed more MOBs with my Welrod than with my sniper rifle.

* A big part of the above (virtually forced) play style is that SE5 utterly nerfed your capacity to CHOOSE to take a silenced shot versus a loud shot. There is NO subsonic ammo for the rifle, as in ALL other iterations of this franchise! You have to choose a silenced WEAPON, but even then the sonic reduction is at most about 30%, which doesn't really affect your strategic decisions. Again, WHY? Sniper Elite 5 – Silent, Surgical, and Best Played With a Partner
I came into Sniper Elite 5 already loving the co‑op from Sniper Elite 4, and I was hoping for something similar. I didn’t get disappointed. This game delivers exactly what I want from a tactical co‑op experience: slow, silent, disciplined infiltration where communication isn’t optional — it’s survival.

This is not a game where you magically drift into perfect positions without speaking. You talk. Constantly. You plan every movement, every angle, every shot. And when it works, when you and your partner move like two ghosts through enemy territory, it feels incredible. That shared responsibility — knowing the mission only succeeds if both of you stay focused — is what makes Sniper Elite 5 so satisfying.

I always go for the surgical, silent approach. Not because it’s easier, but because it’s harder. It forces you to be patient, precise, and fully committed to the plan. When you finish a mission without alarms, without chaos, without improvisation, you get that deep tactical satisfaction that says: yes, this is exactly how it should be done.

As for the public multiplayer… I never really got into it. It’s fine, but it’s not why I play Sniper Elite. For me, this game shines brightest in co‑op — two players, one mission, one plan, and the quiet thrill of pulling it off perfectly.

If you enjoy teamwork, communication, and the challenge of doing things the hard, silent, disciplined way, Sniper Elite 5 is absolutely worth your time.

If you've played any of the previous Sniper Elite games, you already know what you're in for. You play Karl Fairburne, lone wolf American sniper and infiltrator marching through 1944 France and single handedly investigating and ultimately sabotaging a new Nazi weapon system over the course of 9 chapters (well, 8 chapters and some change). 

As with Sniper Elite 4 the maps continue to be amazing. The third chapter in particular (Spy Academy) takes place at a fictional Beaumont-Saint-Denis which is loosely based on the real life Mont-Saint-Michel in northern France. It's perhaps the most amazing FPS map I've experienced. After I thoroughly cleared the place of Nazis I seriously pondered setting up a virtual coffee shop in one of the courtyards. Unfortunately after that map (and one that proceeded it, Occupied Residence) the remaining maps felt just kinda... meh (Until the final map which was pretty good but involves a lot more close combat than, you know, sniping). 

The AI is... fine. Ish. I played on the middle setting and while it was a challenge, there were choke points on some maps where the AI soldiers just didn't behave logically. On one map in particular there was a small bridge that soldiers just kept crossing even after watching their comrades getting picked off by Fairburne. It made for an easy culling of the herd, but it felt a little bit like cheating.

All in all though it's a very fun game. The maps are sprawling and challenging and I appreciate that they put a LOT of work into a long and varied single player campaign. Looking forward to Sniper Elite 6!

Rebellion has obviously put a lot of work into updating this game from SE4. There are two innovations here. The first is much improved AI behaviour. I bumped into an SS officer running up the stairwell in the hotel on the first level and tried to melee kill him. He fought back, blocking 4 or 5 of my attempts and we both struggled to grab out sidearms. He was faster than I was and I went down. Very nice and a huge surprise. It is nearly impossible to fire a weapon completely unnoticed. The AI's will systematically hunt you down, working together to surround you and flush you out. They will sneak up behind you all the time. Watch your 6.

The other innovation in SE5 is non-lethal mode. There is non-lethal ammo and a non-lethal melee takedown. You get extra points for this, and it's generally quieter than a kill melee, so you can do this standing right next to another AI without alerting them.

So far I've played the first level through with all the defaults, and then in Authentic Mode which I find far more enjoyable. I use an xbox 360 controller.

Speaking of the controller, I find some of the selection mechanics really difficult and clunky. Rebellion needs to work on this. Picking stuff up, searching bodies, and even choosing things from the inventory wheel is just way too hard. Maybe it's easier with the keyboard/mouse. Dunno. Needs fixing.

I've been a big fan of this series since Sniper Elite V2 was released, with Sniper Elite 4 being my favorite by far. So, most of this review will be written as a comparison to Sniper Elite 4. I haven't played any multiplayer yet (including the invasion mode of the single player campaign), so this is going to mainly be about the campaign.

For starters, the graphics are better than SE4...hands down. The maps/map design was maybe on par with SE4--the maps/levels seemed to be a little bigger, but ultimately they were roughly the same as far as size and potential routes/paths go. The ability to traverse the maps--whether through climbing vines or using ziplines--seemed more in-depth and varied (and using ziplines is fun too).

The "Kill List" objectives to unlock weapons was entertaining at least, but they weren't very hard to do. And while the weapon customization is nice (and the task of finding the workbenches adds a nice little side challenge to each mission), I feel as though recoil control, aim stability and suppressor upgrades are the only worthwhile rifle upgrades. Here's why:

The longest shot I was able to make in the campaign was around 475m in the Spy Academy mission if I remember correctly, and that involved a lot of positioning myself to make that long distance possible. Outside of that shot and a couple others in "Rubble and Ruin," the average shot distance in a campaign mission I was able to pull off--just by roughly guesstimating--is somewhere between 100m and 200m. That was a bit of a disappointment to me, as in the *very first* mission of SE4, you are able to make about 12-14 shots (maybe more) that are between 200m and 400m without going very far from the starting position. So, unless there are "hidden" or "secret" long shots (kinda like in SE3)...muzzle velocity, scope zoom level, and match grade ammo is all but useless unless you just hate compensating for wind and gravity.

The "sped up" weapon reloads seem more like a multiplayer gimmick to me, as does the "focus" ability that basically gives you free wall hacks for a certain period of time. I also miss the items/inventory wheel of SE4 where you had nothing but lethal traps/explosives, health items and unlimited rocks/a whistle. You could really make some mayhem in those days. In SE5, your only lethal options are a landmine, grenade, or TNT (and I only really used time-delayed TNT to destroy vehicles when I couldn't get close enough to use a satchel charge or I couldn't find a Panzerfaust), you have a limited supply of bottles--which took the place of rocks, which were unlimited--and the non-lethal Schu Mines...well....I didn't use them once, since the only time you need to knock somebody unconscious is for the Kill List challenge where you have to kill the one officer by burying him in concrete, and you can KO somebody by using your knife/melee takedown. The decoys weren't really useful either, since if you take the right skills, people will get tagged if they shoot at you...which means you don't need to throw out a decoy to get their position.

The skill upgrades were nice, but most of them were either useless, or weren't necessary/very helpful. Like, yeah...it's nice to be able to have enemies get temporarily tagged when they shoot at me, but isn't that what the decoy is for? You can get by without using traps for the entire campaign (ask me how I know) so you really don't need an increased supply of those or be able to throw them down faster, yeah the "focus" skill is nice...but that's basically free wall hacks for a certain period of time. The only ones worth it to me would be the ones that give you slots for special ammo, and the ones that reduce how fast your heart rate rises. And even to that point, the only special ammo that is worth your time would be the AP ammo so you can one-shot enemies through their helmet with your Pistol & SMG, or destroy vehicles in fewer shots.

When it came to the enemies and how hard they were to conquer...I was again disappointed. I found them more annoying than challenging (I was playing on Sniper Elite difficulty, the one where you have to compensate for both distance and wind), and I was able to go through the whole campaign without dying at the hands of the enemy (I can honestly say that the only times I died was because I stood too close to a satchel charge, or because I took hella fall damage from trying to parkour my way through the level). The engineers were cool in that they could undo/fix your sabotaged generator or truck to take away your soundmasking, and the snipers caused you to be extra careful unless you wanted a "bleeding" wound that forced you to use one of your precious med items...but everyone else was just kinda...a nuisance rather than a credible threat. The enemy variety is roughly the same as SE4: radio operators and spotters were replaced by gunners and engineers. Most everyone else you already know and love, with a few variants sprinkled in (like Vampir Jagers or Elite Snipers).

Even the vehicles weren't hard to deal with. If you can't satchel charge them, if there isn't a Panzerfaust nearby, or you can't use a landmine to stop them, just lob some TNT on a timer near them and call it good--it might take two or three TNTs, but it'll work. Run out of TNT before that King Tiger went boom? Just load some AP ammo in your weapon of choice (whether it be the Welrod, MP40 or something else) and just keep shooting the glowing red area.

Satchel charges are either useless or the only key you'll ever need, depending on whether you want to go full stealth or guns blazing. If you take the time and have the patience to take out everyone on the map or hunt down officers...you probably won't need satchel charges unless an objective specifically calls for you to use a satchel charge. Or alternatively, you can just blast your way through doors, safes and walls since you can usually find more than enough to get you through the mission.

The ending was really anti-climactic as well. "That is quite some distance Mr. Fairburne..." *Binoculars say the distance is 230m to the target* "Hurry! Before he gets away!" *Target stops on a balcony, then leisurely strolls to his car before slowly driving away* Sniper Elite V2's final shot was harder than the final shot in this one.

TL;DR While I'm not too disappointed with SE5, I was honestly expecting more. The enemies aren't really a challenge, most traps are useless, and almost half the weapon upgrades seem useless unless you really just want to have a laser beam of a gun that laughs in the face of wind and gravity. There isn't really a lot of opportunity for taking long distance shots (200m or further), unless you really look for them or are willing to do the necessary legwork to set up a long shot. And even if you take your time and go through each mission slowly...the campaign still seems really short. Blasting people with the anti-tank rifle was really fun though, I would recommend using the anti-tank rifle on infantry and nothing else.

All things considered, SE5 isn't a bad game...but I believe that SE4 is better.

I first played Sniper Elite 4 and enjoyed it so much that I ended up getting V2, 3 and now 5 soon after.  These games remind me of what I liked so much about the older Call of Duty and Medal of Honor games back when they were single-player only.  They focus on a vibrant single player story, fun game play and polished level design instead of just large bland arenas designed for endless PvP.  The name says "Sniper Elite" but the game allows you to play however you want.  Want to snipe from hundreds of meters away and play "pop goes the Nazi"?  Great!  Want to set up an explosive booby trap for nosy patrolling enemy?  No problem!  Want to charge into a bunker and clean it out with an SMG?  Go for it!  The missions drop you in a large open-world-ish map (each mission gets it's own specific map) with a couple known objectives along with some extra objectives that can be found while playing.  Apart from that, you are free to chose how you complete them and in what order.  The maps are also beautifully designed (aside from occasional invisible wall) and suit the story and missions well.  The over all result feels like a classic WWII action movie.

I also enjoy that the series knows what it wants to be and keeps polishing the concept and expanding it.  The games are not very realistic (taking out a tank with a few well-placed rifle rounds??  lol!)  but much more importantly they are FUN to play.  The enemy AI is not brilliant but they will take cover, attempt to flank your position and raise alarms to call in their nearby allies.  There are lots of collectibles to find and things to unlock which gives it more replay value than most single player game IMHO.  

My one minor criticism is that it is often easy to chose a defensible location, setup a few booby traps and make a grand racket to piss off half the enemies on the map and then wipe them out as the try to storm your location, leaving you to explore the map unbothered afterwards.  I played on  "Sharpshooter" (medium?) difficulty though, so this might be less true on higher difficulty settings?  Also, the enemy models in kill-cams sometimes seem to lock solid in their death animations which looks a bit awkward?  A more random rag-doll animation might be better.

Sniper Elite 5 is the most polished yet but V2, 3 and 4 are also excellent and worth playing as well.  I got the versions with DLC included and enjoyed the DLC missions as well.  These games usually have great deals on Steams sales too.
