And it's not just that the maps are large, they are incredibly detailed - every problem has multiple solutions, every destination has multiple paths and there are multiple objectives to choose from. You can see Rebellion play around with different ideas too, like one map that takes place on an island and it looks like a normal-sized SE4 map but as you snoop around, you find that there is this sprawling underground facility with more tunnels than an ant farm. It was really cool, like being in some sort of 70s espionage film. Oh and there's also a colossal nazi castle. IMO this is by far the best level in any of the Sniper Elite games. There's so much you can do - from the starting area, you can snipe dozens of enemies, then you can wind through the streets, sneaking and knifing guards as you please, taking out elite soldiers in the sprawling beach in the back. You eventually make your way to the very top and spy on the three krauts planning the operation, assassinating them individually as they make their way to the ground floor. There was also a school for spies that sums up the many ways you can approach a challenging problem. There were about six agents and I didn't really have the twitch skills to go in guns blazing. I could have thrown a grenade, but they were spread out and I would have been spotted by the survivors. I decided to toss some TNT at three of them that were close together; of the remaining three, one of them barged through the front door, which I had prepared with a proximity mine. The others were not going to share his fate, so one made for the side door, which I had also laced with proximity mines. Finally, the remaining spy beat a hasty retreat for a secret downstairs tunnel, which I had also prepped with a proximity mine. All I had to do was hide in a corner and let out a chuckle as their tortured screams filled the afternoon air.

There isn't as much sound-masked sniping as in 3, or even 4, but there are definitely 'shooting gallery' moments where you get your chance to snipe many many guards. The rest plays like a conventional stealth game and I didn't mind that. It's almost like a WW2-era Splinter Cell game - the last level is even similar to the Korea map from Chaos Theory, with you making your way through war-torn streets and enemy propaganda blasting through loudspeakers. There are some improvements over the previous installments. You now no longer have to press a button to tag an enemy, you can just hover over them for a few seconds and they're tagged. It's now possible to alt-tab without crashing the game, which is a bonus! The "radar" is better now (for the difficulties that use it) - it used to portray the enemies as dots on the HUD, which was a bit too easy since you knew exactly where they were at all times. Now, there will be a large translucent white circle that only shows their general area. You can only track them once they've been tagged. The difficulty level is also very atomistic, which I appreciated. You can decide how difficult you want separate components, like the aiming, the enemy AI, the HUD, etc. You can also have "invasions" - a multiplayer aspect where other players can enter your level and hunt you; you can use special phones to get an idea of the invader's location, but this also gives them a hint as to where you are. I didn't try it but you may like it if you're a Dark Souls fan. There's also a skill system that feels a bit tacked-on. You gain XP to gain more skills and they're fairly unremarkable - more health points, more items in your loadout, etc. I guess it's a more tangible xp reward system than previous games, but I could have probably lived without it.

Sound design is excellent, with very vivid foley work - also, I very much appreciated hearing the germanic cursing of your name to the sky, all the while yelling out loud that they're not afraid of the mighty GHOST SNIPER. The music is quite well done but I was very amused that, because the game takes place in France, the composer makes several attempts at shoehorning an accordion into even the sinister and tense string sections. The attempt at making the accordion into a menacing instrument is [i]adorable[/i]. A for effort. The AI is ok, nothing great. If you snipe without sound masking, guards will attempt to get a bead on your location and will frantically search for where the shots are coming from - of course if you make several shots from the same location, then I hope you surrounded your nest with proximity mines! Guards can sometimes get "stuck" which is an example of the buggy behavior that you can sometimes see in the game. However, Rebellion has done a lot of patching and also provided a free DLC - all the bugs that I encountered were mere nuisances and never prevented me from completing any objectives. Although, if multiplayer is your thing, I've heard that the included Easy Anti-Cheat can be a huge headache and you may want to proceed with caution. I didn't test it out myself. Aside from that, I note that bottles are much more useful now...they will almost always distract the AI away, even if they're actively hunting. This can help if you need a strategic way around multiple mobs.

Sniper Elite 5 is a third person shooter set during World War 2, where player character Karl Fairburne is sent on another mission to stop a top secret Nazi weapons project being developed in France.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

•	Missions take place in ruined cities, rural towns, and fortified German strongholds. Each location is quite large and contains multiple main and secondary objectives. There are usually a few different paths to move around each map.

•	You can equip a sniper rifle, SMG, and pistol. There are several different types of each weapon to unlock, and most of the ones I tried felt pretty good to use.

•	Each weapon can be customised with mods which are unlocked by finding workbenches hidden around each map. You can adjust stats such as damage, rate of fire, clip size, recoil, noise range, and reload speed. 

•	You can also carry various useful items such as medkits, grenades and mines. In addition to defending narrow chokepoints and doorways, one of my favourite uses for explosives was to booby trap corpses of enemy soldiers so that when someone else came to investigate, I’d eliminate them too.

•	Most enemies are equipped with the same pistols, SMGs and rifles that the player can use. You’ll also encounter a few armoured cars and tanks, so be on the lookout for panzerfaust RPGs.

•	There are a few ways to take advantage of stealth, including silenced weapons and sneaking up behind enemies for melee takedowns. You can whistle and throw bottles to cause nearby enemies to investigate the noise. And if there are loud environmental noises such as planes flying overhead, or cannons firing, this can mask the sound of your rifle fire. However, each map has a large number of enemies, and they can see you over quite a long distance, so I found it hard to stay hidden for long. 

•	When alerted to your presence, the AI will quickly identify your location and aggressively chase you, usually with multiple soldiers from different directions. Objective locations often have alarms which will summon more reinforcements until you disable the alarm. During a couple of missions I had lengthy and very chaotic firefights against massive numbers of enemies.

•	I played on the hard difficulty and while I died a few times on each mission, it was rarely frustrating. Most of my deaths resulted from attempting to be stealthy and messing up in an exposed location. When I started just shooting everyone on sight from a more tactically secure location, it actually became much easier.

[h1]Story[/h1]

•	The writing and voice acting are both average quality. The story only really exists to give you a reason to perform each mission objective.

•	The story doesn’t connect to the previous games in any significant way, so if you haven’t played the other games you wouldn’t feel like you’re missing anything.

[h1]Technical[/h1]

•	It took me 14 hours to complete the campaign and I only missed 2 optional objectives. There’s also a survival mode where you have to fight multiple waves of enemies while defending a control point, which could provide a few more hours of playtime.

•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

•	I didn’t have any crashes or framerate problems.

•	I noticed a frequent flicker/shimmer effect on distant objects like trees and narrow railings, which I think might be caused by poor anti-aliasing. You can’t choose which type to use, you can only select low/medium/high/ultra, which didn’t seem to make any difference.

•	There is some inconsistency relating to whether or not you can climb over walls and other waist high objects. Sometimes I approached an object that my eyes told me should be climbable, but the game wouldn’t let me interact with it.

[h1]Recommendation[/h1]

I really love this game. I'm a massive fan of the Sniper Elite series and in my opinion Sniper Elite 5 lives up to the series, though it is not a substantial leap in quality over Sniper Elite 4 in the same way Sniper Elite 4 was over 2 and 3. It's more of a side step, with certain areas improved, others worse, and others changed. 

There's been a ton of negativity surrounding this game, and while certainly it lacks the polish of 4, I think it has enough alterations to the formula over 4 that it can stand alongside 4 as a great Sniper game. While I don't think it is as well realized of a game as 4 (all of the components of that game worked together perfectly to make a game greater than the sum of its parts), I love the increased complexity of the game. I found the levels were larger in scope and more varied than 4, not just in terms of visual design but also in layout, approach, and gameplay. Along with the complete weapon customizability and non-lethal ammo types, there is far more player agency in the levels. While it doesn't have much positive gameplay function, I found the non-lethal options were a fun player-imposed challenge, and its honestly also fun to be a complete bastard and play judge, jury, and executioner based on what it says on the individual enemies bios. I also appreciated the fact that you get updates on the games missions/side missions by exploring the level itself and reading documents/overhearing conversations. I found the game generally easier and the sniping more forgiving than 4, but its still plenty challenging if you want it to be. Being able to unlock different starting locations for missions is a great touch as well. The biggest negative for me is that it is reasonably buggy, particularly with AI and animations, though this has improved quite a bit since launch. I really like the music as well. Different themes for the different levels is an awesome touch, and I really appreciate the more organic way the music changes based on the alert state of the enemies, over 4 which was often far too explicit in its music an audio cues. 

Sniper Elite 5 is not Sniper Elite 4, and I think in accepting that you'll come to find that 5 is a very good game indeed. I was pretty disappointed by this game after launch (probably in large part due to its super buggy state), but have come around to love it. It's refreshing to play a game that's super straightforward and gameplay focused without the fat and nonsense, though I still don't see that a skill tree is necessary in this game. 

There is a TON of content in the base game too, especially in considering the reduced MSRP. The single player levels are more expansive than they have ever been, you have multiplayer (which I am not much of a fan of in general but IMO the multiplayer in 5 is an undeniable improvement over 4), survival (a personal favorite game mode of mine) and invasion, which is an awesome, awesome addition. 

Don't buy the season pass though. It's an absolute rip off, particularly when its price is compared to the price of the base game.

"If it ain't broke, don't fix it" is probably this development team's motto, because Sniper Elite 5 builds upon the open-map and tactical diversity that began with the previous entry, whilist not changing around too many things.  It's not all just more of the same, though.

For one, gun customization has been greatly expanded, along with the overall gunplay.  Not only can you accurately aim down the sights with the handguns and SMGs (somethings the previous games neglected in favor of the sniper rifles), but with the proper gun upgrades its possible to turn the handguns into machine pistols, give the normally silent-but-weak Welrod a decent kick in exchange for being a bit louder, or craft the STG-44 into an accurate and damaging makeshift sniper rifle, if so desired.

The real treat this time around is the inclusion of the PvP Invasion mode, which is frankly a stroke of genius.  It works quite similarly to the invasions from Dark Souls in that another hostile player can drop into your campaign session at any given time, but it's overall less punishing since the game has a generous auto-save system and allows you to turn off the feature at any time if it becomes too annoying.

Survival mode is pretty fun too, but I'd advise raising the difficulty a bit - on medium with friends it's just too easy.  Can't speak about the competitive multiplayer since I've yet to touch it, nor will I likely ever get around to it since that's just not my type of thing anymore.

This game is a fantastic successor to Sniper Elite 4 and adds new features that fit right in with the franchise. They’ve improved the formula in almost every way, but didn’t compromise the core identity of the game. Rebellion understands the phrase, “If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it” and in the era of modern gaming, this is fantastic. And hey, if you’re just looking for a fun new action stealth game and haven’t touched a Sniper Elite game in your life, I highly recommend this to you too.

The core gameplay is incredibly strong. It feels well put together and satisfying to play. The game’s movement and weapon handling feels more tactile and immersive than ever before, especially with the new active reload system. The weapons feel punchy and the gunshots are very satisfying. The AI is a bit more dynamic this time around but it’s nothing to write home about, it’s stealth game AI. They can’t be perfectly smart even on the hardest difficulties or else the game wouldn’t be fun (This is why Invasion Mode is so fun. More on that later). The game also provides you with tons of different playstyles all equally viable, and with the addition of a graph summarizing your playstyle upon the end of the mission, it ups the replay value and feels fun to try different methods. If you’re a completionist, this game will give you something to chew on for a while with lots of collectibles, badges and achievements.

The actual narrative of the campaign is a bit different than other SE titles in that it actually tries to tell a bit of a story. It’s still mostly just “World War 2 people, doing World War 2 stuff.” But the characters are a little more memorable and there is a narrative that shines through. It’s not why you play the game, but it’s there. Just a way to provide reasons for why you’re playing through the missions that you are. It’s not bad, because it never tries to be good. Rebellion knows exactly what they’re trying to make and I respect that. It’s like John Wick, or Nobody. There doesn’t always need to be an incredible narrative, sometimes you can just have fun.

There are some cool gameplay features new to Sniper Elite that fit the formula pretty naturally. You can now pick up enemy weapons WITHOUT replacing what’s in your loadout, in the form of a “temporary weapon” that is dropped when empty, or unloaded manually for its ammo, meaning there’s a LOT more ammo to go around for your loadout weapons. You can now toggle between soft aim and aim down sights with any weapon, even SMGs and handguns. There’s nonlethal options now! I’m not a huge fan of the fact that sparing the nazis you’ve been sent to kill gives a huge XP bonus, I usually just wished I were able to spare one or two guys that I read about on the binoculars, not play a pacifist SOE commando behind enemy lines. But more optional gameplay styles are no skin off my back, always welcome, glad it doesn’t affect how I want to play. There’s also a more in depth customization system than Sniper Elite has ever had, with so many stats for each weapon it makes your head hurt. You can look more into the stats, or look at a simple visual summary if you don’t care. All the attachments available can start teetering on “cursed gun” territory like CoD Vanguard but nothing that’s unforgivable or COMPLETELY immersion breaking.

The multiplayer aspects of this game are cool, the deathmatch, free for all and objective modes are fun enough, they’re what you’d expect. It’s Sniper Elite but PvP. I haven’t sunk much time into these modes, but the time I have spent was very fun, it’s just not the thing I’m looking for when I boot up SE. When I do, it’s because I want fun stealth and cool killcams, but if you like the idea of sniper deathmatch, go nuts! There’s also Co-Op survival and campaign. Co-Op campaign seems a blast, I love Co-Op stealth experiences, but I don’t have any friends that play, and I haven’t felt the need to delve into Discord or Steam communities to find playmates. Survival seems to have gotten a bit of a downgrade in terms of map count and possibly map size as well, compared to SE4. It also feels much harder. Some command posts feel near impossible to defend from there just being no safe vantage points or high ground and there being way too many flank routes to viably defend against. Aside from a few QoL improvements to the survival formula, I prefer the experience of previous survival iterations more. Give us more maps, guys! Now, all other multiplayer aside, Rebellion has done something fabulous with this one:

There is now, of course, Invasion mode. Invade a player’s campaign mission and hunt them down as an Axis Sniper. That is so damn cool. It’s like the sniper boss fight in Metal Gear Solid, at its best. A tense matchup of two equals, a dangerous game of cat and mouse. At its worst, it’s a game of chicken where the other player finds your approximate location, and bum-rushes you with an SMG. But even then, it’s over quickly and you can get back to finding a good matchup! It’s usually an incredibly fun experience. I can’t figure out which side I like to play more. This may be my favorite mode. I’ve gotten over 100 kills now as the invader and something over two dozen kills as the invaded. Each has their own advantages and disadvantages. I highly recommend the campaign with Invasion on. Getting invaded by a thinking enemy when you’d otherwise breeze through the mission of hapless minions immediately changes the tone to something much more intense. Especially when that enemy can put on the exact same uniform as any other NPC and walk around slowly in a group with them, blending in near perfectly (This is still my favorite way to play as the Jaeger, even with the ghillie suit an option for me now).

Last but certainly not least is killcams. ALL weapons now feature killcams. Handguns, rifles and SMGs. It’s cool, I always wanted the option for other guns to have them. Cool cinematic trickshots shouldn’t be limited to just rifles! And like SE4, melee kills, traps and explosions all feature killcams now as well. There is so much more detail in the X-Ray models it’s almost too much, to the point of taking away from other details. It’s certainly gross and seems anatomically correct, but do I need to see like, the salivary glands in the jaw? It obscures the destruction physics on the bones! I digress. The boring, repetitive organ shots of SE4 have been improved. It used to be that any time there was a fatal shot on an organ, say a liver, that it would BLUR OUT all the other amazingly detailed layers (muscle, bone, etc.) and just focus on a hi-def render of a floating liver getting split in half, the same way, every time. But they’ve done away with this now! The frequency of this has been decreased, and the organs all dynamically respond to the caliber of the bullet that hit, and the direction it hit from. There are also bullet hole effects on enemies now, making X-Ray free killcams very brutal, and still immersive. Used to be that the ai would make a ridiculous face as a floating bullet phased through their nose, with no blood in sight. But no more! It’s a little lazy, just adding a generic blood spat on the exit wound. But when it covers a textured part of the body like the eye socket, it really looks like you blew the dude’s face off. When the blood effect is just pasted onto a flat surface, like the bald head of an enemy, or a torso, it looks pretty boring. And why oh why aren’t there destruction physics on the character models themselves? There’s a beautifully dynamic, fully destructible skeletal system, but if I blow a jaw off in the X-Ray, the guy’s chin is beautifully intact!! Anyway, the killcams have also been improved in every single way, I’m just nitpicking.

In summary this game MIGHT be the best in the franchise but I'd have to replay all to be 100% sure. Like I said, I recommend it to Sniper Elite veterans, shooter fans, and stealth game fans. Definitely a hard cop, maybe even get the DLC too.

Sniper Elated

The setting is WW2, the location this time is German occupied France. You play as an undercover operative called Karl Fairburne, your goal? To complete your mission in any way you see fit. Would you like to run in guns blazing, popping heads like fascist pinatas? You can do that. Would you prefer to become the night itself, sculking and sneaking your way to the target? You can do that. Or, would you rather play a sadistic game of cat and mouse with the A.I., setting traps like some sort of messed up WW2 themed home alone? Well, you can do that too.

Sniper Elite 5 manages to expand upon the familiar formula of Sniping and Eliteing used in previous installments, Karl feels more responsive than ever, the weapons feel punchier with great sound design to boot, the maps are huge and the A.I. isn’t as dumb as it once was.

However, nothing is perfect. I did encounter a few glitches and bugs that forced me to reload a previous save. The last “mission” is a big wet blanket, too short and the payoff feels cheap as hell.

Apart from that, it was a really fun game.

SE5 took some time getting used to.  For one thing, it's the first game of the SE series that does not have a Singleplayer mode.  Presently playing in Cadet difficulty to get a feel for the game then progressively enter the other modes to the top where I use trig to help guesstimate distance settings, etc. One thing I miss is when picking up equipment you now have to click the item to get it where as in SE4 all you needed was close proximity and it would automatically be equipped. 

Absolutely love the additional background info on the enemy soldiers when binoculars reticle is focused on their bodies.  Must have been fun for the developers to make up these background tidbits. Although only  80+ hrs. into SE5, and being limited to Cadet difficulty,  SE5 feels more open world in some ways but not in others.  More open in that the choices for the modes are more robust.  Can't wait to get into Invasion mode as this should make the game more interesting and also the ability of another player to enter your environment as a sniper to knock you off.  It's like a PvP and PvE in a Singleplayer like mode.  Love it!!

IMO the PvE (negotiating the terrain, getting from one objective to another) is not as open world as in previous SE series.  Many brush and rock hiding places are not as available in SE5 with less opportunities to stealth around things.  To me, that's not realistic as it should be.  Many times your forced into open territory needlessly or onto highways and walking/crouched or belly crawling the shoulder for long periods of time (10 seconds+)  Lucky for me no vehicles, tanks, etc. have advanced on me in this state, especially from my back.

All in all, it becomes more exciting as you play it and become more familiar with its characteristics.  Like any Sniper, you have to adapt to and overcome various conditions to meet and accomplish your objectives.  You'll enjoy it once you play it long enough.  Once you become familiar with SE5, like all the other series, you can't stay away from it.  At least, I can't.

Unlike many of the players offering reviews, I don't have any past SE baggage to drag into the conversation.  

SE5 is highly immersive. The enemies feel real especially when outside of buildings. Shooting feels real. Enemies will "pincer" you if you are not careful, or even come up from behind you.  (Inside of buildings they are less immersive).

One thing I love about this game is how highly detailed the difficulty settings can be, so you can tailor the game to your liking.   You can reach into the difficulty settings and do an amazing amount of customization.  Many games  offer "play it your way". This one delivers. 

Many people have commented that the open world has artificial barriers, such as a stone wall you can't climb over. And they are correct.  I originally thought these we programming limitations. And they sometimes feel like that.  But having played the game now for some hours I see (many) of these limitations as actually the dev's way to shape the level, to make the areas you can go more exciting.  It works for the most part, but running against one of these limitations during a heated battle can be frustrating.  So it's not a perfect system. Still, the battles feel real, and that's a pretty good thing.

There are many things the game shines in. "Sound masking" where you try to shoot when there is noise. You can of course sabotage generators and vehicles to making backfiring noise, but you can also shoot when a loud airplane flys by. It takes a while to learn the ins and outs of noise masking (for example, you have about 4 seconds to shoot after a generator/vehicle backfire) but when you do fully understand how it works your game enjoyment will increase a lot.

I love the weapon upgrades, but do find the "workbench system" somewhat contrived.  I wish physically finding them in the game world was more straight forward. There are 3 workbenches per mission but you don't know where they all are. Further, each workbench specializies in one of three weapon types - rifle, pistol, smg.  But they physically look identical. 	So if you have played any of the other 4 games you pretty much know how this works…. You have been tasked to infiltrate your way through a number of locations to weaken the enemies fortification so the fleet can stage their attacks on the Germans. Same plot as all the other games but with different locations and tasks. Ya know what, it aint broke and so no need to fix it! They even have the pretty much mandatory Hitler DLC. 

	What makes this game the best in the series you ask. Well absolutely nothing in my opinion. There are a whole slew of things I enjoyed about this game, but the only thing I feel that was added was a good coop play. If this was in part 4, I never tried it. But I did manage to cross play with a friend on their xbox for this version.

	Lets start with the looks. The game is very polished. There was a lot of attention spent on how everything looks. The smoke, explosions, weapons, and environment all look awesome. This is the best looking version of the 5. Taking that with a grain of salt, graphics have stepped up quite a bit since SE4. So that was expected. What I can say, is that the previous game had better looking locations due to its vibrant colors and focus on detail in cities. Considering this game returns back to a more gritty war environment, you loose some of that. There are some scenes that definitely show off what the game is capable of doing but they are small little sections on each level.

	Next we have the sound. No complaints about that. Voice acting is awesome with little sync issues. The acting was done in a respectable way that presents well to the overall feel of the game. Weapon sounds are done just right. They are not over bearing but definitely let you know what you are shooting. Explosions have that surround effect that just makes you feel like you just dodged something horrible.

	Then we get to the AI. Honestly I think this is where they spent the least amount of time. I consider SE3 the pinnacle of the series. It had a lot of things going for it to include a good set of AI characters. This game seams to use the halfway brain-dead logic from SE4. In one larger map, I managed to make a lot noise near a tower. Half the map ran over to investigate that. This gave me the opportunity to visit two almost three objective locations to set explosives with almost no guards around. I would say this was an isolated incident, however I was able to utilize this tactic throughout the game. I would love for them to take the AI that was in F.E.A.R. 1 and incorporate it into this game. That was the best AI I have ever seen in a shooter.

	Gameplay wise, I would say that nothing much has been changed over from previous games. The controls are intuitive and purposefully placed on a controller. The difficulty level jumps up and down depending on where you are in each map. Honestly, I think the first level was harder than some of the later levels. The game is plenty long. You are definitely getting your moneys worth. This does not even count the pass and DLC. For those looking to leader-boards or all the achievements, you will be playing this for a long while. There are so many little details like shooting a certain number of these small gnomes to keep you entertained. 

	Summing things up, The game is awesome. There is definitely a lot to do and a definite challenge in many locations. The story is on par with all the other Sniper Elite games. Graphics are really well done and complimented with a great audio experience. If you are a fan of the series or just starting out in the Sniper Elite world, you cannot go wrong with this title.

In order to enjoy your time playing these games you have to be within the top ten percent of all players or else you will just get killed over and over again by players who are sadder and sweatier than you, players who can find and properly get shots off at your head before you can even get your cursor on their avataar..... Because of the "realistic map design," the game forces you into their bad stealth.....CLOSE RANGE combat, in a SNIPING GAME, because the maps are near claustrophobic. A few maps are a bit more open and include a few open fields with bushes at every angle blocking your views. To top it all off, DLC suck as of the time of this review...so I either didn't buy them or returned them.

The invasion mode is the only thing I play on this game anymore. Using your map knowledge to track down the Allied sniper with the AI's locations, the completed objectives, and the sound cues which the sniper might cause is extremely fun and satisfying. Then once you find them you get to land the classic Sniper Elite cinematic X-Ray kill or get into a sniper battle with you flanking to a new position. It's thrilling.... but has some flaws. Many games end with the Allied sniper getting killed by the AI before you get close and ending the match as a victory (witch doesn't count as a kill for you in order to unlock items) or, they finish the level as soon as you spawn. The Victories and losses aren't tracked at all actually; only your direct kills on the sniper are counted and tracked. But you get nothing past the 100 ghillie suit other than a number going up. Even still, the invasion mode is FUN and by far the best part of this game. If this game mode were to be split off into its own game somehow, I'd only buy that and ignore the rest of this game.

It's exactly what you'd expect from a third person perspective game based around sniping.... people camping in one spot for much of the match and using third person to peep over walls. I know some people like it but I find it boring. 

     That's all I've got to say about this game, hope it helps you....

THIS IS AN UPDATE TO MY OLDER REVIEW IN WHICH I RECOMMENDED SE5, BUT HERE'S A NEW ONE ADDRESSING THE CURRENT STATE OF THINGS:

Sniper Elite 5 Falls Short: A Beautiful Shell with Disappointing Updates and Lackluster Content

Sniper Elite 5 had the potential to be a standout game in the series, but unfortunately, it missed the mark on several important aspects. Here's a breakdown of my experience, taking into account the game's positive and negative aspects:

Visually Stunning, but Superficial:
One cannot deny that Sniper Elite 5 is a visually stunning game. The graphics are top-notch, with attention to detail that immerses players in the game world. However, it quickly became apparent that the game's visual appeal was merely a façade, masking deeper issues that detracted from the overall experience.

Intriguing Invasion Mode Lost in Updates:
The Invasion mode initially piqued my interest, offering a unique twist on the gameplay. It had the potential to provide hours of entertainment. However, any enthusiasm quickly evaporated when I discovered that every update for new content required a whopping 60GB download. This excessive requirement not only proved to be a hassle but also strained my patience and ultimately diminished my enjoyment of the game.

Multiplayer: A Haven for Cheaters:
The multiplayer aspect of Sniper Elite 5 proved to be a letdown. Both console (Yes we know cheating on consoles is a thing) and PC players faced an onslaught of cheaters, ruining the competitive integrity of the game. The lack of adequate anti-cheat measures made the multiplayer experience an exercise in frustration and disappointment. It's disheartening to see the developer's failure to address this glaring issue, leaving legitimate players to contend with an unfair playing field.

Insulting "New Content":
One of the most infuriating aspects of Sniper Elite 5 was the so-called "new content" updates. Instead of delivering substantial additions to enhance gameplay, the updates merely consisted of three new items, such as skins and some weapons. To make matters worse, these additions were not even available for all characters (if rebellion wants to add skins at least please do it for all characters). This lackluster approach to expanding the game content feels like an insult to the loyal customers who were promised meaningful updates and improvements.

In Conclusion:
While Sniper Elite 5 initially impressed with its beautiful graphics and intriguing Invasion mode, it ultimately falls short due to its problematic updates, rampant cheating in multiplayer, and insulting "new content" additions. The game's superficiality and failure to deliver on promised improvements leave players feeling unsatisfied and betrayed. I hope that the developers take these criticisms seriously and make the necessary changes to provide a more fulfilling experience for their loyal customer base.

[h1] This is going to be a weird one. [/h1]

I will try to abstain to it, but I will most likely drop some minor spoilers of this game's story. As B movie as Sniper Elite tends to be, some people might not like it being spoiled. You have been warned.

If you want me to substantiate what I say in this review: I have played all Sniper Elite games except the first, never touched Nazi Zombie Army but watched full playthroughs of most of them.


TL;DR: This plays almost like a side-grade to 4, its actually quite fun once you get used to it, but it feels like a "Megaman Zero 4" effect where things were changed solely for the purpose of making the game feel different to 4.

Sniper Elite 5 is certainly one of the more divisive titles in the series history, and that's even with Nazi Zombie Army and the whole Epic Games fiasco that happened a while ago. I can see why it does have a somewhat mixed reputation from most of the longtime players of the series, regardless there is some merit to be found in many aspects the game offers.

Gameplay at its core is still Sniper Elite, you have 3 weapons, an assortment of traps and distraction tools, and your goal is to move through the expansive maps to complete your missions and any side missions you encounter along the way, while also finding the best spots to pick people off from long range. The real difference lies in the nuances and subtle changes to the formula that make it stand differently from its predecessor. 

There is a level of weapon freedom much more pronounced in 5 than other previous entries. Newly added Weapon customization allows you to kit out all 3 of your weapons to your heart's content, provided you have parts unlocked. You can make the loudest, most powerful rifle imaginable, or you can sacrifice performance for stealth with the addition of a variety of suppressors, some quieter than others. This system makes every single weapon a worthwhile investment, and makes loadouts more interesting as a whole. Want to snipe with a pistol? You can do that. Want to create a stealthy, near absolutely silent SMG? You can do that. Want to go full German and run around with a scopeless Kar98? You can do that. Unfortunately, this same system also dilutes the identity of what makes Sniper Elite . . . well . . . Sniper Elite. It somewhat removes the purpose of the Rifle if you can simply kit out an SMG or a pistol with a silencer and a scope, and often times the Rifle is much, *much* louder than both unless you have suppressors only found in the later portions of the game. Given that there is also a strange closeness to this game that I will elaborate on later, this can make it feel more like you're playing "Commando Elite" instead of "Sniper Elite".

You can also select what kind of bullets to use in your weapon, carrying up to two extra types for each weapon in addition to the standard ammo for general use. Each serves a purpose in-game, AP can destroy locks and damage vehicles quicker, Non-Lethal allows you to knock out soldiers for extra XP, Subsonic makes your gunshots significantly quieter, you get the idea. As novel of a concept this is, it generally doesn't have much of a use outside of making things slightly more convenient to do for the player. It almost, *almost* feels like a tacked on, slightly more expanded concept of suppressed ammo from the last game.

Weapon choice and Enemy Choice feels a little lackluster in my opinion, I like what is there but there could be so much more. Referencing Sniper Elite 4, there were quite a few Italian weapons to better represent that "You're in Italy, go fight the pizzapasta people and their German friends." I don't see that as much in this one, both in terms of Weapons and Enemies. There are a grand total of 2 french weapons you can use: The RSC 1917, and the Model D. Where is the MAS-36? Where is the MAS-38? MAS-44? Berthiers? Lebels? Where the ♥♥♥♥ is Vichy even? I was expecting at least a few French turncoats to plink at. Instead its all Germans [spoiler] and some Japanese later on.[/spoiler] Its not the biggest deal, but it just feels bizarre to have so few weapons from the theater you're in. Maybe its future DLC? I dunno.

The Map design in Sniper Elite 5 is both good and bad, if that makes any sense. Maps are still large and impressively detailed, supposedly they referenced real historical photos of Nazi-Occupied France and it really shows. The areas genuinely look like the real deal, and I'm not one to care all that much for scenery, but I can appreciate it when it shows up. Unfortunately, the map design can be really hit or miss from a gameplay standpoint, especially early on when the maps feel really close quarters-y. Again with the whole "Commando Elite" thing, the first half of the game has not many opportunities for long-distance sniping. This gets better later on and the maps do get a fair bit more open and visible after the first half, but it can be very off putting to quite a fair bit of people. I think the highlight of maps is how you discover objectives, some are given, some you have to find. Finding them can range from hearing a conversation between 2 soldiers, or by finding a collectable that indicates the objective (Usually a military document). Its a really novel system and I like the idea that not everything is laid out to you immediately, you actually have to do some scouting (You know, that thing that snipers would sometimes do, especially commandos working with a resistance?).

The story is pretty standard as far as the series goes. Karl Fairburne is dropped into X place to foil the plans of Y Nazi High-Ranking Officer to stop Z from happening, with Z usually being a war-winning superweapon or strategem. Moller is an okay antagonist as far as the series goes, he is not Bohm by any means, but he is not completely boring, Its fun watching him piss himself from Karl undoing his years of work.

Overall, Sniper Elite 5 is still a fun game and still manages to stay in the same vein as its Predecessors. Its not quite a step forward from 4 however. It feels almost as a side-grade, again bringing up the Megaman Zero 4 analogy for those who understand. It feels like it was made different for the sake of making it different from 4, for better and worse. Its a solid 7, maybe an 8 depending on your taste. I would at least recommend waiting for a sale unless you're really sold on the concept of sniping in france.


EDIT: Forgot to talk about bugs. This is probably due to me playing well past day 1, but I have not encountered any game breaking bugs, nor any that couldn't be solved by saving and then just reloading to fix a pathing issue (Looking at you Wolf Mountain). So I cannot comment on what people have experienced beforehand, for me it was relatively bug free aside from maybe a ragdoll inverting out of existence.

Again the umpteenth World War II Senario but more versatile. Sniper Elite is, after all, a seventeen -year -old series that revolves around the sniper Karl Fairburne, who takes on the Nazis during the Second World War. The first parts revolved around fighting in Berlin, the third part brought Karl to Africa and the fourth part took place in Italy. Sniper Elite 5 uses an even more recognizable setting for many. This time Karl ends up in Normandy, where on the eve of D-Day he has to ensure that the invasion can be a success. Once in France, Karl tracks down a mysterious plan that, if we can believe the Nazis, the war can decide to their advantage. To the one -man army called Karl Fairburne, the clean task to thwart that operation!

Although there is a lot of tactical or if a sniper to go through, there is a lot of recognisability from the previous versions, which makes it less attractive for me, at least from my point of view. Furthermore, the entire gameplay is reasonable to properly adjust to any difficulty per game component, which can be quite useful to achieve and unlock certain achievements. And anyone who knows how to deal with that tactically can easily play the game and unlock all the achievements.

The possibility that other players can penetrate your game or level is a fun and exciting experience and gives an extra dimension. All in all a good game that gives beautiful pictures in the graphic area but at the same time a lot of the same from the previous versions and that makes it a bit monotonous. The yellow and red colors warn you that enemies are on the track or are in fighting. That works intuitively as a steering element; You don't want yellow and certainly no red at all. In addition, the game assesses you at the end of a mission and thereby shows elements as how often you have been seen through enemies and how often the alarm has gone off. So you are clearly sent in the direction of Stealth, which means that Sniper Elite 5 is indeed more a tactical spy game than just a pure snipers game.

As mentioned, it is possible to penetrate games from others, as a sniper on the German side. The player who is busy as Karl Fairburne then receives a report that there is an enemy sniper nearby with an indication of where that sniper is. The telephone system in the game that players can provide extra information about where the enemy is, is also a funny element. This creates a cat and mouse game between Karl and an enemy sniper, which without a doubt yields the most exciting moments in Sniper Elite 5. The dynamic changes when it becomes two-to-one. As soon as you as a loner manage to kill one of the two players, the other player from the team of two only has three minutes to kill you because otherwise you will win the game by definition. That produces a nice tactical issue. So it pays to try to attack one of the two players quickly, because you only have to keep yourself hidden afterwards to let the other take all the risks. And if you don't want all this, you can also turn off the option to have intruders in your game.

In summary, 'Sniper Elite 5' has nice parts, but it is not convinced to me enough and I found the storyline a bit boring. I understand the chosen course of the game developer and you can go through the game as well as a sniper or in stealth mode from start to finish. All in all, it looks like a kind of Hitman game. And for the target group that knows these games a little less well and is not waiting for a very high level of difficulty, then Sniper Elite 5 can be set so that it is still a very nice game. I think the purists among us will miss the focus on real sharp shooting, but at least they can also opt for an authentic level of difficulty.

Regards Q

[b]Sniper Elite[/b] is back with more Nazi super-weapons, more Karl Fairburne and more gruesome bullet cams; if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it. This successful series is serving an old recipe with some newly added buzzwordy ingredients, including weapon customization, non-lethal takedowns and more.

[h1]Setting[/h1]
This time, the year is 1944, the German stranglehold on Europe is loosening as desperation begins to set in for the Third Reich. The Allies are about to launch the largest amphibious assault ever to be seen in history. You play as Karl Fairburne, an elite sniper who has yet to find his match. Your objective, along with some U.S. Army Rangers, is to weaken the Atlantic wall in preparation for the Normandy landings. However, Fairburne soon assigns himself his own mission, destroying the new wunderwaffe, Operation Kraken.

[h1]Weapon Customization[/h1]
The most notable change to the series is the ability to select new attachments for your many armaments. Suppressors, muzzle brakes, night-vision scopes and more are among the various pieces one can use to modify their weapons. No longer must you be content with a single silenced sidearm or DLC weapon; you can now live out your dream of infiltrating enemy lines with suppressed SMGs.

However, one curious addition to all of this are less-than-lethal rounds, the long-range solution for a pacifist run, working in conjunction with non-lethal stealth takedowns. As far as I know, you don’t receive any bonuses — or achievements for that matter — for being a pacifist, other than being able to live out some grand fantasy of being an elite operative who saves their blade for the hearts of the most malicious of enemies, if they even have a heart. Do be careful, however, that your unconscious victims don’t land in centimeter-deep puddles, they will hilariously drown themselves and you will have a conscience to clear.

[h1]Level layout[/h1]
The missions in [b]Sniper Elite 5[/b] feel like they were an attempt at making realistic levels that felt like they were organically evolving and to some extent they achieved this. The previous entry in the series had almost every, if not all, optional objectives revealed to you through character interactions before even starting the mission, sort of like a debriefing, whereas [b]Sniper Elite 5[/b] will often have optional objectives revealed to you either by listening in on conversations between soldiers, or simply stumbling upon them as you go from point A to B. Many missions also have roads with traffic going through checkpoints, which stop those vehicles for inspection making the map feel alive, though the illusion may only last through your first campaign.

None of that is to say that this game’s level layout is a masterpiece. As much as I jumped for joy at the ability to mount stationary machine guns, I didn’t find an opportunity to use it, that being said, I didn’t perform any sort of extensive search to find said opportunity.

[h1]The Resistance[/h1]
One feature I was hoping to see the return of were resistance forces. The previous installment saw the Italian partisans fighting the fascists in skirmishes for at least two missions. Disappointingly, however, you never see the French resistance forces fight anywhere. Fairburne even participates in an airborne assault on German positions along with Army Rangers, but you never see them in action either; it’s like having your significant other send a lewd text, only to find them sleeping in bed when you get home.

[h1]Axis Invasion[/h1]
On a more positive note, there’s another new addition to the formula; the Axis Invasion game mode allows you to drop into another player’s campaign as Jäger, Fairburne’s Nazi counterpart whose description declares him as infamous, but he may be better described as being opportunistic.

The best time for Jäger to strike is when his rival is in a firefight, when he will be ensnared and unaware of the glare coming from Jäger’s scope. Therefore, those going up against Jäger must not get tied down in an unwinnable fight. It is best for Fairburne to run and hide, rather than become a sitting duck for Jäger’s crosshair. But one particularly useful skill Fairburne does boast is his innate ability to sense from which direction Jäger might be coming from until he gets too close, then Fairburne’s senses will tell you that he’s right on top of you. Jäger, however, may get even more detailed information on his rival’s location as he can have fellow soldiers report it directly to him. Notably, however, Jäger can invade a co-op campaign and in that instance, should he be successful in eliminating one sniper, the other will have just three minutes to avenge his friend’s death.

This game mode has the potential to make a high-stakes game of stealth, however good luck in finding a good match if you don’t have a friend to play with. Rarely did I find a skillful sniper in strangers’ campaigns. Most of the time they abandoned the idea of stealth at the first sign of trouble leading to an easy win for Jäger.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Much of the [b]Sniper Elite[/b] series could be accurately described as a casual stealth experience, the same is true here — especially so in many co-op campaigns — with the potential exception of Axis Invasion, which makes stealth a borderline-necessity. [b]Sniper Elite 5[/b] took around 20 hours to complete the campaign, mostly stealthing with a few instances of careless running-and-gunning plus a half hour of incidentally recreating the JFK assassination with a Nazi officer. The non-existence of friendly soldiers clashing with Germans is only disappointing because of the potential that such an improvement could’ve brought, the Italian partisans were present in the last game, but they felt like a test run rather than an integral part of the game. Thus with all that being said, most of what was present in [b]Sniper Elite 4[/b] is still present here, with a few great additions and all with the latest game being cheaper in price, thus I think veterans of the series will like this iteration. Overall, it was quite enjoyable and I can see myself playing through it again.

Sniper Elite 5 is an installment in the series that doesn't set out to reinvent the wheel. Rather it refines and iterates on elements to make for a smoother and rich experience. 

There are a few new traps and tools at your disposal this time around like bottles, decoys, and shu mines. Weapon customization returns with a variety of options to suit your loadout for your preferred playstyle. 

Enemy AI has improved and will surprise you at times when they manage to flank you. At other times the AI can still be rather stupid and stand outside in the open if they don't know where you are or are firing from. But those are the exception not the norm. 

Like Sniper Elite 4 before it? The scale is even bigger with some truly large maps that can take you two hours or more to complete. Depending on whether you go stealth or loud of course.

The Kill Cams look as gory and superb as ever. Melee kills feel more visceral as well. 

The biggest and most impactful addition however is the Invasion mode. Where you can be invaded by other players or you can invade them. It turns the game into a game of cat and mouse and can lead to incredibly tense moments as you and the other sniper try to figure out where each other are. There are phones to radio to roughly reveal where the enemy is. But doing so alerts the other player. You can't camp as your position is revealed to the invader if you do. It's great fun and yes you can play co-op with invasions which means you and a partner can use tactics like baiting the enemy into looking for one...while the other kills them. This may seem unbalanced, but even if you have two players against an invader...if the invader kills one of you? You have a limited amount of time to kill the invader. They still only need to kill one of you and if you can't revive your teammate or kill the invader? You lose. It's a great dynamic that adds further replay value to the game. 

If you like the previous games? You will enjoy this one. I

This review will highlight some of the German kit, which was a huge plus to me as a reenactor. Generally speaking, most games are horrible about getting the small details of kit right. while this game does still have stuff wrong, its *technically* correct even if unlikely (for 1944) for so much early war kit to be plentiful.


The german kit, overall, is quite good albeit basic. The regular infantry is clearly based on a reenactor, as the gas mask can is identical to the modern reproduction cans, which have shallower ribs in the can compared to an authentic gas mask can. The tunic is an early war M36, with early war Litzen on the collar. The shirt is the mid-late war soft cotton it seems, which is a common reenactor-ism. That is, being worn for an impression covering any time period of the war. The boots are well done, especially gamaschen with the low boots. 

You do have one mistake early in the video regarding low boots. They were not issued as a cost-saving measure, they were issued alongside the marching boots. Their frequency within units all depended on the unit itself. Some units were only issued lowboots and others just marching boots. 

The officer seems to be wearing the iron cross first class, second class ribbon and a knights cross on his neck... which is ambitious for a generic field officer.

The Jaeger class is just a Fallschirmjaeger, which is also well done. The zeltbahn tents are also well done, along with the weaponry and German vehicles. The helmets are late war M42 helmets, which would have been an odd combination with an early war tunic. They have good k98 ammo pouches, but I was disappointed to not see any K43 pouches in the game. 

All the small details, kit laying around, field items like the trinkwasser, and propaganda posters are a great touch. 

For vehicles and equipment markings, they just picked unit logos out of a bucket it seems. The anti-tank guns all seem to be the smaller 37mm, which was gone by 1944, and they have the logo of the 12th SS on them. 

US uniforms are quite rough. but alright.

The story leaves much to be desired, but there are some comical oversights. Such as you liberate the town in Liberate, advancing North, only to have Sherman tanks move through the town to advance south... where you just killed like 100 people. Overall, the game's story is easily forgotten, it is generic as hell. But if you like shooting Germans in ww2, popping skulls and nutsacks, this is the game for you.  8/10 imo

This series has evolved and grown a lot. I honestly didn't like the first 3. 4 was ok, but this is actually pretty good. Secondary missions appear and evolve as the primary mission happens, just like real time warfare targets of 'opportunity' are found and become things you can do or not do. I like this format a lot, it feels organic. The sniper cam is cool, but just like previous titles only the first 10 or 12 times you get it. After awhile it's clear regardless of how you shoot there are only a handful of headshot sequences you're going to get. My biggest issue with this game, remains my biggest issue with the series. Except for headshots, guns don't do proper damage. I cannot count how many times I've nailed an enemy center of the chest and they are stunned, but re-compose themselves and remain combat effective. This is World War 2. There was no body armor or bullet proof vests, if a Kar98 hits you in the chest, you're dead. Sometimes helmets deflect bullets and I'll buy that, it did happen. But he game has some broken math, for instance the .45 pistol, if not a headshot, takes roughly 3 shots to kill and enemy in the chest. The .45 thompson sub machine gun, firing the SAME bullets but faster, takes 5+ shots to kill the same enemy. That's not how weapons work, firing faster doesn't mean less dangerous. Finally, and this is trivial, I was super heart broken to see the anti-tank rifle A) fires a tiny round instead of a big proper sized bullet, someone messed up on that and B) does NOT make people explode on impact, the bullets hit with the same force as the normal rifles which is entirely incorrect, you hit someone with a round made for a tank and they pop. 5 games into the series and it still feels like there is room to grow and some basic things should be understood about how firearms work. BUT, at the end it actually is a fun game even if the maps are a bit tediously large and laid out.

That's a little bit sad -- that is, you shouldn't need to run around an trigger thresholds/spots and then run away to get good sniping distance (if you can).

But again, it'a a beautiful game and a worthy sequel of SE4.

Ok so this game definitely has flaws, theres no doubt about it, but I also think it doesnt deserve the semi-hate it gets. It has a lot of fun weapon customization, different ammo types for different situations and imo some very cool missions. Yes we lost the golden camos and got some boring camouflage ones, yes the dlc's as of now are veeery underwhelming but I wouldn't go that far as to call it bad.

And probably the best thing for me the invasion mode which is most likely the best thing that happened to this game, without it I definitely wouldn't have played it as much as I did. Yes its definitely not flawless either but I have my hopes up that there will be a lot more updates to come

the game is better in visuals though i like the sniper elite 4 upgrade system better, The axis invasion where i m playing single campaign and invaded by a multiplayer sniper is the definition of creativity. its a game changer not only in sniper elite 5 but a new genre of that type.The only thing though its still constrained as a single default type i think itll expand in the future further.
i like it as the multiplayer is fun to play as well.

Very good. I have gotten this about a month ago and I've got to say this game is amazing, the details are amazing and so are the graphics, and the missions are interesting 100% recommend it
It is very fun, you are not John Wick, but you can get out if you plan ahead.  Also, the Jager thing adds alot more variety, even to the campaighn that I think is implimented well.

I'm a big fan of the series.  I only play single player so I can't comment on that aspect f the game.  For me this game is really good and continues the adventures of our fearless sniper.  I've played it on every difficulty setting.  I like to start of with casual play where you have aim assist so I have time to explore and then move to authentic.  I also turn off bullet cam for more realism.   The graphics are good as are the weapon ballistics.  The game has an occasion issue but nothing major.  If you like WW2 shooters this is a good one

There might be a few things I miss from SE4, like the wire traps etc.
But this game makes up for them by being big mapped, very good AI (when setting to authentic) And I am loving invasion mode.

Right now, there's been a 40Gb content patch that chonks up this games data to 120Gb total. Ouch. You'd better delete some of your files before you get this game because it is AWESOME. Really makes me feel like an elite agent sent in before the army comes, while being hunted by enemy agents through the invasion system. Invasion system now allows you to set it to Invite Only, letting friends be the Elite Nazi scalps that you collect throughout the whole campaign. And if you play smart as the main character, you will scalp enemy players who must rely on the info passed on from their threatening yet misleading Axis AI allies. Freshest part of the game.

Though I did buy this game on a discount, I would say it is worth the full price. But if you can get it on sale then great. The DLC on the other hand I would not say it is worth its $15 price tag. The visuals and Game-play are stunning and as normal with this series the story is fantastic.

started out as a ~6/10, seeing this as a Metal Gear Solid: Phantom Pain... but less complex in every way, from no base admin (which was welcome because it did get a lil long in MGS:PP), to incoherent decisions about which walls you can or cannot jump over (which is just lazy & stupid, hence the 6/10, but still I could live with it 6/10) .... but now after 10hrs.... am a 3/10. it gets boring quick, and your play style/approach per level becomes the same. it's the most closed/no-real-options of a self declared 'sandbox' i've ever seen

if you're fortinute so the £/$ means nothing to you and you want an easy thinking-free week/weekend, then hit it (i have had some fun with it), but if you think about the cost and/or want to really engage with game, look elsewhere

Yeah ... so it's not Sniper Elite 4 v2, or an upgraded SE4 with more missions - but that's not what I expected anyway. If that's what one expect SE5 isn't quite up to par, can't really put my finger on why though. I'm a 98% pve player though, so that might be why.

On its own though, it's a game where you can roam around on big maps - not open world as you will find paths iinexplicably blocked, although you can get to the area behind that block by taking another route ... somewhat irritating. 

I'm a somewhat exploring type of gamer, and in that capacity this game tend to reward me when I start roaming around and not just follow the main mission points. Extra missions pops up, special killing missions and so on, and that's always fun.

So ... I do like the game, just need to take time to explore a little, and its rewarding - the ai isn't all that stupid, allthough it could be better ... and possibly a few more npcs.


Edit : What would've made it immensly better was if the developers/map designers had made the maps more vertical - in mission 3 the map could've been so much better if they'd actually made more of the buildings open/more floors.

Basically, the game is a stealth game with a little bit of sniper action. If you like sneaking around and taking out German soldiers, then get this game. Interestingly you get a massive point bonus at the end of each mission for just knocking everyone out. Kind of strange in a war, leaving all these knocked-out soldiers all around. But the maps are big and you are pretty free to go around where you want. You can do some shots, but there is not much sound cover in a lot of missions and you will be heard pretty easily. I like games sneaking around, so for me, it's worth it. Other versions 1-4 were better, but it's not as bad as some people complain.

I tried my best to give this game a good shot, but from weapons fallign through the ground, to enemies not loading in and forcing me to restart the entire mission, to objectives outright being failed and the game not telling me when something like that occurred needing for me to restart the whole mission AGAIN just to try and complete the objective, to the fact that you can't use weapons you pick up for more than the ammo it currently has and nothing more and can't even switch off the weapon without dropping it and ENTIRELY ruining the point of scavenging around for weapons to take from your surroundings...

I tried to refund this game because of all of its glitchy, buggy, half-baked and little thought-out mechanics coming together as a whole to make something unsatisfying...and because I wanted to give this game a shot, I REALLY wanted to after how much I loved SE4, I wholeheartedly do not recommend you get this game. Don't fall into the same trap that I did. This game only reared its ugly head after a few hours of play, and it WILL make you regret how it plays and feels in comparison to how good 4 was. I was excited to actually keep up with this series after how well things came up altogether prior, but I am thoroughly disappointed. Please, please, save yourself the money, as the glitches and bugs I have found have not even been attempted to be patched out. After all, why scavenge around at all in a level to try other things out when instead your guns can fall through the floor when you try to make a stockpile? In MULTIPLE areas? Please, save yourself the trouble...as of course, since I 'passed the 2 hour mark when attempting to refund the game, I am ineligible for a refund.' It's clear these guys want to focus on multiplayer...in a series that never focused on multiplayer ever before, and left things dissatisfying in single player.

I honestly do not know why anyone would say that this is not a fun game to play. It is what i was waiting for, met all the expectations, and just delivered on what it set it out to do. It is another of the series and it is excellent. The artwork, the mechanics and the play are what most games get wrong, but Rebellion got right.  It can be a lot of fun, for those that do not get it, well - move along.  If you don't like it, don't play it. This one does not disappoint and is everything I expected it to be.  Seeing the progression from Rebellion makes me think they've got a winning formula here for a good game. Seeing the people saying it isn't fun is just like, why bother? There are games that have serious flaws and warnings are warranted. This is not one of those - this one is fun, challenging and enjoyable for a stealthy challenge. If you take your time, each level can take hours to play. If you have no patience, likely not a game for you.

Very fun, like if Ghost Recon and Splinter Cell had a baby and it was born in WW2. The controls are admittedly annoying at times (Oh you're carrying a body and quickly need to dump it? That's not how this game was designed.

I simply do not understand why you would develop a newer version that is no where near as appealing as the prior version.  I can promise I will be very skeptical and likely never make another purchase from Rebellion as a direct result.  It is such a waste of money.

Bland gameplay. Fraction of weapon selection. Weapon modifications are cursed to hell. Story is boring. Characters are terrible. Rebellion tried to make a WW2 Sam Fisher copy and failed in the dullest way possible.

My storage doesn't appreciate the additional 45.7 GB update that their 1 map, 2 weapon DLC added. 

Game can be fun with a friend, however they go forwards in some areas, and backwards in others. For a sniping game, there sure are a lot of invisible walls. The term open world loosely applies to the game when you put invisible barriers up that severely limit your avenues of approach which mainly hurts you in Axis Invasion. The focus ability that the Allied sniper has should not be implemented the way it is currently in Axis Invasion. I understand trying to level the playing field but if you use focus, it feels overpowered, practically wall hacks (when close) or a compass (when far away) that tells you where the enemy Jäger is.

Minor complaints: 
-The cover art shows this massive D-Day landing with all these allied troops behind you. In game, you never fight alongside Allied infantry, or see so much as 2 allied infantrymen together. 

-AI is incompetent, German Snipers will stay "in combat" and shoot at a wall if it is in the last known direction of the Allied Sniper.

-How do you manage to mislabel a German Panther tank a Tiger in a game with this much funding. This is one mistake of many that big developers making a World War 2 game should not be making.

What would be great is some new campaign levels for Sniper Elite 4, best game ever made. Cheers!

The game is different than previous versions (v2,3,4) but not bad. Little things like the flash of a telescope or very visible characters in the multiplayer are annoying - it's impossible to hide somewhere, aim and shoot - such dances behind the cover. In the campaign, the characters are not so visible, there is a more gray monochromatic scenery, where the enemies blend in more with the surroundings - there are places where you have to look closely to spot them (and graphics settings are set to High and over 60 FPS, RX 6600 XT). And somewhere I read a review that the shooting distances are smaller than in the previous parts. My opinion on this subject is that compared to the previous parts, the scale of the maps is different, what in the previous parts was about 300m, now it is 200m - that's my impression. And weapon modifications are exaggerated in my opinion - well, where for a handgun a long stock, or a metal one, and an additional handle, or armor-piercing ammunition. fun with modifications that forcibly turn a pistol into a shotgun.
Updates are the worst. Well, once a week, name, u,. I turn on the computer on Saturday and want to play - NOOO, now a few GB update. Now (July 27, 22) 44GB update again!! Come on, control yourself - the whole game was downloading 55GB during installation, and then another 6GB if I remember correctly. So that you can play without updating and turn it on after the end of the game, that's how I understand it, but steam wants it now and it's over. It's annoying.

In the end, I don't know if I can recommend it or not. Because if some fan of the series (probably I am, but a staunch believer), expects similarity to the previous parts, it's a bit of an old "sniper", but more stealth and melee combat than ranged combat. Opponents, on the other hand, look for the "intruder" more, searching not only those parts of the map where they were on duty, but also other parts. Because the map is divided into parts to do specific tasks. And as in the older "snipers" the opponents moved only in one part of the map, so in the "five" they also search in other parts where they did not have a patrol. And there are units that raise an alarm, which causes the arrival of reinforcements from other "parts" of the map, or, for example, from passing vehicles - when they notice a corpse or hear shots.
As someone new and this will be his first contact with this series of games, he may not fully feel the atmosphere that was in the previous parts. I personally do not regret the purchase. However, I liked the multiplayer maps and the overall graphics (colors, contrast) more in "4" - because "3" is a cheater's paradise.
I recommend five, but conditionally. If someone expects a graphical revolution and similar gameplay as in its predecessors, then no, but if he is open to changes in the way the game is played and more gray graphics (in my opinion) and extensive character building, then yes.

One thing of note that I completely didn't expect:

I was hiding in some tall grass near an open gate between hedges to a road.  On the other side was a guard I wanted to get near me so I could incap them.  I tossed a bottle behind the hedge getting the guard's attention.  As he walked over, crossing the road, an oncoming transport's headlights shown on him and honked their horn. It’s Sniper Elite. There’s some new additions here as with every new addition to the series. But it’s more or less the same visceral, satisfying action game you remember.

The biggest change is the idea of invasions -- other players busting down your door mid-game, usually as you’re carefully infiltrating a nazi mansion, or gunning down a blockade. Always a little inopportunely. Always a little too frequently. And always a serious monkey wrench in your machinery.

I love it. It fits the rest of the ethos perfectly. These games have always been about embracing a bit of chaos. Sure, it disturbs the otherwise meticulous and predictable gameplay. But it’s all about being allowed to play and improvise. It’s not really a puzzle, even if you can treat it as one. But you can throw caution to the wind too. 

You’re allowed to bring out the big guns one moment, and recede into the darkness the next. No one makes you feel bad, or lectures you about how to play. In fact, the game implores you to explore both its world and all the mechanisms and systems.

Invasions embrace that, turning games into heart-throbbing cat-and-mouse rounds. Both parties with itchy trigger fingers; knowing full-well that every missed shot, unnatural movement, or revealing glare from your scope gives you away. It’s tense. It’s fun. But it’s also a serious distraction and padding to your overall play time -- for better or for worse.

Recommended, if you enjoy Sniper Elite.

I decided to write a new review after I got a new laptop (Acer Nitro 5) which allows me to play the game with the highest settings. It's clear that the better visual details are not just eye candy but also improve the overall gameplay experience.
Also I now have played more than 100 hours of the game, so I felt I have new things to say about the game.

A disclaimer: I love the previous Sniper Elite 4 and I've played it a lot.

I was a bit annoyed in the beginning that Sniper Elite 5 changed a lot of things including most of the action keys for example. So you have to re-learn many things that you took for granted in SE4.
It took me quite a while to get used to SE5 because of these changes specifically.

Also, while the first mission is good, it's not a great mission to open the game with because it takes place at night and it adds an unnecessary level of difficulty when you're already struggling with so many new concepts in the game.
So if you find the first mission frustrating, don't lose hope ;)

It's clear they tried to make the game more grounded in reality, so for example you don't have an infinite number of satchel charges but instead you have to find each one in order to use it. Also you have to press a button to collect an item, not just bump into it. And you can't destroy every vehicle with a single shot except when they carry explosives. The enemies can activate alarms to call reinforcements which only makes sense. I like these changes.

It's also clear they put a lot of effort into improving the existing UI. 
For example, I love the larger permanent crosshair in the middle of the screen and now I really miss it when I go back to play SE4.

I have to say, the more I play SE5, the more I like it.
It takes a while to get used to the new game mechanics and the new action keys but I like them better.

Some people complained there's far less sniping in this game and much more stealth. I don't think so. It may seem so at first but as I was replaying the missions again and again, I discovered many opportunities for sniping when you take the time and explore the environment.

So overall, despite some initial frustration, I grew really fond of this game over time and now I love it.

A solid entry to the Sniper Elite franchise.  I don't think it's the best entry, if I had to choose only one to play, I would choose SE4.  But it's a Sniper Elite game, there's not a whole lot of variation or evolution here.  You're Karl, you are on a mission to destroy some Nazi super weapon, there is some shadowy Nazi pulling the strings and you must track him, put him down and stop his plans.  The game sticks to the formula and while it would be nice to see things evolve more, the formula is good so it's hard to fault it for that. 

Anyway, here's the things I liked and didn't like.

Liked:

*  Some of the environments in this game were really fun to explore.  I particularly enjoyed the bombed out ruins of the final level, which was full of lots of little perches and crawlsapces to snipe and slip away from... or get sniped by the enemy.  I really enjoyed Spy Academy and Guernsey as well.

*  The new weapon upgrade system is pretty nice.  I preferred the SE4 way of unlocking upgrades by completing challenges, but the amount of choice in this system is a clear improvement.

*  The inclusion of that AMD supersampling was a great addition.  It's no DLSS, which would have been better for me and my Nvidia card, but being able to play in 4K on High+ details at a fluid framerate with no noticeable loss in image quality was great.

Disliked:

* This game felt a lot more claustrophobic in parts than other entries in the series.  There were a few too many indoor spaces and not as many opportunities for extremely long range shots.

* Wind in this game is just bad compared to other games in the series.  It's mostly non-existent, and on the off chance you do have to adjust for it, it seems to only be on the extremely long range shots where it's bound to screw you up, especially since you're not practicing with it throughout the game since most of the time it's non-existent.  I played through hard difficulty and rarely used the breath holding mechanic because it was mostly unnecessary, as long as you're sighted in, it's very point and shoot.

*  This game feels less difficult than other entries in the series.  Enemies don't do as good of a job of tracking you, they don't feel any more difficult when they're on edge compared to passive, they don't hone in on the direction you're sniping from even if you drop a half a dozen of them all from the same direction as long as you're far enough away.  There was little need to use traps to cover my trail or aid my escape because they don't track for long enough and as long as you take a shot or two and then move you can happily pick off half of the Wehrmact with hardly any hassle at all.

Overall I give it a 7/10.  I liked SE4 better.  It's better than SE3, but not by much.
