Starting the review with Rebellion have absolutely knocked it out of the park for me with Sniper Elite 5 for me and if you want a short review, this game is a blast to play and a great addition to the SE franchise.

in-depth review for any of you interested, if you're new to the Sniper Elite games or a returning fan this game is a must buy for you and I want to start out with what I think are Sniper Elite 5's strongest features.

Top feature for me is the campaign maps as they are phenomenal to me with such a high standard for detail as it's not like they are just large, expansive maps that are full of just empty fields or void buildings as all of the maps have amazing structure to them and every map is very unique even down to the architecture of them as you go from very various settings that all are a breathe of fresh air and I didn't once think a maps designs were repetitive at all. They are very in-depth maps as each map can take you anywhere from 45 minutes or 2 hours to fully explore depending on your play style and how you approach them.

Second best feature for me is Axis Invasion, an optional feature that takes inspiration from the Dark Souls series where a German player can invade your campaign game and put even more pressure on you, or you can be the Axis Sniper and hunt down players in the campaign. It's an extremely refreshing idea and is very addictive on both sides and this is boosted by my previous comments on how good the maps are. If you are the Allied sniper and get invaded it pumps the adrenaline to 10 as you start staring at all the NPC axis guards to spot out the invading player. I really hope they expand on this feature more.

Third feature for me is the gun play in general, the customisation in guns and their variety while not a vast expansive list is still big enough to make you switch out and try different weapons. It gives you a reason to also explore the maps and try to find all the places to unlock said customisation. 

Some of the cons I will mention is while they maps are very good and expansive it can seem like you've become less of an Elite sniper and more of a stealthy infiltrator as it can feel like you're playing a Hitman game sneaking around tight areas and stealth executing or knocking them out but it does give a bit of variety rather than being able to sit from a high-point and take every enemy out. 

The story is also on the rocky side as the main protagonist "Karl" seems to be voice acted like he's a 80's action hero and the cutscenes can be a bit questionable at times but you bought this game to see rifle bullets go through skulls and crotches in X-ray vision so the Story can be a background feature.

I like the game. It is beautiful and the sniping is fun, but there are a lot of "buts"

* The game feels very arcadey, meaning it have tons of invisible walls, small rocks and hedges that you just cannot pass. It feels far less open world than SE4. You are very much stuck to one or two paths.

* The fluffing ladders from SE4 is still in. You just automatically grab a ladder when you don't want it and you can never climb one when you want to.

* Very often you have to stand up to pick something up and you frequently pick up things you don't want to pick up (at least you don't drop your stuff at random like in SE4).

* Even if you kill all the winesses in your vicinity the marker for "last seen location" is still on you and 15 new ai is coming your way. This makes it more of a combat-oriented shooter than a sneaky sniper game.

* Very often the notification that you are about to be discovered is never there. From nowhere you are just suddenly shot. It is also a lot harder to discover ai than SE4 (not necessarily bad) and the minimap is very imprecise  - sometimes it looks like ai is extremely close and then you realize they are far away.

* Some of the objectives are very unclear and the markers does not help.

* SE4 was a better game overall than SE5, but SE5 have very much content (you spend hours on each mission).

The campaign follows Karl Fairburne on a mission to hunt down and destroy the next Wunderwaffe of the Third Reich and its head, Abelard Moeller. The Wunderwaffe of this game is again based on a real German project, [spoiler] U-480, a Uboat coated with rubber to break apart soundwaves and evade SONAR detection [/spoiler]. Kill or incapacitate enemies and enjoy the gorgeous scenery in between.

The cons are minor but could be ironed out over the next few months. The main issue is a disappointing variety in weaponry. While the customisation definitely adds to the potential. it still requires mutliple run throughs of the campaign to find all the workbenches to unlock various elements to customise weapons. Another minor con is that the larger maps require much longer time to traverse and it's more than likely to spend 25% of a mission playtime just walking around to various objectives. Objectives always seem to be at opposite edges of the map, but c'est la vie. 
Aside from the minor cons listed above the game is an absolute pleasure to play, survival mode offers different operations to spice up the 3 available maps which go through different checkpoints.

For once I find myself in amazement at the Steam reviews for this. I bought it because I enjoyed SE4, and the reviews were mostly positive. Could not disagree more.

Note: This game needs a LOT of work, and Rebellion needs to seriously consider getting back to the basics and listening to their players. They always used to be responsive to player input and prompt with support tickets in SE3 & 4, now there are rampant reports of them being completely ignored.

This game is just not fun to play, and I'm on PC, while half the bugs are on console. Didn't even make it through the first level before I quit.

Karl pops out of cover for no reason. In a stealth sniping game.

Noise radius of rifles is grossly inaccurate. Got heard by enemies 300-400 meters away with a rifle rated for 96 meters.

Vehicles, especially gunboats, are now bullet sponges.

When trying to hide an enemy body, Karl strolls along like he *wants* to get spotted. Why would I hide a body and stand up straight as possible and make a huge *THUD* noise when hiding it?

Sound masks are few and far between and now must now be created purely through sabotaging equipment. As a result a common complaint is that their pistol and knife get used often when the rifle hasn't even left its sling.

SE4 basically eased you into the game, making gradually harder and harder missions. The first map is damn near impossible not to get spotted. Constant invisible walls often force you to walk on roads with frequent traffic if you want to get to the vantage point early. with absolutely nowhere to hide. Speaking of hiding, apparently the only place to do it is tall grass, which Karl repeats ad nauseum "this will be good to hide in" but crouching in a bush does absolutely nothing, if you can even walk through the bush.

"Play your way" is one of the first things said about this game, and it's less true than ever. It's no coincidence that all the featured images for this game are open combat or with a pistol/SMG in your hand except one. The game forces you into choke points, half the map is not usable, and generally makes trying to remain in stealth such a pain that the SMG comes out more often than your sniper rifle.

Apparently non-lethal takedowns of Nazis gives you more XP than lethal ones. In a war. That the Allies are desperately trying to put to an end. Against Nazis (I know not all of them are Nazis). The game takes it further by making a point to humanize the enemies much, much more than it did in the past with their backstories. If there is a game that should encourage taking out as many enemies as possible, this is it. This isn't Hitman where the ideal goal is to make it look like nothing ever happened and the only death is the target which happened by accident. It's to leave a silent trail of death in your wake without being seen.

Many other bugs reported such as getting stuck in walls, stuck in reload animations, guns getting stuck in the ground, bullet drops and travel that often have you aiming 4 inches away and below the enemy (on the first level). Zeroing your rifle isn't even mentioned unless you go looking for it.

TL;DR: I'd give this a 3/10. It's playable, the graphics are good, and they put some effort to make it not SE4 DLC, but not much, and it did more harm than good. I feel bad for the console players. If I was on console it would be a 2 at best.

This game is fun and I would recommend it to fans of previous Sniper Elite games and also to new players who are fans of games like Splinter Cell (and to some extent Hitman), as they have definitely changed things to be more appealing to a wider audience. 

While I understand why some people are saying it doesn't feel like a SE game, I would like to clarify that you have many opportunities to climb up to an elevated position and snipe from far distances if you choose, but there is now the option to essentially skip all sniping (except for the last mission) if you would like. I am glad they did this as it is obvious they want to bring in new fans rather than just catering to the core audience from the previous 3 games, which is great for the health of the series in the future. My only real complaint about the gameplay/missions is that there are essentially no "Snipe/Kill this Target" main objectives, although there are "Kill-List" optional targets in every mission so it doesn't bother me too much.

I do not understand what people are talking about when they say these maps are not as open/big as SE4. Yes, there are invisible walls/barriers that push you towards one of a few different entrances to certain objectives but it is never just "you must enter from this one point." There are always options on how to approach objectives/areas but I guess if you can't just walk to it from any direction that means it's now more linear (?). The maps are also very big and most have huge open areas with no invisible walls, but I guess having any wall that isnt a cliff like in SE4 is the issue.

Another big complaint I keep seeing is complaining about the invasions from players during your campaign. I don't really understand this as you can turn off invasions with no repercussions except that you can't gain the xp from killing invaders. In my opinion I am a big fan of the invasions as I find both hunting a player down as invader and hiding/ambushing the invader to be very fun.

The graphics are fine. I don't think they're exceptional or great in anyway but definitely a slight increase from SE4 and definitely not as awful and "dated" as I've seen some others complain about. 

I haven't played multi-player at all so can't comment, but I will admit that if there is no sniper-focused/sniper only playlist then they definitely need to change that. There is invasion but obviously the core fan-base comes back to these games for the sniping so not having a multi-player focused section for sniping would be a huge misstep by Rebellion.

My main complaints would be that I find the weapon options to be very limited and the plot is basically pointless. There are only 2 bolt-action snipers which is immensely disappointing (at least give me a mosin-nagant, I know Russia isn't close to France at this point but who cares) and there are only like 4 or 5 pistols/machine guns for secondaries. You can customize each individual weapon which I really enjoyed but that needs to be built upon further to be truly satisfying. As far as plot goes they just randomly toss in cutscenes of Nazi's complaining about Karl and saying "how can one man do this" alongside your "allies" giving you some intel on the next mission or complaining about something random before disappearing. Just stop with the plots at this point and go back to Karl doing narration between missions, no one would be upset. 

All in all I think this one is more fun than SE4 due to the replay-ability of invasions and being able to complete missions in different ways, but obviously fans of previous games looking for just sniping gameplay will be slightly dissapointed.

Played on release with my little brother, and honestly had some of the best fun I've ever had gaming. The levels are really well designed, interesting to explore, and the plot is engaging. The graphics are absolutely beautiful and the French countryside setting adds greatly with luscious flower fields, pristine castles, hanging gardens, war torn streets, and mysterious German bunkers to name a few. The customization and weapon variety is just enough to add an extra layer of depth to delve into, making you want to find all the parts and collectibles that you missed on earlier missions. The new axis invasion mechanic is also very stressful but rewarding forcing you into outsmarting other players. It adds a whole other element that completely changes how Sniper Elite is played, and invading other player's worlds is 10 times more satisfying with cosmetic unlocks as your progress. 

The survival system they added is also tons of fun having to face down hoards of enemies wielding MP40's to King Tiger Tanks. Each map is wildly different from the last and adds different challenges to defend a command post. The only drawback is that there are only 3 maps currently. The Multiplayer seems well thought out, but was not enough to draw me in, but provided some fun every now and then. 

All these things together this game is an absolute blast and honestly would get a 10/10 from me if it weren't for the bugs. There are several game breaking bugs in the Voice System, the party matching, and the axis invasion. Some have been patched, but many still persist. It's a shame that these tarnish an otherwise amazing game, however they are not nearly enough to push me completely away, because I'll always be back to shoot Nazi's in the balls.

[h2]Sniper Elite 5 Review[/h2]
	
[h2]Storyline[/h2]
I am pretty sure you would have realized that the Sniper Elite series are gameplay-heavy games. In Layman’s terms, the Sniper Elite series is known for the Genre-specific gameplay rather than the storylines. People play this game just to attain satisfaction from the kill cams or for the fun co-op experience they offer. 

There is a lot of redundancy in the storyline across the series. It usually involves infiltrating bases, taking out the higher-ups, and finally killing Adolf Hitler. The games’ plots are always something along these lines. So, if you’re looking for a proper unique storyline in this game, this isn’t meant for you. Let me sum up the entire plot in one line:

[code]Play again as Karl Fairburne in 1944 France as he fights to uncover a secret Nazi project called Project Kraken.[/code]

Yeah yeah, it’s the same ol’ plot. Karl is immortal or some ♥♥♥♥ & Hitler can apparently respawn. Alright, I’ll stop questioning the logic in this game’s story.

[h2]Gameplay Mechanics[/h2]
The gameplay part of the game is what made this series so popular. The kill cams and the gory after-effects of your shots are what the players find most appealing. Well, here are the multiple segments again:

[b][u]Core Gameplay[/u][/b]
The core gameplay remains the same. As I mentioned in the introduction, Sniper Elite has established a solid gameplay. It’s already challenging and fun. It is because of this that the developers are not trying to introduce any major differences whenever they release a new part. And the good thing is, people are barely complaining. 

So, each mission takes place in an open-worldish environment where you are given multiple objectives. Yeah, the objectives are very similar to the ones from the previous games; killing targets, destroying stuff, etc. The very generic shooter game objectives. What’s good is that you are given completely free reign on how you approach these tasks. There’s no laid path for you to follow to complete the missions. Since it’s an open-world setting, you get to choose your own approach; stealth or guns blazing. I prefer stealth since that’s how a sniper should actually take down their targets. At the same time, I take up the guns-blazing approach when I run thin on patience. 

You must be wondering how one would take a guns-blazing approach in a Sniper-focused game. Well, you have secondary weapons. These secondary weapons obviously have less ammo to discourage relying on them all the time. It’s best to use them when you’re in a pinch or want to take out someone in close range!

[b][u]So, What’s New?[/u][/b]
Apart from the usual upgrades to the already existing features, Rebellion apparently added a handful of new features to Sniper Elite 5. So, here is the list of the so-called new features:
[olist]
[*] [b]Improvements to the game’s campaign:[/b] They’ve taken references from real places and included them in the game now. Some assets used are the result of photogrammetry which gives them more detail since they are basically scans of real objects. You can now share ammunition and healing items with your co-op partner. 
[*] [b]Weapon customization and Map Traversal:[/b] Weapon customization has become a bit more detailed by allowing you to customize almost every part of the weapon. Traveling across the map has been enhanced a bit through the addition of slopes and ziplines which can come in handy in various situations.
[*] [b]Invasion Mode:[/b] This is an entirely new campaign-based PvP mode they introduced in this part. This allows randoms to invade your playthrough. Their main target is taking you out. This adds a bit more spice to your playthrough while making it a bit more challenging. 
[*] [b]An Enhanced Killcam:[/b] The Killcam in the Sniper Elite series has been one of the most vital features the game offers. They keep on making it better and better with every new release. So, it’s pretty obvious that they have made a lot of improvements to the kill cam in this game. It’s more graphic than ever!
[/olist]
[i]Source: [url=https://gamerant.com/sniper-elite-5-improvements-campaign-weapons-traversal/#:~:text=Sniper%20Elite%205%20will%20additionally,companion%20within%20co%2Doperative%20gameplay.]Gamerant Website on the Same Topic.[/url][/i]

So yeah, this is all the new stuff the game offers. Not a lot but the core gameplay is what would keep you hooked. And yes, I had to look up the stuff that was new in this game since they were not very obvious when I played the game. I hope the next part will have actual noticeable introductions.

[b][u]Difficulty Modes[/u][/b]
So, there’s a new difficulty mode in Sniper Elite V named “Civilian”. It’s now the easiest mode. The other difficulty modes are the same as they were in the previous parts:
[olist]
[*] [b]Civilian:[/b] As the name suggests, pretend that a civilian is given a Sniper Elite and is thrown into the battlefield. The civilian would now know how to fend for themselves. Hence, everything should be easy as ♥♥♥♥ in order for the civilian to have higher odds of surviving. That’s basically this mode, easy as ♥♥♥♥.
[*] [b]Cadet:[/b] This is the somewhat easy mode where weapon ballistic is omitted and the AI would have the IQ of a rock. 
[*] [b]Sharpshooter:[/b] Basically, a slightly harder difficulty mode where bullet drop is a thing. Enemies can now aim a bit better and can deal a bit more damage to you.
[*] [b]Sniper Elite:[/b] Oh my god! This difficulty mode is the name of the game! But it isn’t the hardest difficulty mode. This is where the actual sniper ballistics come into play. You have no assistance whatsoever. Everything becomes manual.
[*] [b]Authentic:[/b] The hardest mode the game has to offer. As the name states, this mode is as hard as real-life….apparently. It requires a lot of skill since enemies are as sharp as a knife and can deal a ♥♥♥♥ tonne of damage to you. Pretty sure they can one-shot you.
[/olist]

Apart from these, there’s obviously a custom difficulty mode where you can alter the difficulty of the different aspects of the game. These options not only make the game tailor-made for you but also add a lot to the replayability rate. 

[h2]Visuals & Audio[/h2]

The visuals have greatly improved when compared to its predecessor. Everything is way more detailed and polished right now. I love the new gorey and overly-detailed kill cam kills. It’s way more satisfying! The visuals are an easy 10/10! As for the audio part of the game, I am not really sure what to say since I didn’t pay that much attention to it. I was a bit too focused on the gameplay…

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*] The killcam still reigns supreme.
[*] You have complete freedom on how you want to approach a mission.
[*] The AI is challenging depending on your chosen difficulty mode.
[*] There’s quite a handful of difficulty modes to choose from which adds a bit to the game’s variety and replayability rate.
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*] The story is very dull and kinda repetitive since the previous games have a similar plot.
[*] The missions also feel repetitive.
[*] There are minor bugs but I am sure the developers will rectify them in the upcoming updates!
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Sniper Elite games always manage to fascinate me. I am a sucker for the kill cams and the authentic sniper mechanics. Yeah, the game is a bit too pricey. It is worth that price but I do recommend waiting for a sale. It’s very expensive since it might be considered a AAA Release. If you wait long enough, I am sure the game would go for a dirt-cheap price!

[b]Sniper Elite 5[/b] is the 5th installment in the Sniper Elite franchise [i](Not counting Zombie Army games)[/i] which improves a lot upon its predecessors with new mechanics, but also downgrades a little bit.

[b][u]Pros:[/u][/b]
- A lengthy campaign, which purely depends on the way you play, stealth, which is more fun and interesting, or all out loud which kills many possible little encounters you could find along the way
- Game looks absolutely gorgeous
- 1944 France setting
- I really love the fact that the swastikas and the rising sun flags are not censored, which really pumps up the whole immersion of the game.
- Story is straight forward, but still intriguing
- You can complete the whole game in co-op, and you can also get invaded which makes it harder for the invader to neutralize their targets
- Soundtrack further enhances the atmosphere on all maps
- Enemy AI is quite clever
- Multiple ways to approach objectives
- You can customize all your weapons to your preferred playstyle using the workbench with various attachments you can find during your playthrough by exploring the map and finding new workbenches.
- Kill List missions, which are essentially challenge missions that are fun additions.
- Invasion, which is what you expect, a random player can invade your campaign at any given time and his sole mission is to hunt you down.
- Player customization, not as deep, but still a really welcome feature
- Before you invade as Axis, you can customize your soldier to your liking and it also has a fun little progression system tied to kills. It's just plain fun, I wish more games did something like this.
- A really fun multiplayer component with game modes such as "No Cross", "Deathmatch" and "Team Deathmatch". Pretty straightforward, yet unique.
- Side missions
- Steam achievements
- Community Challenges
- Photo Mode [i][url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/TheBeggarSoldier/screenshots/?appid=1029690](Check out my screenshots)[/url][/i]

[b][u]Neutral:[/u][/b]
- Survival game mode, which is just a wave based game mode. It's neat, but not the main attraction.
- At first, the movement can feel janky, but you can easily get the hang of it.
- Just like with the movement, the new ADS mechanic introduced can feel a bit weird to use for the first few times.

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
- You can pick up enemy weapons, however, you cannot keep them. You can fire them at will, but when they are emptied or you change weapons, Karl drops it.

- It has some bugs

[b]9/10[/b] I really loved my time with this game and I will still hop in to play some invasion or multiplayer. Definitely worth it and I'm calling this [b]Game of The Year[/b] 2022 so far.

Out of every entry from 2 to present, I think this is my absolute favourite. Depending on what you enjoy about the franchise, this may or may not apply for you as well. 

I preferred playing this as a stealth game rather than a sniper game. In that sense, this entry is no doubt the best one yet. Nonlethal approaches are plentiful in ways that previous games lacked - nonlethal takedowns and bullet types are at your disposal and work great. There seems to be a lot of scrutiny towards the new bottle system which replaces the traditional throwing rock. But they are much more versatile - they can distract or even take out enemies, which is really handy. Yes, you have a limit on how many you can carry, but restocks are plenty and I never found I was lacking even as a stealth-heavy player. In past games you would be soft-punished as a nonlethal player. Even if you committed to it and snuck around enemies to progress, the lack of nonlethal takedowns meant you couldn't acquire letters or other collectables enemies keep on them. This problem isn't present in 5. 

This game sometimes gets described as a WW2-themed Metal Gear Solid V. I think it's fairly accurate. Again, nonlethal is encouraged. Maps are open-ended and have lots of enemy patrols you need to watch out for. Like MGSV, non-stealth combat is very enjoyable, so it doesn't feel like you're punished for going loud. Previous Sniper Elite games made combat with SMGs and pistols fairly unsatisfying: enemies felt unresponsive to fire and took way too many shots to kill from anything other than sniper rifles. The animations and time to kill in SE5 make using them a lot more fun, and viable as a playstyle. Each mission ends with a chart showing your performance according to Stealth/Assault, and then Lethal/Nonlethal. It's a small detail, but I felt like it did a great job at presenting other playstyles as legitimate. 

Weapon customisation was something I was sceptical about, but I think it was implemented perfectly. There are lots of options that don't compromise the WW2 look and feel, which is great for me since I personally don't like the more extravagant customisation you see in games like COD: Vanguard (though there are definitely options for that, if that's your thing). What really won me over is the ability to remove the scope on rifles, since I've always preferred the look of a plain rifle with irons. Also great is the option to mount a functional bayonet, making assault/melee playstyles even more fun. Having to acquire these attachments through finding workbenches also gives a fantastic incentive to explore each level more thoroughly than I might have otherwise.

Sniper Elite 5 brings some interesting ideas to the table, but ultimately feels like a downgrade for the series. A lot of the ideas felt like the developers played Hitman and thought, "Hey, that'd be neat!" There's different starting locations, limited climbing mechanics, and the targets have patterns and 'kill methods' like the new Hitman games. 

The problem is, a lot of these features don't feel very polished. The starting locations are unlocked only if you stumble upon them across the map, you can only climb a very limited amount of walls and surfaces, and the targets usually bug out and prevent their special 'kill method' from being used.

Speaking of the bugs, there are a lot of bugs in this game. I've had targets spawn below ground, instances where enemies across the entire map are alerted after a steath event that was unrelated, enemies stuck in walls, and more. I know the developers are working on fixing these issues, but it's a huge issue when you're playing a level and have to restart because targets or events just don't trigger. There are also big optimization issues. Any level with rain tanks my FPS.

Another new feature is the invasion mechanic. Basically it's like Dark Souls or Deathloop, where someone can invade your game or you can invade theirs. I actually really like it (but you can turn it off if you don't). However, the time between invasions needs to be drastically increased. Getting 3+ invasions per level is tiring, since they all pretty much function the same way. 

My final note is on the soundtrack, setting, and level design. I felt like the soundtrack for SE4 was far superior than this game. This game has no recognizable theme, and the soundtrack didn't really stand out to me. I also wasn't as keen on the setting as I was for 4. It could be because just about every WW2 game is set in France, but I found it stale and overused. There wasn't much variety in the locations either, but most of them looked the same. Level design wise, a lot of levels felt very linear and there were very limited approaches for many locations. It's just arbitrary barriers too, like certain fences you can't climb over, or hills you can't go up. That makes it all the more annoying.

Overall, it was still an enjoyable time, especially doing coop. In any future games though, I hope they refine these mechanics to be more polished and workable. I think they have great potential, but in their current state they can cause more issues than enjoyment.

Well, I don't know quite what some negative reviewers have been playing, but this is by far the best of the Sniper Elite games to date by a country mile.  Don't be put off at the start - the first ten, fifteen minutes of the first mission seem rather restrictive in where you can actually go to achieve the set goals, but after that, freedom to move around a vast world gets somewhat better.  
This world in Sniper Elite 5 is simply beautiful.  Campaign Italy in Sniper Elite 4 was good, but this is even better.  The detail is simply incredible - a huge variety of scenic battlegrounds combined with close quarter town elements provide a breathtaking experience.  It is simply beautiful.
Game play is far more challenging.  It takes a few missions to develop a style of play that you find works.  There are multi objectives in each of the main missions bar the very last one whcih is a bit of an add-on compared to the other missions.  There are far more enemies around - you simply cannot go in guns blazing with a hope of blasting everyone in sight and surviving.  Strategy is needed - a space to bail out to if things get tough - and boy are things easier if alarms are not triggered.  Added to that - weapon tactics are much more realistic in this game.  In SE4, you could pick up a weapon, keep it, and add copious amounts of ammo to it as you progressed each mission.  Here, you pick up a weapon, and can only use the ammo left in it before either going back to your own weapon, or finding another similar weapon to use.  Far more challenging and realistic.
The sniping element has changed the least in my view.  Depending on what level of difficulty you play, the sniping mechanics are pure Snipe Elite as it always has been.  Unlike Ghost Warrior Contracts, sniping distances are not that extreme.  However, the cut scenes are pretty brutal and weapon sounds are a huge step forward.
Afraid the voice acting is just as bad as it ever was, but there we go....you won't be buying this game for the cut scenes which are still somewhat predicable and hackneyed.  
I like to play each level to the full - if you want to, you can take a good two hours game play for each of the major levels in this game.  And each mission has such wonderfully created environments.  Most compelling and enjoyable.
Tanks and vehicles are more difficult to destroy - this is one part of the game play thatis nothing like previous SE episodes.  You will need Panzershreks or armour piercing weaponry and ammunition to destroy tanks and such like in SE5.  Much more of a challenge than sniping gunners and drivers as experienced in SE4.
There aren't many games that I'd justify not waiting for a sale price - this is one of them.  Buy it.  It is a load better than SE4 and that is saying something.
At the time of writing, there are two major issues that need sorting - one is the lack of zoom functionality on the middle mouse when in sniping mode.  It's designed to work, but doesn't for me.  Secondly, the zip wire bizz has a bad habit of freezing up which stalls the game play badly.  Save before zip wiring, and it's ok.

It's that solid 7/10 action game; nothing is quite as interactive as an immersive sim, or as freewheeling as an open world. Sometimes it can feel confining or arbitrary - why do I have to walk 200m down a shin-high stone wall to enter a field, or only climb perfectly things with perfectly flat edges? The flip side of that is that it gives Rebellion a chance to control the experience, to funnel you this way or that, and give you the limited-yet-fun options they've dictated for a given encounter.

There's solid, satisfying action here, and once it starts to click, the limitations are liberating, unlike what I find can happen in open worlds or even immersive sims where I'm always wondering if I "played it wrong." Though there's lots of weapon variety, relatively lean set of overall options - loud, quiet, distant, close, traps - make what's there gratifying. 

A little more disappointing is some general jankiness - world objects that are extremely particular about where you are in space to interact with them, enemies that get stuck in alert-investigating-cancelled-alert loops. This last is especially bothersome because despite a huge, rich set of accesibility and difficulty controls, the HUD options are terribly limited. You get quest markers and enemy tagging and status updates (alert, investigating, etc) and tool tips and etc etc or you get nothing - no option just to have, say, a few essentials on the screen and leave the rest of it up to the thrill of the hunt. I might remember wrongly but I'm pretty sure that this is a regression from SE4. 

The menus are also a terrible modern design paradigm where everything is tiles, and there's no simple way to just resume your campaign. It's not a touch interface; I don't need 5cm x 5cm block of screen to resume my campaign. 

I wish it leaned more into the eponymous sniping - it's so rewarding, especially as you dial down assists. This game seems less confident than SE4, though, and does have habit of clearly blocking lines of sight, or tucking enemies into places that you can't engage except at close range. Speaking of things to lean *out* of, Carl talks too much and this game doesn't need (or at least do well with) the cutscenes, in writing or execution. If you want soulful Nazi-hunting, go play the new Wolfensteins. SE5 I think has aspirations but can't meet them.

It's all still worth it though, and so refreshing that, even if a bit less confident than the one before, is still proudly what it is; a schlocky, shooty power fantasy that is fun to play. Turning off all the assists, sitting 800m out from a target and nailing that shot is something that no other game does or has replicated.

Edit 26 July to add: Rebellion has implemented the Shooting Range feature, which is so so helpful to learn to place your shots. Glad to have it back for SE5, thanks Rebellion!

Overall a really fun game, and a worthy addition to the Sniper Elite franchise. Unfortunately I ran into several bugs while playing, and I had a few frustrating experiences with invisible walls and barriers, etc. But they have been working on patching them.

The overall level concepts and designs were really fun. The WW2 France setting was done really well, it reminded me a lot of old Medal of Honor and Call of Duty Games set in France. It had everything from rural farmsteads to ruined cities to fortified beaches., And in my opinion level 3 was particularly great.

The levels are more linear than Sniper Elite 4, and featured a lot more close quarters situations. This lead to less sniping and long distance sniping opportunities, and having to rely more on stealth and traps. But nevertheless I enjoyed it and had fun infiltrating Nazi bases by using distractions, traps, and stealth.

The story was a pretty standard Sniper Elite story. The Nazi's are working on a super weapon project, and you must find out what it is and destroy it. Nothing special but not terrible either, but I found myself invested at least.

There are also new game modes, such as Axis invasions, where you can invade someones campaign, or have your campaign invaded by a counter sniper. It can be turned on and off optionally, but not using it gets you less XP, and it's also required to unlock single player items (like guns and cosmetics) which I didn't care for. But overall the mode is fun.

There's also Survival Mode where you can survive against waves of AI invaders, single player and Co-op. There's also Co-op in the campaign mode, and regular multiplayer battles.

So overall it's not my favorite Sniper Elite games, and it's not perfect, but nevertheless I had fun playing it and I feel like I got my money's worth. I would give it a 7.5/10 and recommend it (after they release more patches if you can wait, but it's still fun right now)

Summary: If you like Sniper Elite, there's plenty here to enjoy.  There are some curious choices that bring it down for the singleplayer campaign compared to SE4, which remains the pinnacle of the series.


The Meat:

Karl's starting to show some grey in SE5, but it certainly isn't slowing him down.  The tried-and-true stealth/action gameplay of the Sniper Elite series is alive and well, letting you ghost your way through tense situations, be an angel of silent death from close quarters or far, or even Rambo your way across a map with as much explosive, frantic carnage as you feel like, dealing out a veritable feast of bullets, bombs, and grenades.  The gunplay is more of the sweet, sweet gravy the series is known for, with the famous slow-mo x-ray kill cam displaying what high-impact ballistic projectiles can do to Nazi innards to your heart's content.  Now even frequently applying to closer-combat weapons as well as the titular sniper rifles.

The setting of France brings some beautiful vistas, winding cities, rolling plains, and grungy factory towns.  All now very French!  Mission 3 of note is a perfect diorama of everything SE is built for, a stunningly gorgeous fortress of an immense castle-like church and its surrounding walled-in town of very tight, winding streets, all jutting out from the broad, sandy coastline and ocean waves.  All of it explorable and full of enemies and things to find.  There is also the obligatory "kill Hitler" mission with plenty of options and amusing cutscenes of the deed being done with every avenue.

The story continues the trend of recent SE games of being "stop the secret Nazi wonder-weapon!", which is very fine by me.  There are a smattering of NPC's to liven up the place, though their inclusion is light set-dressing at best.  The focus remains on Karl and his one-man war on . . . the war.  The main villain is a bit lackluster and doesn't come across as vicious and evil as one would hope, merely wanting to see his project through and getting mildly annoyed when things go wrong and it throws off his timetables.  There are plenty of minor villains that are plenty evil and fun to take out, however.

In addition to the regular singleplayer and co-op campaign, there is a survival mode against waves of enemies, and a new "invasion" mode, wherein another player can drop into your game at random as an Axis opponent whose sole task is hunting you down.  Additional start-points and some risk/reward mechanics around scouting out where this assassin is in return for making yourself more findable give enough of a balance to make this tense rather than a forced nuisance.  It can be entirely turned off, thankfully, if you don't want to deal with that noise.


The Potatoes:

Weapon customization reaches new heights, with a variety of unlockable weapons and parts for your rifles, pistols, and secondary weapons slots.  Lots of options here and it's as fun visually as it is in stats, though I found myself leaning toward specific features that had me using the same weapons throughout most of the game.  Tweaking them with new bits was still enjoyable, though.

The first part I found as odd was the new focus on non-lethal options.  Up to now, SE has been entirely about mass death or avoidance, but now gives you the option of knocking your enemies out for the duration of the mission unless someone rouses them.  In play it doesn't feel very different aside from that minor risk of your targets being shook awake again, but it does add a touch of personal choices of morality, as you can now decide if you want to empty a soldier's skull or just choke them out and dump them in a box to wake up later next to their dead commander and have some lasting trauma.  It's also a bit of a reach that wooden bullets fired from a sniper rifle count as "nonlethal", but . . . game-magic!

This inclusion of this nonlethal approach, as well as the new invasion mechanic, has resulted in the loss of some of the fun items from prior entries in the series.  No longer do you have tripwire mines or S-mines for personnel elimination.  Now there's just the teller mine for all purposes, and a new nonlethal mine that can often just kill enemies anyway (at least for me).  The loss of the tripwires is especially rough, I really liked those, but it's understandable in light of players being able to cheese them against an invading player.

As a minor sidenote, it feels like there was a lot less trucks with exposed fuel tanks to explode, nor did I see viewports in tanks and armored vehicles in order to bullseye the driver or gunner.  It's probably by design, to make the player use armor-piercing ammo and use customization to boost the penetration power, but it felt a lot less fun, even if it is more realistic.

Soundwise, I found SE5 a downgrade as well.  The weapons and explosions are still fine, but the music is kind of . . . bland, now.  The rousing, dramatic title theme of SE4 has given way to a quieter, tepid score that felt a pale imitation.  The music bumpers during loading screens has gone from suspenseful mandolin plucking to bland.  The stinger when you find or complete a task has gone from dramatic woodwinds to bland.  The genuinely-frightening scratch of strings from being spotted by an enemy sniper has gone to bland.  I genuinely found it all quite lacking compared to SE4.

We've also lost a lot of the pre-mission interactivity with the characters involved, where you can have personal conversations and learn more of the background story.  Now it's mainly just brief wraparound cutscenes, and if NPC's are around at all when you start a mission, you or they just piss off without much in the way of hello or goodbye.


Verdict:

Plenty enjoyable, and as a ginormous fan of SE4 (I may just go play it again now), I found SE5 to be a good time.  It just doesn't reach the same heights to me, and some of the new additions like the invasion mode don't interest me at all.  I'm sure it spices things up for those who are into it, though, so YMMV.  Nonlethal is fine, and I did find myself using it for some variety, but it doesn't make or break the game.  It was a good time, but I still prefer SE4.

Courtesy of the folks at developer and publisher Rebellion, I’ve been taking a look through Sniper Elite 5. The latest in a long-running franchise, I’ve been exceptionally excited about this one, having thoroughly enjoyed all of the Sniper Elite titles since V2 released back in 2012. As usual, you can find a full video review (and a nicely formatted version of this written review) at https://www.pixelbandits.org/2022/05/review-sniper-elite-5/

[h1]The Basics[/h1]

In this the fifth instalment into the Sniper Elite franchise, we return once again to take control of our hero Karl Fairburn. Initially dropped behind enemy lines to weaken the Nazi “Atlantikwall” fortifications, the mission soon goes awry (there’s a surprise). Meeting up with the local French resistance, you’ll undercover the Nazis’ secretive Operation Kraken. Kraken leads players on an adventure through nine expansive locations, allowing you to choose your own playstyle and tactics.

Sniper Elite 5 doesn’t only look to extend the franchise by adding new story, and there are a number of welcome new features in this iteration of the title. To start with, a number of the locations in game have been captured using photogrammetry, allowing Rebellion to base levels on real-world locations, accurate to historical photography. This has made the various locations feel expansive and immersive, as well as providing a variety of ways to approach each target.

Players can also traverse these locations much more freely within Sniper Elite 5. New mechanics include the ability to utilise zip lines, handy for escaping a compromised sniper’s nest or bell tower. In addition, players can now shippy along ledges as well as climb trailing vines. These new abilities work together to allow much more freedom in how you approach each level.

Photogrammetry has provided some exceptionally immersive levels
The new Invasion game mode is one of my favourite new features. This new mode places you as a specialist German sniper, and allows you to invade the campaign missions of other players. Similar to Dark Souls invasions, Sniper Elite allows you to turn this feature on or off within your campaign gameplay. Invasion provides a great opportunity for stealthy and tactical one-on-one multiplayer, and as the German sniper you’ll work alongside NPC characters to track and eliminate the player’s Karl Fairburn as they attempt to complete the mission.

Players can also now team up with a friend in two-player co-op through the whole campaign. In addition to further multiplayer modes including cooperative survival and adversarial PvP matches, there’s a lot of multiplayer to get stuck onto in this new addition into the Sniper Elite franchise.

Within the campaign, players are also able to customise rifles, SMGs and pistols using workbenches hidden within each level. Finding these workbenches (three within each location) will allow players to unlock and swap out various stocks, barrels, sights and more, to customise their experience. Each new unlock brings pros and cons, and you’ll have to spend a little time looking over each in order to build your perfect weapon.


[h1]Parent’s Guide[/h1]
[b]Rating: Adult Only[/b]

Sniper Elite 5 is rated by PEGI at 16 and above and by the ESRB as a Mature 17+. Sniper Elite brings back the well-loved kill-cam, which now also extends to knife, SMG and pistol kills as well. Each shot in Sniper Elite can now bring this in-depth view, with new mechanics meaning that bullets will rip and tear in more detail. There’s also language to consider as well as many online modes, and overall we’re saying this one is for Adults Only, from around the age range suggested by the PEGI and ESRB warnings.

[h1]Accessibility[/h1]
[b]Rating: Low Barrier[/b]

In terms of accessibility, Sniper Elite 5 has a decent number of difficulty options, and while the levels are expansive it’s still relatively easy to drop in and out. It’s still not the easiest in terms of aiming, but good hints and guides do make it relatively accessible.


[h1]The Run Down[/h1]

[b]Visuals – Good:[/b][i] I’ve been playing through Sniper Elite 5 on both PC and Xbox Series X. In both cases the visuals for environments are pretty great, and each level provides a realistic battle ground, often modelled on real-world locations. Character models could do with a little polish here and there on all platforms, which is especially noticeable during cutscenes. Overall, while the close-up views of characters’ faces leaves a little to be desired, things do work well, and the new kill-cam mechanics are definitely worth a look if you’re a fan of the more gory side of Sniper Elite.[/i]

[b]Audio – Outstanding:[/b][i] Sniper Elite 5 brings the usual fantastic musical score and I need it to be made available on Spotify as soon as possible. The voice acting holds up well in cutscenes and also works nicely in game to give you a steer and potential clues as to what’s happening. The weapon effects are well executed, and the sounds for Sniper Elite’s close-up kill cam are suitably nasty.[/i]

[b]Narrative – Outstanding: [/b][i]The franchise has a history of solid narratives and Sniper Elite 5 is no different. I have really enjoyed the story within this one, and as well as having it front and centre within cutscenes and missions briefings, there’s a fair amount to discover in collectables as well.[/i]

[b]Replay – Outstanding:[/b] [i]Sniper Elite 5 really shines when it comes to replay value. Even played alone, the solo campaign covers roughly 20 hours, or a little more if you’re anything like me. Added to this the various multiplayer modes, and this one has significant value. The availability of co-op gameplay throughout the whole campaign is very welcome, as is the new Invasion mode which will tickle anybody who enjoys trying to screw over other (consenting) players. Survival and adversarial multiplayer on top of this, as well as a significant number of collectables on each level, means that there’s always something to come back for.[/i]

[h1]The Verdict[/h1]

Pixel Bandits [b]Achtung Headshot Level for Sniper Elite 5 is an Outstanding 4/4[/b]. Sniper Elite has been a long-term love of mine for around ten or so years, and it’s great to see it improving over time. The new story is excellent and in truth I would probably have enjoyed Sniper Elite even without the new features. The pistol, SMG and knife killcam provides a nice little touch, and the locations brought to life with photogrammetry have been exceptionally immersive. I’m awful at it, but the new Invasion mode (where I’ve been killed by the player far more times than I’ve managed to stop their mission) has been a genuinely enjoyable PvP experience as well.

The new mechanics to allow you to zip, shimmy, slide and climb your way through the nine expansive levels is also very welcome and (potentially due primarily to this) I’ve felt much more free in this iteration of the franchise, and able to approach levels as I like. If you’re a fan of the previous titles, Sniper Elite 5 brings enough of the old to keep it familiar, while adding enough new to give fans a reason to go out and grab this one as soon as possible.

Sniper Elite 4 was an overall wonderful game. The maps had dozens of spots where you can set up a sound mask to conceal your shots, grab some cover and wait for the perfect shot. Despite not being an open world game the maps felt large and full enough to give you a lot of freedom. 

When I read that Rebellion was bring open world to Sniper Elite 5 I thought this might just be the master piece game of the Sniper Elite series. Instead this open world game is somehow more closed off than it's non-open world counterparts. There are only 1-2 to paths you can take just like in 4. However, they offer much more limited opportunities for sniping. In 4 Rebellion would set up sniper nets with sound masking, long field of views, and multiple enemies visible that could be spotted if you were patient. In short, they encouraged you to play like a sniper move quietly and slowly to a good vantage point. Observe the enemy, conceal your shots, and wait patiently for the perfect shot. 

In 5 Rebellion will either give you cover or a sound masker almost never both and never a place that offers a good view of multiple enemies at a time with sound masking and cover. Instead, you will be funneled into trenches and buildings where enemies are too far for CQC but in perfect pistol range. Rebellion has replaced the Welrod pistol of the previous games with an overpowered 1911 equipped with a modern style suppressor. The pistol is way overpowered and in the cramped quarters of Sniper Elite 5 is way more useful than the rifle. 

If you try to play as a sniper and not a pistol toting cowboy the game will become much more difficult. Since the sound masked locations really only give a god view of one or two enemies and little cover you will find yourself taking one shot and running away quickly. Many enemies can’t even be seen from logical sniping locations. So you’ll be forced to fire one shot which will be detected by enemies and runaway from all the return fire. You’ll soon give up on snipping for most of the game as it becomes an exercise in frustration brought on by poor level design. 

If you are a Sniper Elite fan this game is an easy miss. I wish I missed it and I am sad that I missed the return window hoping that his game would get better. Rest assured it does not.

Played this one fresh after playing through 4 again. This game overall was an improvement on the series and I hope they can find additional stories to tell in the future. As for the unique differences compared to the previous, here's what I've noticed:
- Virtually no more grenade kills? Idk if they removed them or the chance of hitting one but I still haven't been able to snipe a grenade on somebody, which I did frequently (maybe too so) in 4
- Vehicle combat is very different now. This actually is one of my few real complaints with the game; they went from a system of being able to snipe out gunners and snipers to "blow up the back and then shoot the engine a bunch." At first I was actually wasting resources because I didn't realize once the engine is exposed you just have to shoot it repeatedly until *kaboom*. 
- Much more linear maps overall, compared to Italy you're generally more restricted in this game. More walls you van't vault, more gray areas on your minimap. This coupled with sometimes vague mission instructions left me running back an forth across the several lanes of map to find my objective. (Don't call destroying a radio "neutralizing defenses", it's misleading at best. 
- Much better "quiet" options in the loadouts. While we don't have really more options than previous games, they've made suppressors more accessible and subsonic ammo a great option on all guns. I really have a wide range of configurations to decide on how loud I want to be. For 4 I actually purchased a DLC just to get the suppressed pistol in it (only quiet option base game is the Welrod) while in this game basically all pistols can. 
- Slow-motion controls are kinda neat if you really wanna get cinematic with your shots. I only wish the slow motion focused more on bullet entry/cavitation and less on after the bullet has passed through, but that's nitpicking. 
- I'm too much of a ♥♥♥♥♥ to do Axis invasion, because I hate pvp in most games, but I'll happily join an easy coop. This is something made easy to use and though connections are tenuous at times it can be a fresh change to play a map through with someone. 

Overall recommending to anyone who's enjoyed the previous games, any sniper games, or some Nazi-smashing therapy.

I read the reviews before getting this game and I was a little skeptical but I risked it and let me tell you : BEST DECISION EVER! Personally, I bought every Sniper Elite game since the SE V2. I played all of them for like 3-4 hours so I thought this is just one more for the collection and it will sit in my inventory never to be played. This one hits different though. This is going to be a longer review but I wanted to clear things for people who are skeptical like I first was.

How I play the game:
-I play at sharpshooter (medium) difficulty for everything except the sniping which I play at the hardest difficulty Authentic.
-I NEVER engage in combat and play every mission undetected. It takes me approximately 150-200 minutes per mission (usually 90-100% completion for collectibles).
-Sometimes I take 10 minutes just to do recon and learn NPC's paths from a distance before deciding my next move. Also, I ALWAYS hide the bodies or throw them out of sight when possible as to avoid suspicion.
-Sometimes I stay in a corner encircled by NPC's for several minutes just waiting for an opening. I also make use of ALL of the available equipment (70% is bottles/whistle/sticky grenades). 
-If they find a body or I create an explosion and they start investigating I simply plan ahead where to hide and wait it out.
-I really try to stick to the games script and play it as if it was real. Sometimes I even reload a situation if I don't like the outcome or it comes off too unrealistic. 

With that being said, nothing is stopping me to try and snipe everyone or run and gun in with my smg... But I just find it so much more satisfying when your have to work for every kill. Also that way, the x-ray cam when you finally have the opportunity for a long shot never gets old!

LOADOUT:
-Springfield M.1903 with attachments that maximize long range shooting (reduce bullet drop and add power). I also use the silencer that doesn't affect bullet drop (gun is audible from 87m).
-The rest doesn't really matter lol. But I usually use a silenced pistol and silenced smg.

1st negative point I saw in the reviews: You have to play online to unlock certain things:
-The only things that you unlock through multiplayer are a couple of COSMETIC skins for the guns and some character skins that you can play in the main story instead of Karl.
-Every other gun/attachment that actually changes the gameplay is unlocked while playing the story.

2nd negative point I saw in the reviews: You get less xp when you turn off Invasion mechanic for you campaign. This is true, however:
-The skill tree is like 70% useless in my opinion so xp is really not that important as it is only used to unlock perks.
-When you thoroughly complete each mission, you get more than enough xp to max out the  different skill trees without needing to enable Invasions.
-I am currently on mission 6 and need 2-3 more skill points to max out my skill tree.
-To give you an example, I've only lost like 3 health bars total in all of my 6 missions so far.
-Once I complete the campaign I will try out the Invasion mode to have a change of pace and work towards 100% completion but is really not required to fully enjoy the story and all of the weapons, attachments, etc the game has to offer.

3rd negative point I saw in the reviews: There is not enough sniping from huge distances going on. Instead, game is focused on stealth and sneaking around with pistol.
-Personally I get somewhere between 10-15 long shots (100m-450m), 15-20 short range pistol kills (10m-40m) and like 20-30 takedowns. Tip: when you perform takedowns try to pacify them as it gives you considerably more xp at the end of the mission. 
-Here is the difficult thing : You REALLY have to plan your approach. Sometimes I don't take the cool long shot x-ray cam even though it kills me inside because I know it will screw my whole stealth set up.
-The 3rd mission offers a ton of great opportunities for like 300m-500m shots in the beginning before you start approaching the castle. Just use your binoculars to scout around.

4th negative point I saw in the reviews: There are bugs and you often get stuck on like small ledges.
-Yes you do get stuck on some stupid small rubble sometimes but you just go around it or find another path because the game doesn't want you to go through there. Didn't really affect my gameplay at all.
-There are some bugs that I saw like enemies getting stuck in object or walls. Nothing that prevents you to complete the game properly tho.
-WARNING: In mission 4 (war factory) it took me an hour to complete the kill list target with the special objective (using the rat bomb to kill him). This was the only really annoying bug so far.

I really hope this helps you have a better idea of what to expect from this game! I hope you get to enjoy it as much as I do! :)

Sniper Elite is a game franchise that manages to refine itself on every iteration.

2 was linear, but had some nice setpieces, gore, and a focus on sniping, which let it stand out from other WW2 shooters.
3 added bigger maps with different routes between points of interest.
4 had open map design, lots of interesting architecture, and was fun co-op.
5 seems to be a culmination of the previous game's improvements.

Maps are open ended and dense with enemies and terrain. The freedom to move around also means that close combat and melee takedowns are viable and useful. The gore is pleasant as always. There is meaningful gun customization that changes rifles, smgs, and pistols functionally and aesthetically. Coop is back, though I can't speak on its systems without having played it. The new invasions are extremely fun.

Allowing invasions in the campaign game gives extra XP. I played the base campaign solo, and by the last level I had plenty of XP to upgrade all the skills. The game seems balanced around solo XP gain. XP gained by allowing invasions is extra. Unfortunately, many people seem to allow invasions to allow the additional XP gain, but disconnect the moment someone invades. When attempting to invade, maybe 1/2 or 2/3 of players d/c immediately or soon after. Of those who remained, there was a lot of fun to be had. The mechanics support an enjoyable invasion system. Tracking enemy players by gunshots, tagging ally AI to better predict player movement, seeing what objectives are already destroyed on spawn, planting bombs and traps, makes for an exciting and tense game of cat and mouse.

Overall, pretty fun game to wander around and murder in.

I have honestly been waiting for years for this game. I played through (and re-played through) SE3 and SE4 so much, they were my go-to games when nothing else held my interest. They will STILL be my go-to games over this one. 

What SE5 got right: 
- Moddable/swappable parts for guns
- updated held-breath mechanic
- Removing the "always know where an enemy is" bits. I feel the new wide-circle system makes the engagements far more entertaining and challenging
- Crowbar, Bolt-Cutters, Satchel Charges needing to be found in order to be used. This opens the player up to a multitude of different playthrough options per engagement

What SE5 got wrong:
- Simple mechanics. There are SO many ledges under 3ft in this game that cannot be vaulted/mantled where in SE3 or SE4 you could pretty much climb almost everything, OR the game map was built in a way where the only ledges you encounter WERE climbable. 
- Sniper Posts, or lack-there-of. Finding a good spot to snipe from, with or without noise blocking, was an awesome thing in all SE games until now. It feels more like they focused on the objectives rather than the actual gameplay when the gameplay is what made these games fun
- Map Size/Intricacy? Maybe its just me but I truly feel that these maps are smaller than ones in previous games and don't allow for much fun in setting up a sniping position, grouping enemies together, etc. I felt like I was just constantly moving from one objective to the next which really makes this feel more like a combat game than a sniper game. I ended up using my pistol more than any other weapon, nearly twice as much as my actual sniper rifle.... in a sniper game... because of the constant movement. 
- Time. In SE4 I had the option to race through everything, guns out going loud and insane and finishing in under 20 min. OR I could take my time, scope everything out, snipe everything that crossed my path and move on quietly, utilizing the entire environment, taking an hour or so to get through each level. In SE5 it feels like I'm rushed to get through everything. 
- Silly challenges for weapon parts or weapons. need I say more? Just make them available once you reach a certain gun table or find them within the level.

Possible solutions for SE6 (if it happens):
- Start with simple game mechanics. Copy a game like Assassin's Creed where you can climb all walls, you can jump off things onto soft areas, you can hide, you can sneak around. Take those game mechanics and slap the better features of this game on top of it
- More selection in gun modding. I loved what you brought to SE5, however if I look at other games with similar capability, ones like Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon: Wildlands takes the cake when it comes to modding your guns. The differences in available scopes or magazines made a huge difference to how you would play any given situation. Also add to that the fact that you needed to find them. I did enjoy a good portion of that with the gun tables in SE5 but it still felt lacking.
- DLC Weapon options. I won't deny, once I've played the game through with the base available options, I like to splurge and buy the super silent weapons or the super loud weapons and see what trouble I can get into with those. That makes the game fun. There simply aren't any of those with this game.


Final words: Will I play this again? maybe. At this point its not likely but who knows. Its a possibility. Would I recommend it to others? if it comes out discounted or free, go for it. Its an ok game, but not one I would spend full price on again.

The game is however full of bugs, from menus, to loading in, to playing the game. Rough edges, literally between aliasing and context grabbing, are easy to find and will occasionally frustrate.

There's an interactable chain that drops the chandelier. If you use interact, you will fail the Kill Challenge. You instead have to shoot the chain. As the fifth big installment of the Sniper Elite Series, this game does not contain many surprises. As every Sniper Elite has a bit of an identity crisis, this one is no different. The gameplay of Sniper Elite 5 is probably the most hybrid third person shooter gameplay of the whole series. The sniper rifle is still a trusted tool (also the only weapon with optional aim assist) but submachine gun and pistol work almost equally well - and I like that. I like variety in my shooter gameplay and this game gives me enough choices to fill that want. 

The levels of the campaign are beautifully crafted and offer very different combat arenas/sandboxes/sneaking challenges. I've read the critique that many maps don't offer that long shooting distances as in previous installments and while that is certainly true, I don't think it takes away much. You're still able to fight at ranges of 100-200 meters very often and it isnt like you would hit much beyond that without the aim assist. The story is nothing to write home about but that is also not the point of the game. It is written well enough to justify the mission sandboxes you're getting dropped into and for me that is very much sufficient. 

Also, the invasion mode: Before buying the game, I apparently dodged all the announcements about this gamemode and was pleasantly surprised upon discovering it. In this gamemode, you can join the campaign games of other players. You play as an enemy sniper and have to stop the other player. A simple concept that makes each mission way more thrilling for me. I absolutely love getting invaded in a mission and suddenly having to adapt to the new circumstances, because NOW I am facing not only the AI but also a human player that can do almost everything I can do - and can also kill me in one shot. It is really something else and even if you get killed by an invader, you don't really lose progress. You can still save. 

And you can turn it off. You can turn the invasion mode completely off and be done with it. I don't get the negative reviews where the major critique is this gamemode. Just turn it off. You can also kick an invading player from your game session since you are the host (yes, really. I also don't get why you can do this).

Definitely a nice game.
It's in a far more finished state than most games that were released in the past few years.

[b] Pro: [/b]
Each mission gives you plenty of options for many different approaches. It's a lot of fun to find all the secrets that are hidden on each map.

It's a lot of fun to customize your weapons to optimize your sniper for the longest shots while being relatively quiet.

Sniper Elite 5 takes the battle of the Axis to the Northern France during the Allied invasion of France during 1944; what was ultimately considered the World War II's biggest turning point. However, much like all the Sniper Elite games before, the setting is more of a means for some nice scenery instead of telling a factual story. As for the story itself, well, again its barely there because what's there is a plot device rather than an overall narrative. That plot device drives the real driving force for this game; killing Nazis through the scope of your rifle, watching the bullet of your sniper slowly penetrate a soldier's skull as the X-Ray vision highlights someone's brain contorting to the force of a .30-06 going 2800 ft/s and climaxing with an explosion of blood and bone particles coming out the eye socket. It's Sniper Elite's formula and signature style that has kept these games going for as long as they have.

I know that may sound negative and to a point, yeah, it kind of is. Sniper Elite doesn't really change much. In fact, it's changed so little that I haven't really cared about the franchise since V2. I only got interested in this game solely because, for the first time, this game started rippling through the internets in the same way V2 did when it was first coming out. I dug around a little bit, found out the game was on Game Pass, and fired it up. 

Sniper Elite 5 is no longer a game with a sequence of linear environments with a slightly open ended design. Apparently, this open ended design akin to Sniper Elite 1 was re-introduced to the series with Sniper Elite 4, but I sadly have not played that game so I can not give you a fair comparison. What I can tell you, however is that Sniper Elite 5's open ended design is both very well developed and simultaneously frustrating as all hell. What I really love about this change in direction is that now you start a mission with a designated objective but if you go around and explore the map a little you'll end up finding intel that unlocks alternate objectives you can complete to earn additional rewards. Making the missions feel more dynamic instead of static was a phenomenal idea. However, the open ended design is kinda bogged down by the actual new mechanic to this installment; the invasion mode.

Yes, PVP in the campaign. Should you have invasion turned on a player controlled German sniper can invade your game and kill you. I'll go over this mode in a moment, but the reason why it hinders the open-map design so much is that Rebellion needed to add so many restrictions to pathways and there's just sometimes downright invisible walls. You quickly learn that these maps aren't actually big open areas. They are basically arenas stitched together to look like a big map. This is likely due to balance out the invasion mode. But the problem is this restriction with the maps is also present when you have invasion off and its very frustrating when you just want to go somewhere that seems accessible but it turns out you have to backtrack to a different walkway to get to the correct walkway that takes you around the game barrier to get where you want to go. Again, I get why they did it, but it's really an immersion killer sometimes.

Now, how is the invasion. Its good. It's really good in fact. But it does have it's problems. Much like the single player, a well placed shot on a player can lead to a slow motion kill cam with x-ray. While it's not a new mechanic at all, being able to see you inflict that damage to another player is just fresh enough to make these slow motion kills exciting again. The way it works is that, during the initial invasion, the player being invaded is able to use invasion phones almost immediately to track the invading player's location without detection. After 5 minutes, the invading player is also able to use those same phones to ping their location, but they also get a ping right back. The invading player does, however, have an extra trick up their sleeve in the form of ally tagging. An invading player can use an AOE command or ping individual nazi soldiers with their binoculars which allows them to find out where the player is should they get spotted by one of the NPCs. However, this also means that the player being invaded really doesn't have any means of defense other than not getting caught. Maybe it was intentional, I mean, Karl is one American fighting dozens of Nazis. He's already outnumbered, but it's really annoying that Karl can't do something like hide in the tall grass, which is the game's only true hiding mechanic, to avoid a ping through a phone. I think a patch should be implemented to include this as it'd make the game of cat and mouse all the more heart pounding. 

Invasions also have another very annoying feature; the matchmaking. If you are getting invaded, and you die, if you select either "Reload from Start of Invasion" or "Reload Last Save" you IMMEDIATELY get invaded again. If you're in an absolutely awful situation to begin with this can be doubly frustrating and lead to a string of getting repeatedly killed over and over again. Thankfully, you can turn off invasion upon death, but it'd be nice if the game gave you a break after dying. The only way to truly earn a break without turning it off is to kill the enemy sniper. 

I'm pretty sure I'm running out of characters so I will try to wrap this up. Along with the above, Sniper Elite 5 also introduced first person view on SMGs and pistols which is really nice. However I noticed the Thompson's iron sights are just completely messed up and don't line up. Alongside this, these weapons are also capable of achieving slow motion x-ray kills as well. There's also a weapon customization system and, just as a forewarning, you can make some pretty cursed looking guns akin to CoD: Vanguard levels of cringe. They tried to incorporate real attachments that existed during this era but there's also modern ideologies like grip tape which was just not a thing in WW2. So if you're someone who cannot stand anachronistic weapon philosophy I suggest avoiding this one. Much like the dynamic objectives, the provides more incentive to explore the map in form of workbenches. There are 3 kinds of work benches; one for rifles, one for SMGs, and one for pistols. These workbenches grant you new customization options and sometimes new weapons.

There's also the inclusion of different ammo types now too. There's types for penetrating armor good for piercing helmets, soft point for non-armored combatants, subsonic ammo to make guns quiet, non-lethal ammo, etc and all these can be swapped on the fly from your weapon wheel.

Along with this are small snippets of information you can get about a Nazi by tagging them. People are claiming Rebellion is trying to humanize some Nazis but, honestly, I don't think so. It's just there for the sake of adding some depth. Second, you earn MORE exp if you knock an enemy out first and then kill them while they're unconscious. War crimes are rewarded! 

This game also features co-op too! All of the missions in the game can be played with a fellow friendly sniper. And this co-op mode also works in invasion as well. If the invading sniper kills one of the players, the other sniper has 3 minutes to find and kill the enemy or they automatically lose. 

Sniper Elite 5 also introduced a 4 player Survival mode, which I haven't had a chance to try, but I'm sure it's alright. The game also re-introduced V2's team based PVP multiplayer alongside a snipers only mode for it which, you know, is pretty fun if you don't mind extreme camping. So all in all for $50 you get a lot of bang for your buck; 9 large scale missions all playable with a buddy and PVP, the Invasion mode, Survival, and traditional multiplayer PVP.
