Sniper Elite 5 feels really scuffed. Despite having a lot of legit improvements and QoL changes from Sniper Elite 4, and the gunplay being significantly improved, this game feels like it SHOULD be better than it actually ends up being.


The main issues of note (imo):

- AI absurdly over-perceptive compared to SE4, as well as other general AI issues (Even on normal/medium difficulty they spot you very quickly, even through foliage you can't even see through yourself. AI frequently flipflops from braindead to picking you off across the map like Simo Häyhä).

- Enemies wearing helmets are an annoyance (Funny flak/shrapnel helmets shrugging off high powered rifle rounds like they're made out of titanium. Makes shooting for the head (especially from behind) on most enemies an issue. I don't remember helmets being nearly as much of a problem in SE4).

- Movement feels far more sluggish than previous titles (Animations much slower in general, and too easy to accidentally do the wrong action, particularly with things like dropping down from ledges and climbing vines).

- Confusing map design, and lots of invisible walls (Plenty of areas you have to go the long way around to get into, and barely any shortcuts to connecting areas. Also, lots of fences and railings that you can't vault over, which forces you to go all the way around them).

- Lots of OOB spots in the terrain, and general stuck spots (Such as running too close to a wall and glitching out of bounds accidentally, which more often than not ends up with you perma-stuck and you're forced to reload a save. This ended up happening several times in different levels during my solo AND co-op playthroughs).

- Generally plenty of bugs, especially in co-op mode (Glitched animations, slow LoD fade-in, netcode issues, unkillable enemies, even as far as some softlocks in modes like survival (e.g: 2 tanks becoming unkillable and making finishing the mode impossible)).

- Lackluster ending (even by sniper elite's usual "B-movie" plot standards).

Game is pretty fun however when it's not being buggier than a Bethesda game. If you really want to buy it, I'd recommend waiting until rebellion fixes some of the more significant bugs with the game, or just wait for a sale.

Big maps are a plus and I didn't notice too much repetition with the missions.

Stealth system doesn't feel to great. I feel almost like im playing a COD game. They rarely give you an opportunity to shoot someone from over 100 meters. I found myself never even changing my zeroing because of how almost all engagements were close range.

Another feature i'm not a fan of is the enemy spotting system. Say you shoot someone in the head and it hits the helmet, If you get a follow up shot and it kills him within a second or two everyone in the vicinity will know exactly where you were even when you are suppressed simply because that one guy by himself saw you for about a milisecond.

PvP Can be fun when it works. Most times the Host will die before you even get close. Or they disconnect you not sure how that works but that happens quite a bit.

It's a fun sniping and stealth-game. My favorite type. You can go Rambo too but it can become deadly (for you) real fast.
I like putting down mines, covering my spots. AI react to their friends blowing up by trying to take an alternative way towards you. If they know where you are. If you play more stealthily and don't trigger fights or AI looking for you, you get to experience more of the story. Some "extra" conversations.

I have no-lifed the game since release. There is replayability. Huge maps, different approaches, different routes to take. Spy Academy and Rubble and Ruin are my 2 favorite maps. Especially Rubble. I love the blown up city where you can shoot from window to window or window to the street. I say window but its basically a hole in the wall or a frame for a window.

I kill like 100+ enemies on every  map. And if you manage to trigger 10-20 enemies, it gets very hectic. You have something like 6 sniper rifles that you can customize. Do you go for range and damage or maybe less zoom but fires fast? I like using both options, depending on the map. You can change your weapon choice midmission if you go to a Workbench. Theres 3 on every map. Except map 9 but that is a short filler to finish the story or something. 1 objective, no collectables or anything. On top of that you have SMGs and Pistols to unlock and customize.

Performance, I feel, is very good. At 1440p I can run all maxed except AA to have a steady breezing locked 75 fps on an Nvidia 2080. GPU isn't fully utilized, just the way I like it, fan stays quiet. Ryzen 5600X, 32 gigs of 3600 Mhz HyperX Ram. The game loads really fast too. I have it installed to a regular slow harddrive but even then, loading into a map takes 15 seconds. Crazy fast.

Bugs, there are a few I can think of. Nothing showstopping to me. From what I have read, Easy Anti-Cheat seems to have issues. I chose not to install it during game installation. I can still play online. But EAC can crash your game or just not load the game at all. Weird issues. The "forever reloading" bug was fixed 2 days after release but a new bug was introduced. Sometimes, when you want to throw a grenade or TNT, you get an arc showing you where it's going to land. Well, that arc can randomly disappear. You see no line. Then there's shooting from cover. Sometimes you press the shooty shooty button and nothing happens. To fix that, you gotta move to the left or right a bit more to be able to shoot. It's quite rare but it happens. Speaking of that, I was using some pistol and it would randomly stop shooting, I click left mouse click but nothing happened, I almost died becaause I was in CQC at the time. I just never use that pistol any more. I can't remember which one it was. I think it only happens with normal ammo. Anyway, I assume these little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ will get fixed.

I can't wait (well, I will have to) until more maps and weapons are released.

SE5 is pretty fun. I am glad gun customization has been added to this degree. You've got scopes, stocks, mags, weapon skins and much more. It is a nice touch to give you the edge you prefer. Every time I find a workbench I am excited to see if I unlocked anything. Throw on the new piece and see what it looks like. Although every attachment comes with pros and cons to your weapons overall stats. As it stands, cons feel kind of random. As an example, throw on a cheek pad and reload slows down.. K? But these cons are not ruining my fun by any means. So far the maps are very nice. My only gripe is they come with choke points between major areas. So you have a playground halted by a very narrow road, then it opens again to another location. I wouldn't mind this sometimes, but here, it is too much. SE4 had a more preferable balance with this. Also, I did NOT download the anti-cheat, so I am not playing online. Understand in this game, that means I have chosen to be punished by being rewarded less XP for everything. I just want ppl to understand, this is a real thing, in a single player game. Which I highly disagree with. 

I also have to say, so far it feels sniping has taken a back seat in SNIPER Elite. I guess Rebellion is handing the crown over to Sniper Contracts. Not to be mean, but in Sniper Contracts 2, that game came with the longest shots I've ever taken in a game. Meanwhile, in Sniper Elite, the longest shot has been 180 yards so far. I truly hope there is more to come. 

Frustration aside, as I have had more time with SE5, I actually really like the guerrilla warfare style here. Close or far (if it permits) can be really fun. Granted I shoved every difficulty farthest it can go. No hud, no sniper assist, enemies at max, lose remaining ammo in mag when reloading. I think Rebellion could do something with this. Tighten up both close range fighting with more take downs, tactical reloads and better animations (opening a door while crouched), and this could bloom. Heck. Even the bottles I am on board with. Look, I know it sounds weird to carry 4/5/6 empty glass bottles around in a loose sack when you're trying to be stealthy. However, lets be fair here, constantly having a rock is just as immersion breaking imo. Although no, I didn't use rocks in SE4. Still, I found out real quick you could just spam rocks and get soldiers to, one by one, walk right up to you for a stabby stab in the tall grass. Making close quarter combat trivial if need be. Bottles make sense. Well, not the loose glass that would clank around every half step in real life, but replace it with a finite item. Granted, I think they knew there would be some backlash so you still have your whistle. So calm down there buddy. (Sorry, honestly the rocks truly bothered me. Back to the review).

What brought me over more for my review was the map design. It looks very authentic and pulled me in. The music feels right for the time period and fits perfectly. The guns sound crisp and when he drops the slide on his .45, after loading in a new clip its sounds well oiled. Time was put into this and it shows. I was complaining about this on another game. Why do devs focus hard on one aspect (in this case, long range shooting) and slide on the other (short range)? Why not zero in on both combat styles and allow the player to choose? I understand maybe with time constraints, but outside of that, its a win/win. It seems Rebellion read my mind because this is pretty good. I just hope later levels really open up the long range (which I expect them too) and they didn't just trade one for another. 

All in all, if I find long range in this game with some beautiful shots, I'll be truly happy. As of now though, it is fun and I am enjoying my time. I still have to say, Rebellion, please, stop with the massively expensive DLC and punishing us who just want to play the game solo. I am a very talkative person, I meet people with ease. Game time is my time. This isn't to say invasion isn't a cool idea, it is. But to basically force players to opt in, is pretty egregious imo. 

Hope this scattered review helps!

My choice for a new game would have been, in a perfect world, "please can we have MORE Sniper Elite 4 for the single-player campaign?"

Rebellion delivered!  

It's more SE4 but even more gorgeous (except that distracting AA shimmer) and with lots of small enhancements, like 'focus' where, when especially close to enemies, you can press focus to gain a faint outline of where the enemy is on the other side of a wall or barrier.  It's a bit of a cheat and you don't have to use it, but I liken it to assessing where someone is by their footsteps - so yeah, I'm using this!  Other new things include weapons now carrying an indication of hearing range.  If a rifle has a hearing distance of 130m, you need to be at least that far away from the nearest enemy for your gunshots not to not be heard.  Even the trusty Welrod suppressed pistol can be heard within 14m by default, so it's not quite so much of an easy way out in this game!  The game now offers workbenches in the locations where you can upgrade and swap weapons mid-mission (love this).  You can now sabotage vehicles as well as generators to mask sound, though nuisance soldiers will insist on poking at the noise and trying to fix it as in previous games...  There is the polarising addition of non-lethal weaponry and attacks - polarising because why wouldn't you kill off someone wearing a Swastika?  But it adds a new gameplay option, and you get more points for non-lethal combat.  Polarising yes, but you have total freedom to play how you want - and who doesn't want extra choice in a game?!  Finally, you can now also upgrade Karl as well as your weapons - by earning skill points, providing enhancements such as the ability to carry more ammo, or to automatically mark an enemy that takes a shot at you.

The maps are again HUGE with plenty to do and to find (each, when played properly as a stealth operator, taking several hours to complete - easily 7 to 10 hours for me per map).  I'd estimate the title divides game-play into around 60% sniping and 40% close-quarters stealth (or combat - choice is yours).  A lot of reviews are panning it for not enough sniping and there probably is less in this one, but it's also a lot to do with how you play.  Like the previous games, you CAN run-and-gun, but the way you're supposed to play is to scout out some suitable vantage point (if lucky, with sound masking) and pick off enemies at distance.  Unfortunately, the story, map and objectives unwittingly steer players straight into direct routes leading to close quarters combat and that's probably why there are so many complaints about lack of sniping.  Ignore where you're supposed to go next.  Take your time, pick high points, mark enemies through your binoculars, and pick them off at a distance.  

Along with the good is a little bit of bad too.  Karl's impediment for climbing over small walls is back (he really suffered this in SE3 too).  This time, the 'wall' might only be an ankle-high pile of pebbles around a tree and the gap looks easy to traverse, but nope, Karl cannot go there.  He cannot climb low rocks, squeeze through what look like decent gaps in hedges etc.  It's a tad frustrating.  I get why it's been done but I think, in SE4, it was better disguised by blocking off no-access routes visibly with barbed wire, fencing or other obvious barrier.  Another issue is trying to interact with things like opening doors or picking up ammo.  There seems to be some issue where you keep having to spin round and find a perfect position to trigger the interacting prompt and, if you're in a hurry, this is beyond maddening and ideally needs to be fixed.  One thing I DON'T like: if you opt out of playing "Invasion" (yes, players can land right in your game and kill you), you earn less points.  In my opinion, a game mode should be able to entice people to play without gating game rewards behind the feature.  But that said, even without invasion points, you will ultimately find enough points to unlock all upgrades before completing the game.

The AI is a bit hit-and-miss.  Sometimes, creeping up on a foe unseen launches the red COMBAT! alert without you making a sound, and other times, the AI can seem a bit confused and bewildered before shrugging their shoulders at the dead body in front of them and assuming it was nothing.  It's not ALL the time, but it does happen here and there. 

The NPCs are a little bit wooden, but they always are in SE games.  There's a nice mix though.  You'll see complaints about some, like the black woman you first encounter because "unrealistic".  I have NO time for people who whinge about this sort of thing.  It's a fictional game with fictional characters and a whole fictional resistance.  If it was realistic, then Karl would be kicked out from the off given his lack of fitness, huffing and puffing after 10 yards of running and not even able to hop over a short stone wall, so...  I like what Rebellion has done. 
 Why can't Rebellion fictionalise it as much as they want?  I 100% support their decision and welcome it.  I can count the number of games with a black female primary on the fingers of one hand from 40 years of gaming which is shameful, so it's about bloody time!

People are commenting that bullet physics are a bit off.  I only play medium difficulty so wind direction isn't a biggie for me, but it's worth bearing in mind what others are saying.

Final criticism others make is a greatly pared-back selection of weapons.  That's true, but honestly?  All the hundreds of weapons in the previous game were just clutter and most were not used.  The weapons in this game might be fewer, but they vary in a meaningful and interesting way.  I almost feel like I've had MORE choice because the differences are greater (whereas in past games I just shrugged them off and played mostly with the default load-outs).

So, should you buy it?  If you enjoyed SE3 and/or SE4, then an absolute yes.  It is more of the same but with enhancements.  If however you found the earlier games repetitive, you'll be no better off here either.  It IS more of the same and, for that, I'm very, very glad!

It's fun for one playthrough, but prepare to be frustrated if you want replay value, especially if you want to complete the challenges. To begin with, the game has some poor design decisions. Just off the top of my head: if Fairburne knows he'll need a crowbar and bolt cutters in every mission, why doesn't he just include them in his loadout instead of having to search for them in every level? 

Pressing E to search bodies gets tiresome very quickly, especially because if you have a body and a weapon close together, you can't just walk up close and press E - you have to aim precisely or you might pick up the weapon instead of doing a search. A small irritation, but when you have to do it hundreds of times, it adds up. It would've been a lot better if the keys for searching and picking up weapons were different. It would've been even better if the body-search mechanic was removed entirely and replaced with ammo resupply crates where you could replenish your entire loadout with one keypress. Having to search enemy bodies for ammo and items is one of the more tedious and annoying things one can do in a game. The same applies to searching for workbenches, collectibles, etc. 

There aren't that many opportunities for actual sniping. Most of the time you're better off using a scoped, suppressed pistol.

The night vision scope is just badly done. The effect looks like something from 2000.

Bugs are quite frequent: bodies and weapons fall through the ground and disappear. A tank firing right next to you doesn't create a sound mask. If you're crouched and approach an interactive item on a table, very often you can't interact with it - you have to stand up. The map marker representing your objective is sometimes precise, and sometimes only in the general area of the point of interest (See the submarine pen mission).

Some bugs are much worse and ruin your entire mission: in the Wolf Mountain mission, you're supposed to be able to kill Hitler in a variety of ways. For instance, you can painstakingly make your way to a teahouse, where you can poison his breakfast. In a properly-designed game, this would trigger Hitler's arrival in the teahouse where you could then observe the culmination of your efforts. In this game, you just wait and wait and Hitler doesn't move an inch. 

There just isn't enough innovation: the game feels like a mission pack for Sniper Elite 4. This might be just me, but it's getting tiring playing with the same old WW2 weapons, doing the same old WW2 stuff. It would've been fun to be able to use a wider range of weapons, like mortars, artillery, fictional Nazi weapons (an experimental .50 caliber rifle, for instance.) Either that, or I wish Rebellion would drop the WW2 theme entirely and make a game that's set in the present or maybe even the future. With all the advances in weaponry, there is so much more a game could be.

Finally, the worst thing of all by far: buggy challenges. Completing these challenges is the only way to unlock certain items, but the game often fails to detect when you've completed a challenge. 

Example one: in the Secret Weapons mission, there's a challenge to kill an NPC "with a V2" (you have to drop a wind-tunnel-suspended V2 on him when he walks under it). There is a switch on a gantry above the rocket that drops the rocket. I go there, wait until the scientist shows up, drop the rocket. The game says [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I reload the previous save, drop the V2 on him again. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I restart the mission, play all the way through to the same spot, drop the rocket on him. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. I switch to a lower difficulty so I can get to the challenge faster, drop the V2 on him again. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. Finally, instead of pressing the button, I try shooting the hooks holding the rocket up. This time, [i]Challenge completed[/i]. So dropping the rocket on him by shooting a support works; doing so by pressing a button doesn't. 

Example two: In the Festung Guernsey mission, there's a challenge to kill an NPC by causing him to fall into wet concrete, when he's leaning on a rickety wooden railing. First attempt: I wait for him to lean on the railing, then shoot the railing. The railing falls off, the NPC stays there, leaning on air. [i]Challenge failed[/i]. The second time, I weaken the railing beforehand by kicking it, then trigger the sequence that causes him to lean on it. This time he falls in, but the game says [i]Challenge failed[/i].

At which point I quit in frustration.

[h1]Mediocre game that leaves mixed feelings[/h1]

[u]What I liked very much[/u]

Graphics: In the era of questionable attempts at Global Illumination and fifty thousand image filters, SE5 surprises very pleasantly with needle-sharp textures and well-chosen color palette. It's a gorgeous game, at least when it comes to map and texture work, even at huge distances.

Sure, the characters shown in cutscenes look quite outdated, but that's not really what the game is about and not a big deal. If anything, they could just pre-render the cutscenes to smoothen out the experience a bit.

User interface: Is simple and functional, with tons of tutorials for newcomers and so on. Again, really good.

[u]What felt lackluster[/u]

X-ray vision has now way more organs per enemy soldier. Which makes it somehow worse, because you're not feeling like you're hitting a vital organ, but just a mess of human anatomy. X-ray thing was always something to tip serotonin in player's head, a gamified reward of doing something well, and now it just doesn't work.

Audio feels lackluster, too. First mission had supposedly music, but it was just some sort of weird jungle howling that I tuned down a lot. And I never noticed any music after that, in other missions, even if it was there, it was so dull that it never added anything to experience nor registered in my brain.

Older games had sort of screaming sound effect effect accompanying "X-ray shot", like death coming after enemy. It was very well engineered and added a lot to the feel of taking down an enemy. That, too, is gone now. How could they mess up the most distinctive element of their series, is quite puzzling.

There's a talent/skill tree, but skills feel totally pointless, and do little else than alleviate bad game design decisions that could have been avoided to begin with.

[u]What I don't like at all[/u]

Well, you're not a Sniper anymore. Most missions require you to infiltrate complex, narrow mazes of buildings and interiors, packed to the brim with enemies, while wielding loud, inaccurate firearms and very aggressive AI. It's puzzling, really. And unlike Hitman or Splinter Cell series, there's no gamified reward system of avoiding the enemies and going just after targets, nor even good map design to attempt it, so I really don't get it. Game asks you to collect all sorts of intel, which means - "kill everyone, explore everything". Then makes killing anything quite difficult and messy (poor weapon choice, aggressive, telepathic AI, endless reinforcements). It's just bad game design.

Levels are supposedly open-world, but in reality, feel quite linear, with hedgerows and chest-high bushes forcing you to choose from only 2-3 linear paths at most. It's quite annoying, as is lack of high ground to snipe in a game called 'Sniper Elite'. 

I played for 5 hours, but I still can't figure out breath-holding sniping. There's a diamond over enemy. Then there's a double diamond. Sometimes the bullet kills enemy, sometimes it does not, no matter which diamond you see. What does it all mean and why couldn't that be solved more elegantly?

There's non-lethal options for melee attacks and even... "non-lethal bullets"! I have zero idea what led to such laughable decision in a game where main attraction is seeing a well-placed bullet crush an eyeball or kidney. Feels like yet another half-cooked, "have it to have it" idea. 

Why would you go non-lethal [b]at all?[/b]. In Hitman series, you're hired to kill 1-2 people. Rest are either civilians or security guards or otherwise quite innocent people. In Metal Gear Solid V, you spare soliders to evacuate and turn and hire them to your side. In Splinter Cell or Alpha Protocol, you're a spy/saboteur and evading enemies makes sure that if you learn intel, they won't know you learnt it and change the plan. 
In Sniper Elite, leaving Nazi soldiers alive.... [b]why[/b] exactly? First mission of this game tasks you to sabotage coastal defenses and radar to make landing easier for Allied troops. Why would you leave enemy infantry there? To help Third Reich win???

I'm sure nobody thought about this question while making Sniper Elite. Which tells the tale of this game.

Sniper Elite 5 Review

Controls, movement & traversal mechanics:

Sniper Elite is first and foremost a tactical game, which implies the player's ability to observe the map, plan ways to approach and then execute the plan with fluidity. For that appropriate level design, movement animations and controls are a requirement. When the player can’t predict whether or not they will be able to climb this wall or vault over that group of crates or hide themselves behind that corner all the tactical elements that give Sniper Elite games their unique identity are removed leaving only generic 3rd person action with clunky controls, glitchy animations and weird AI.

Animations blending is missing resulting in disconnected animations. The main default speed feels like you are in a manga, too speedy to me for a jog and the torso of the character is inclined too much. It’s a tactical shooter. Also the transition between climbing a stair and then resuming the default speed is obviously not proper: seems like the math behind is wrong and the speed is miscalculated because of the slope - happens too often in nowadays games. Slow crouch feels unnecessary as you can still approach enemies with a normal crouch (which looks very similar to the one from Splinter Cell Blacklist). At the same time the fast crouch was removed, so the player can only rely on jogging animation which is too fast and clunky to control. Sniper Elite 4 had the same set of animations but used differently with slow crouch being the default one and fast (running) crouch being an option, jog, walk and sprint all working properly and transitions being smooth. Why keep those animations and then change the movement system completely to speed everything up, so it becomes broken?

Traversal is incoherent: you don’t really know what you can climb and where. Sometimes you can climb a wall and other times you can’t. Same with vaulting: you can’t vault over wider but still small enough walls, tree trunks or crates which is absurd. It breaks the immersion and reduces the tactical options. And it was possible in SE4! Fluidity is missing from player movements. An important thing - fluid vaulting over and jumping down from high walls when sprinting (like in SE4 … almost and Splinter Cell Blacklist) was removed. Instead you’re constantly interrupted by your character hanging down the wall and need to press the jump down button to continue which breaks the continuity, feels clunky and can be deadly in combat.

To resume, people are usually saying that with Ubisoft games you are not in control of your character, but honestly I can legitimately claim that by Splinter Cell Blacklist I was for once in full control.

If the developers tried to mimic Elden Ring (not because it was “a said” good one but because it was a successful one on sales*), they reached their goal by successfully reproducing both clunky controls and the invasion system. 

* I bet my hand FromSoft won’t reproduce that success in their next title if they stick with the same mechanics. I did like, however, the difficulty and the non-handheld approach to the exploration side.

Other parts:

Binoculars are high tech ones. Did devs try to copy-paste Watch Dogs smartphones this time? Because you feel yourself always connected to a satellite database which is giving you precise information about every German soldier personality and lives. Also that wonderful device comes equipped with a powerful long-range microphone you can use to listen to all their conversations (only tested the Hard difficulty level so I assume the “Authentic” removes that superb feature).

Same with markers and UI: Rebellion (the new team) decided to follow Watch Dogs and not Elden Ring (which would have been more appropriate here).

A mechanic to hide dead bodies comes straight from Blacklist, Hitman and Metal Gear Solid 5 games (my preference goes to the last one). Zip lines are … no they are not from Death Stranding.

Gunplay is … meh. Recoil is almost nonexistent from what I’ve seen. It’s becoming a very “popcorn action game” oriented and no longer a Sniper “Elite”. And yes, some people did say it truly on forums here, I’m starting to be much more interested in Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts games from Underdog Studio, it’s just a shame they did not add a co-op feature to those!

And what this animated gif is suggesting to potential buyers, future players, about what you can expect from the game? I’m interested in your answers.
https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/1029690/extras/SE5_Campaign_Final_2.gif?t=1653557291
Here is mine and also suggestions from my friends: we will be able to drive all those vehicles in the game.

Also for the very first time in a game I turned the music off after listening to it for 5 mins. What an idea and a strange one to loop a sound ended with cymbals (drum set) when not in combat?

… could continue talking about clunky and broken mechanics compared to Sniper Elite 4, overabundance of silenced guns, strange way to manage your equipment, alert being irrelevant, AI inconsistencies … but it’s enough said already.

A conclusion:

Don’t get it wrong: I am comparing SE5 to other games not to favor those studios, but to point at nowadays developers copy/pasting existing mechanics and mixing them inappropriately which leads to their own game losing its identity as a result. From my personal point of view it’s not a game made with even a bit of passion, it’s a release rushed to generate funds for the next Rebellion game (by the main team this time and let’s hope that one will justify those sacrifices).

Overall, it's an okay game, but it really feels like a step down from Sniper Elite 4. It has less guns and a less satisfying progression system. I can't really recommend this game because Sniper elite 4 is just better and costs less.

I don't quite get the hate this game is getting from some of it's players. Is it as open ended as 4? No, but the game seems to have more unique ways of approaching seemingly every situation. The game is repetitive *if* you take the most straight forward approach. It seems as though every objective besides AA guns and bunkers can be done without a satchel charge. Yes, even the war room in mission 7 if you don't have enough intel. The levels are varied and interesting with a nice linear difficulty curve (also if an enemy doesn't have a helmet, you can knock them out with a bottle). You get better equipment, but the enemies get better too. More elite troops, more troops with helmets, snipers, better snipers, armored cars, tanks, etc. The enemies also have little info blurbs in the binoculars, so if you want to play this selectively non-lethal as if you're snake from MGS (pick your favorite) but he has telepathy for some reason, you can do that. 

But there are some cons, one of which being that the weapon customization was a little bit annoying as a C&R enthusiast. Grip tape, the M2 sniper scope (which is Korean war vintage and a really terrible scope), and the disappointing pistol selection among these "issues". The welrod is practically a requirement, but the OSS and SOE used other guns like integrally supressed Hi-Standard .22s and at least one modified Webley 1908 self-loader. Just finished the main campaign. Enjoyed it, but can't recommend it, especially for the price. The why follows:

What they have done is taken an atmospheric shooter which really hit a high point in its 4th incarnation and made it, well, worse. MUCH worse. 

The game is supposed to be about traversal, stealth, and finding your way to take out various enemies. What it has become is on-rails, do-this-this-way then do-that-same-thing-again-in-a-different-place, but sometimes they mix in you having absolutely no idea what you are supposed to be doing. 

Stealth Example: Sub pen, surrounded by Germans, trying to figure out how to sabotage a fuel system when the icon it presents for objectives is nothing more than a general hint, when at other times it's showing you exactly what you need to interact with. Turns out there was only one way to do it, by using a crowbar on a nondescript panel next to one of many large doors that for the most part are inaccessible. Only way I found it was by killing everyone so I could have a good look around. Not. Exactly. Immersive.

Other stealth issues: Enemies sometimes get stuck on a piece of scenery then warp to where they were going, resulting in suddenly being where they weren't as you were sneaking up on them. If combat initiates (in other words you have been caught) even if you stay exactly where you are having killed the one who spotted you their mates will, after a short period of running about, go back to what they were doing before despite their pal's corpse now being draped over their position. Oh, and bottles are the new rocks. Bottles. Up to six of them in your inventory and that's exactly the kind of thing a sniper needs, because milk floats are so difficult to hear. 

Traversal example: The first mission looks like a huge open map with endless possibilities for approach and escape. It would be, if not for the huge amounts of invisible walls that force you to follow - at best - one of two paths to a place. Each map has distinct areas, so your ability to move between them is massively hampered for reasons as yet unknown. 

Other traversal issues: There are ziplines everywhere in some missions, meaning that relocation is dramatically oversimplified, particularly if you have been spotted. at the same time, there are 6 foot high walls you can climb but a knee high hedge is magically impassable. And they have added a bit of Far Cry 4 tower-climbing goodness when you have to figure out how to access a workbench (sometimes you will know it's there in advance, sometimes not) where you can change your loadout (good apart from not many different types) and what your weapons are fitted with (massively underwhelming).  To get there, you have to find the only possible path to one half of a bombed out farmhouse because you can't for example, move the light pieces of furniture that are blocking the stairs, or shoot them, or blow them up. Flimsy wooden doors remain impervious to high explosives, as do hedges, arboretums and small rocks. You can kill a Tiger tank with them though. Oh, and interaction with the environment is AWFUL. You frequently have to stand up to pick up some objects because the game won't cycle through what you can interact with when you change what you are looking at. Sometimes, it takes four tries to climb a ladder, and it's really easy for the game to drop you from a great height because it has decided that you moving towards the ladder was you intending to drop down the hole it's in and injure yourself. And sometimes you climb a ladder to find you can't even get onto the surface it leads to, presumably because of a glitch. Dreadful execution.

Finding your own way to kill someone? Well, you CAN sometimes do that but the only problem is you are SUPPOSED to kill them a specific way, usually involving the environment or something else that is simply..a task. Put poison in someone's glass, unlock a weapon. Choose any other way? No new weapon for you, and there is usually only one environmental option for each target. Shooting them from 500 yards through a glass window isn't even an option because the game makes glass impenetrable to high velocity armour-piercing rounds - but again, you can kill Tigers with them. The whole point of the game was to find a way to kill the target that matches how you play - and that has been completely removed. 

So, apart from those three issues, and the egregious, gauche social "justice" messaging that crops up in almost every cutscene, Sniper Elite 5 isn't awful. It looks very pretty, shooting is still fun, although the effectiveness of the assault weapon slot is very limited as soon as Jagers turn up (7 bullets into one and he was still fighting until I used the much more effective pistol). 

So, if you've got this far and still haven't figured out if you should get it, please don't. Get 4. It's a much, much better game in almost every respect.

I'm not really part of the community but I played Sniper Elite 4 and thought I'd give this a shot; having finished the campaign on authentic I have quite a few frustrations and ultimately I think I have to give the game a thumbs down.

Chief amongst my frustrations was the level design. It's starkly worse than SE4: large stretches of a lot of the maps are simply unfun to move around on. Most feature long stretches of arbitrary barriers of various kinds that force you onto certain paths despite looking traversable. Enemy placement varies wildly from tutorial-esque, to interesting, to arbitrarily punishing - and the limited ways to approach a given situation make this problem substantially worse. Sometimes you'll end a mission and have to run clear across the map to exfiltrate. In fairness there were a few interesting locations (Spy Academy is a prime example) but even those were let down by the above issues. The first level is particularly bad and is a terrible introduction to the game (especially compared to SE4's first level).

The level design also encourages you into close-range engagements. The level design provides very few satisfying sniper positions where you can take out more than one or two enemies from a single position, and visibility from the ones you do get is usually limited to the point of frustration. This is especially true at higher difficulty levels where any given sniper shot is likely to cause major problems if you don't get the kill first time, while by contrast you can often correct a messed-up close combat with an extra pistol shot or two, or moving into melee. It's honestly not really what I wanted from a game where you play a sniper.

The game in general is very buggy. Enemies t-posing, vehicles disappearing, camera wildly swinging at random, enemies clipping/phasing through walls, tank turrets juddering, vehicles queueing up on the roads, clunky animations, "cover" blocking shots it shouldn't, the list goes on. It's impossible to play for more than five to ten minutes without encountering some kind of minor bug, and while I didn't personally experience anything gamebreaking there are a number of gamebreaking bugs in other people's reviews.

There are some other design choices I hated too. Limited numbers of saves. Why? Some enemies are essentially impossible to take down in melee and it's impossible to tell which are which, so you get locked into a loop of attack/counter or end up getting shot. Why? They removed SE4's crouch-sprint. Why?

The writing is mediocre, as is the voice acting. Dialogue repeats way too much if you play a level with any kind of patience. The music is jarring and intrusive and highlights how empty the maps feel when you're near the end of the level. Quite a lot of content has been cut compared to SE4 that appears to be being held back for DLC.

And lastly, a big frustration for me specifically: this game absolutely does not respect your hard drive space. I loathe having to uninstall half of my games just to fit this on my SSD. But your mileage (and available space) may vary on this one; there are worse games out there.

I know these sound like a lot of complaints. The game definitely has its upsides, and for a AA game from a smaller studio there's a lot to love. I just wish it'd been released later with more time in the schedule for improving the level design, more gameplay testing (not just QA, though that too), and more bugfixing.

There was very clearly something missed with QA. There's quite a few game breaking bugs that cause you to restart a mission or save, as well as bugs that straight up disable your weapons from working at all. Axis invasion can be fun, but the Easy Anti-cheat doesn't seem to catch any of the cheaters I've come across, and it really sucks the fun out of a sniper vs. sniper match when you get shot from across the map by someone spamming the option to hint where you are without any cool down.
Then there's the level design... some are great, Atlantic Wall has plenty of different areas and objectives with multiple ways to complete them, the Factory has a ton of vertical movement, but then there's Spy Academy.
That entire map is hell. Everything is vertical movement, the streets are confusing and seemingly nonsensical half the time. The directions you're supposed to go are rather hidden, sometimes the soldiers on that map will clip through cover or just straight up see through solid walls at random points, if you aggro even a single enemy, even knocking them out or killing them right away, about a dozen guys in random spots across the map know where you are.
There's some major bugs with Survival mode as well. When injuring an enemy enough, they're supposed to switch to their pistol, however sometimes those enemies will be holding a pistol, but still firing the same weapon as before. This is especially an issue when that weapon was an MG42 or a Panzerfaust, as the AI will try to retreat or get close to you depending on how panicked they are, and there's nothing worse than going to melee a wounded enemy and suddenly being shot in the face with a panzerfaust because the game glitched out.

Coming back to the game over a year later and the majority of the gamebreaking bugs are fixed, but Survival clearly didn't get a pass. You might not experience the game mistakenly showing an enemy using the wrong weapon, but you'll definitely experience things where enemies will retreat outside of the map boundary to avoid you. This was especially fun when said enemy was a tank I was attempting to place a satchel charge on. It just simply drove a few feet forwards until it was out of the boundary I could move in to place the satchel and stared me down until I tried to retreat and grab a panzerfaust instead only for the tank to instant-kill me with a shot from the main cannon. I hadn't been spotted, it just randomly decided to do this. Thank goodness the only unlocks for Survival mode are cosmetic, because I'm not touching that gamemode again.

This game differs a lot from the other sniper elite games,  So let's quickly talk about the good and bad changes:

Good changes: 
Weapon customisation. I was sceptical at first, but it is a nice addition, as it does not make a gun a lot stronger or weaker, it instead shifts it's strengths and weaknesses around which is nice.

Infiltration mode: The mode itself is suprisingly fun, and even feels like a good match for sniper elite which i was not expecting. You do get reduced xp without it turned on, but it has little impact on your game.

The Bad changes:
they removed the rocks and replaced it with bottles you find everywhere. Why? just why? It changes the gameplay only a little, but takes away realisme which was appearently something they aimed for on this version. (*lengty laughter*)

The difficulty. It is so darn easy. Unless it's a vehicle, you can just run at the enemy Call of Duty style and win on all but the hardest difficulties. I remember struggling with sniper elite 4 on authentic plus - no saves. It was hardly a challenge to complete this game on authentic. 

The technical/gameplay stuff:

A.I.
Dear god... the A.I. is terrible. They essentially have 2 states. Braindead or cheater. In stealth you can just jog up to them and stab them. not sneak/crouch. JOG!. It's a joke. But god forbid you are looking at them from 30 meters away, because then they are suddenly hawks. Loud is no better. They either run past you like you don't exist, or they start shooting at you like wallhacks are activiated. It's garbage.

Then there is a lot of changes I am just not sure about. The new maps are mostly bigger and feel more authentic, yet at the same time most of them are very void of life. Not just NPC's, but also sounds and animals are very little to be seen. On top of that the game still feels like it guides you trough the map by blocking off a lot of alternative paths with bushes and barbed wire, so what is the point of having big open maps? You just go full walking simulator from location A to B to C.

They removed  many nice things from previous sniper elites. The officers are less important. The soldiers that I think are supposed to be the new valkeries are hardly any different then normal soldiers. Objectives now randomly pop up based on intel you find, making you run around the map a lot. The killcams make you see more, but also less, because the veins and flesh blocks most of your vision of the organs.

Then there is a lot of tiny things like the very annoying climbing and cover mechanisme and poor hit registrations, but I don't even want to get into that.

As a sniper elite game, I miss the hearth and soul of it.
As a sniper game that is more arcade, I kinda like it.
There is a lot of tiny things that frustrate me, but still enjoy it.

Sniper Elite 5 would be a fantastic game if Sniper Elite 4 didn't exist. I played through the entire campaign of Sniper Elite 4 last week (without knowing this was coming out) and it's an incredible game. Everything in this game is *good*, but most of it feels like a downgrade from Sniper Elite 4. For example:
[list]
[*]the difficulty system is [i]fine[/i], but coming from the highly granular difficulty settings of 4 is a real let down. I miss having a dozen sliders with the ability to customise every part of the difficulty rather than just choosing easy, medium or hard for a couple overall attributes (There are like 3 sliders instead of like 12). This has lots of gameplay impacts that make the game less satisfying than it was in 4.
[*]the maps are [i]fine[/i], but the maps of 4 feel so much more open. I would regularly get kills of 100m-300m in 4, but those are few and far between in 5. My most used weapon in some maps is my pistol because so much of the map is close range and using a rifle is just impractical.
[*]the sniping is [i]fine[/i], but it's just not as satisfying as 4. The kill cams are not as good, and you cannot toggle the aim assist without changing the overall sniping difficulty, which makes it feel like you're forced to play with training wheels the whole time unless you want to play on the hardest modes. This plus the shorter distances the maps let you snipe from and the whole thing is just [i]fine[/i].
[*]the weapon progression is [i]fine[/i], but it lacks the sense of accomplishment that 4 had. In Sniper Elite 4, you upgrade guns by performing certain challenges. For example, you unlock an upgrade for one of the rifles by getting 50 liver shot kills. It's difficult, frustrating, and requires a lot of play time to get, but it makes you a better sniper and it makes the unlock so much more rewarding. In Sniper Elite 5, you primarily unlock upgrades by finding workbenches in the levels. No real challenge or difficulty. Just look for the resistance fighter symbol to be painted on a building and find a way in. This isn't [i]bad[/i], and it would work well to compliment the challenge system. It is, however, not a replacement for that system, and it just feels [i]cheaper[/i].
[/list]
There are some areas where the game is better. For example, I really like the new weapon customisation. This is makes preparing for maps a lot more interesting by forcing you to not just consider which gun but also things like what ranges you will be working at. The map design, however, really kneecaps this. While the guns have many stats that you can adjust for, you rarely adjust anything beyond balancing the most damage you can get with the best accuracy you can get. There are rarely meaningful tradeoffs, and the maps don't really compel you to play in different ways, so you'll likely find a preferred weapon and just use that. 

All of this makes rating this game really difficult. This is not a bad game, it just isn't as good as the last one in the series. If I had never played Sniper Elite 4, I think I would probably really enjoy this game. I have, however, played Sniper Elite 4, and the juxtaposition is simply not in 5's favour. My advice is to play Sniper Elite 4 first and wait for this to be on sale for below launch price. If you've played 4 already and really want more content, this is fine and you probably won't dislike it, but it will just feel a bit hollow.

If you like the SE series like I did from 2 to 4, you'll probably also enjoy this entry!  This game takes the already-widened scope of SE4's maps and makes things even bigger.... at least at first, the maps shrink as the storyline progresses but stay just as densely packed.

The extensive gun customization, new sound design for slowdown pieces (as well as overall soundtrack), and mild stealth improvements are highlights.  The multiplayer maps also seem plenty huge but that seems to be a very small minority of players actually partaking, even just a few days after launch.

Be warned that the coop mode seems to be especially buggy for the campaign, though not unusable by any means, it's mostly an issue for immersion.  The singleplayer didn't have any big blemishes in my experience to ruin the fun like coop could have from time to time, like getting caught on colision and being stuck until reloading a save.

The new addition of "invasions" during either singleplayer or coop campaign time is.... weak, much to my disappointment.  The idea is awesome, introduce some impromptu PvP into the campaign mission maps where the single invader gets the help of NPC allies to take down the player(s).  There's a few problems with this that I believe could be fixed to make the experience far better for all involved:

1.  The invader has NO indication where the player is unless they're detected by the NPCs, or even if it's one player or two.  At 5 minutes they can use the invasion devices to be given a map point of where the player is, but that's on a cooldown, and the player can use these devices as often as they like to reveal the invader.  This tends to mean any games I saw of invasion resulted in either player just stumbling into the other, and whoever draws first wins, extremely boring and not terribly fun.
2.  The invader doesn't know what the map objectives are or what has been completed.  Knowing either of these pieces of information would allow invaders to plan their attacks or set up ambushes for the player, making games far more interesting.
3.  The invader doesn't get a "sniper's sense" ability to indicate which compass direction the player is in, or if they're in close proximity.

When you might invade a game and get plopped literally behind their flank for an easy kill or straight across the map with nothing to do, it's a very mixed bag of experiences, most of them bad.

The core of sniper elite is here and as fun as ever, but as others have mentioned in steam reviews, a lot of the new implementations are lacking, though they don't detract from the overall package in a meaningful way.  For me, this is just MORE sniper elite, and I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it, let's hope SE6 can be on a shiny new engine with more detailed damage physics on bodies.  This game worries me a little that Rebellion will fall into Far Cry syndrome and leave their polished heart to rot, but for what it is, this game is absolutely worth the time.

Yes if you are a fan and have all the other SE titles.  No if you are looking for something fresh, hit this on a sale or wait a few months at least to get the patches in. This review will be primarily for the new Invasion game-mode.

Honestly, it's not bad. But there are two MAJOR issues for the style of game-mode it is, and also for a sniper centered PvP game mode.

So first off, this, as you probably can guess by the name, is a SNIPER game. Which seems like an awesome setting for a Soulsbourne-ish PvP invasion game mode.

The major issue with the game mode is that it has an "Anti Camper" countermeasure, in a game mode where you're playing as a counter sniper that's supposed to be defending objectives from an enemy sniper. Which you'd figure may lead to to stay in a relatively small area while you wait for the enemy sniper to show up. But the game says NO! CAMPER!!! STOP IT!!! GO RUN AND GUN!!! And if you ignore the "Camping Detected" pop up, the game then tags you for the player you're invading. Which is absolutely ridiculous in a game where you'd assume setting up an ambush would be a viable strategy.

The other major issue is honestly a lot worse. The failure state for invading is either be killed, or fail to kill the player who you're invading before they complete the campaign mission they're on. Which is totally fine, except for the fact that if they manage to complete the mission, it triggers a cutscene which you cannot skip, and when that cutscene ends all you're met with is a "DEFEAT" screen. There's absolutely NO reason to make an invader sit through a cutscene just to tell them they lost. Honestly, not only could this give someone story spoilers since you can invade a player who's on the last mission even if you as the invader haven't completed the first mission, but also like what the ♥♥♥♥??? Why are you forced to watch a whole cutscene instead of it telling you that "Oopy doopy, you lost!" and disconnecting you once the invaded player triggers the cutscene.

Or better yet, make it like Deathloop where before you complete the mission you're on you either have to kill the invading player, or you need to complete an objective (in Deathloop's case hack a jammer).

A pinnacle of everything this series has accomplished so far. The best level design, gun customization, gameplay and graphics in the series. I have finished the game after almost 30 hours on Sniper Elite (Hard) difficulty and already started Authentic difficulty playthrough. 
Maps are huge and filled with multiple objectives and large variety of ways to accomplish them. I thoroughly explored each map on first playthrough, yet I'm constantly discovering new stuff on second time around. There is just so much variety and verticality on each map. They expanded on the climbing system from Sniper Elite 4 and its now used to its full potential, opening up the game even more.
Great new addition is an option to use different starting points for each mission once you discover them. They also added workbenches on each map, which allow you to customize your loadout while on mission, allowing you to adapt your tactics.
Speaking of customization, the "gun porn" in this game is crazy. You have multiple rifles, SMGs and pistols, each with large amount of customization options for each part of the gun. Every part has advantages and disadvantages, so you have to consider each option carefully.
Each mission, aside from main goals, offers optional secondary goals and "kill list" targets. These targets are a new addition to the series, clearly inspired by Hitman games, as each target has an optional, special method of killing them (like dropping the chandelier on their head or drowning them in concrete). I enjoyed these targets, but I miss the challenges from Sniper Elite 4. These were really interesting and forced you to play specific way, greatly increasing replay value.
Audio-visual side of Sniper Elite 5 is fantastic. Thanks to photogrammetry and great lighting, each location is very detailed and realistic. Music feels much more present than ever before in the series and really helps build the atmosphere of each location (that mission 7 music).
Story wise its rather meh, it was never a focus of the series, but the main villian feels very underwhelming. Enemy AI feels a bit dumber than it was in Sniper Elite 4 and unfortunately there is no Authentic Plus difficulty at the moment. Also the physics and animations of this game can get a bit wonky at times, its not bad but gets a bit distracting at times.
While Rebellion didn't reinvent the series, they improved on every aspect of previous games, polishing them to shine. I am a huge Sniper Elite fan and for me this is the best entry in the series. You are getting 8 huge missions, each with great replay value and lots of customization options. 
I can't wait to see how they expand on this game and considering the quality of DLCs for previous games, I'd say we are in for a treat. I highly recommend Sniper Elite 5 to any stealth-sniper-shooter fan out there. There are so many ways to play this game, everyone can find something for themselves here.

[h1]A step up from SE4, just not a big enough one given the time gap between[/h1]
As a baseline the game is conceptually nice, however it needs a solid round of patching and QOL improvements.
[b]TL;DR If you enjoyed every SE game prior to this one, you can get this one as well, in any other case i recommend waiting for patches to bring the game up to quality standard.[/b]

Graphics haven't changed much, rendering is mostly same. Assets have been upgraded through use of photogrammetry which greatly improves look of everything except foliage, shading is bit outdated and antialiasing is non existant. Performance is also mostly okay although much like SE4, lack of benchmark on game launch makes synthetic testing and fine-tuning harder.

Gameplay is about as good as SE4 is, couple of things got streamlined for better or worse. My biggest issues are with how clunky player handling is as every interaction seems to have a hefty delay before it's actually executed, turn radius is huge and causes issues indoors.

Level design seems to be sidestep from SE4, levels are slightly bigger than in previous game and more detailed (especially urban parts) but they also rely on having a lot of areas that aren't technically accessible to the player, very often you cannot travel from point A to point B in a straight line as you'll encounter large patches of inaccessible areas in the middle, sometimes they make sense and sometimes they don't, like patch of farmland fenced off with hip high rocks and bushes.

AI i don't particularly mind, it's also an improvement from SE4, stealth is even more viable although enemies are easy to pick off outside actual combat and even if combat breaks out it's easy and way more preferable to run away and come back once they settle down. As far as actual combat is, they are way more deadlier than in previous games.

Audio is also a genuine improvement, it doesn't blow competition out of the water but there are now way more distinct weapon sounds, for up close and distance shots plus some nice reverbs which are sometimes used in interiors.

The new featured gamemode of axis invasions is a mixed bag which sounds great on paper but doesn't play out half as fun in practice. Majority of the time people either are ignorant of the fact that they're invaded and you can pick them off with ease while at another end of the spectrum people will stop dead in their tracks and entrench in one position for as long as they can or outright commit suicide or kick you out of their session. In general the mode has very, very little to do with sniping duels as majority of kills will be in close quarters range.

This also leads into topic of netcode for peer to peer modes like Invasions and Survival/Coop, which is atrocious (and has been for many entries in the series now). It flat out doesn't work, there's a huge delay on everything and players/enemies teleport every now and then. In coop modes this is perhaps a minor annoyance but in invasions it means difference between victory and defeat.

In terms of bugs - there are several, none of them gamebreaking but they can prevent you from completing achievements and getting weapon rewards. On my machine performance and stability is OK.
Perhaps biggest and "wonkiest" change in my eyes are new ragdolls which seem to die in very similar but also very unlikely gymnasitc positions like frog squats, heads between legs, trying to suck themselves off and so on and so forth. The frequency of how often each of those repeats is so consistent i consider it a deliberate feature at this point.

In general the game isn't a necessarily a huge evolutional step for the franchise, it has a potential to be a much refined version of SE4. Provided the develoers sit down on it and implement several much needed features and fixes to further polish the experience.

It's Sniper Elite 5. If you've played any other Sniper Elite, you basically already know what you're getting: an incremental improvement on the existing formula. If you liked the previous games, you'll almost definitely like this one once the bugs are ironed out.

If you haven't though, the really, really short version is that Sniper Elite is a series about being an Elite Sniper who for some reason is also a commando who has to sneak into areas alone to deal with entire platoons, tanks, aircraft, random Nazi super weapons, and in-between all that also has to shoot Hitler every few months.

The game's most compelling mechanics are that bullet drop and wind physics are actually accounted for as part of shooting, and you get a fancy bullet camera showing you every individual organ/tendon/etc. your bullet severed on its path through Nazi #8,792. These are excellent and if the concept interests you, you will probably enjoy the Sniper Elite series (though it might be arguable if you'll find them worthwhile at full price).

As for 5 in particular, the close quarters combat feels a lot better than in the previous installments. The increased information on what ranges weapon and ammo types are audible from is great. Sniping feels as good as ever, and it really hits its stride on chapter 3 of the campaign where you can spend tens of minutes methodically picking off targets from 300m+ away prior to entering the mission area proper to clean up the stragglers. I also believe that the limitations placed on throwing rocks and ressing coop partners was a good idea.

Please keep in mind that I have not tried the invasion mode yet, as I want to finish the campaign once before adding an extra chaos agent to it. I also only really play the Sniper games on authentic/authentic plus, since accounting for bullet physics is what I enjoy most in these games. I have no idea how this plays on lower difficulties with UI assist.

In terms of things I think could be done better. Still a lot of bugs. The map is a bit confusing as to what can be traversed and what can't, as some waist-high walls will completely thwart your progress but sometimes you can also go up what appears to be a flat wall. Still missing a full authentic plus equivalent from Sniper Elite 4.

Overall verdict: give it like a month for some of the worst bugs to get patched. Afterward, if you're a die hard Sniper Elite fan it's probably worth a grab. If you're new to the series, might want to try it on a sale (or grab Sniper Elite 4 when it's on sale and make a decision on 5 based off that).

The Campaign may be pretty bland, but Sniper Elite 5 is very much an iterative sequel that builds upon what players already enjoy about the series without focusing too much on the innovation. That being said, x-ray vision headshots and invading players who just want to have a good time are both well worth the price of admission for a sniper tour of France.

Pros
-------
- Axis Invasions are addictive Dark Souls-esque PVP invasions
- Each map is a unique miniature sandbox
- Cross-play and Cross-Platform
- The return of the internal x-ray gunshot killcams
- Freely tweakable difficulty settings including health regeneration, wind, and bullet drop
- Only 9 campaign missions (10 with the Wolf Mountain DLC) makes it short but sweet

Cons
-------
- Separate unlock progression across Campaign, Multiplayer, and Axis Invasions
- Most weapon and attachments are locked behind either collectibles or kill counts, depending on mode
- Assassinating Hitler is locked behind DLC
- Large amounts of downtime and sprinting around oversized maps to find your next target or objective

While going back to World War II might not be on the top of players' minds when it comes to a new shooter, the new Axis Invasion mode brings Dark Souls competitive PVP to a stealth series in a way that might be impossible to top.

If you've never played Sniper Elite but enjoy games like MGS:V or the Splinter Cell series, you will probably like Sniper Elite 5. There is a focus on stealth-action/espionage gameplay, but unfortunately the actual stealth isn't as good as either of those games. 

Instead there are sniping elements like bullet drop, wind speed, and 'sound masking', with a bit of a focus on things like managing your heart rate - e.g if you sprint for a while, your increased heart rate will make your sniper scope unsteady until you catch your breath, and if you are bleeding from a wound then your heart rate will not decrease until you use a bandage or medkit. 

You can also customise elements of difficulty like turning the minimap, and enemy marking on or off. After going through the game once I found going through a second time without a map or markers was an excellent challenge, because you really need to make some of those shots count.

Be aware that the game is a bit janky. There are invisible walls around the edges of missions, and there is no jump button, so sometimes you can't climb over really simple barriers like chest high walls or small rocky slopes (instead you get a button prompt to climb things like walls and fences if it is possible). It makes just a couple of parts of the game seem weird and confusing. But when it is good, it is REALLY good and you can have some seriously fun and very tense moments moving through very detailed European castles and cities. Trying to do a no kill run can be very difficult.

The most fun comes from the co-op and invasion modes, which add extra layers to the experience and allow you to come back and approach missions in entirely new ways. Invasions especially require players to keep moving and always be alert to their surroundings. 

At the time of writing there is one frustrating issue where the player character will narrate information to himself out loud for the benefit of the player (e.g "I see the enemy bunker up ahead, looks like the intel was correct.") and the invading player can hear him speaking to himself. The defending player cannot currently turn these narrations or control their speaking volume when being invaded, which means they might unintentionally give themselves away just by walking into a new area. With enough feedback the developers should be able to patch something like this. EDIT: they fixed this issue.

Initially I was debating on whether or not to refund the game. But after an hour and a half I decided to stick with it. Sniper Elite 5 is a more slow paced game for sure, contrary to its predecessors. Overall movement is more of an actual methodical pace of a sniper. Some will say that this game is a few steps back compared to Sniper Elite 4. In some ways it is. In other ways its better. Here is a quick Pro/Con.

Pro:
- Better Bullet Cam/X-Ray
- Better Bullet Penetration and Bullet Origination (Meaning from Barrel and not HUD Crosshair)
- Better Weapon Customization
- Better Weapon Statistics
- Better Ammo Stripping and Variety Ammo Types
- Disposable Weapon Pickup
- AI Ability to CQC Counter Melee Based on Training (Basic Officers and Infantry can't counter. Only Special Trained.)
- Multi-platform Cross-play (When it works. I have, on a couple occasions, had a disconnect or two.)

Con:
- Missing Weapons (i.e. Mosin Nagant, M1 Garand, PPSH-41, m1897 Trench gun etc.)
- 9 Base Game Mission Campaign (10 with Wolf Mountain DLC. Overall the game is short, though it does not lack detail.)
- Only 3 Base Game Survival Maps
- Movement While OTS Aiming is Really Slow (Specifically for SMG and Pistol, Sniper is alright.)
- High CPU Usage If You Are a Mid/Low-end Content Creator/Streamer (Tweaking stream settings can help mitigate some of this.)
- Rebellions Heavy Reliance on Adding Content as DLC (Specifically Weapons that would actually be in region), as well as Separate Season Passes 

 That is just a quick summary. Knowing Rebellion, they will most likely add some of the mentioned weapons as DLC. But the weapon variety for Snipers feels lacking. There are only 6 Rifles, 6 SMG's, and 6 Pistols (That's excluding the p.38 pre-order bonus). An interesting choice of numbers, but that is only for weapons you can choose for a load-out. However, they did add in the MG42 and PzB 38 Anti-Tank rifle and still have the Panzerfaust. I know this may sound ridiculous but I wish they could have added them into load-out customization to further broaden play-style aspects as well as open up an avenue for ambush operation tactics for both Campaign and Survival. The MG42 could function almost exactly as the Thompson since the Thompson has a 100rnd Drum mag and you could only carry 150rnd's of regular ammo total (Including Magazine) only differences are the obvious.

 Overall customization is nice, from variety of Scopes, Barrel Extensions and Muzzle Attachments to Magazine, Receiver and Grip Modifications. Each weapon features unique customization options. I like the addition of Bayonets as a muzzle attachment for snipers making CQC more of an option since it increases melee range. Cosmetics such as the Desert and Mastery paint-jobs feel uninteresting. And what I mean by that is, its better to keep your SMG and Pistol as default paint-job in that regard (Personally I don't care about flashy cosmetics like the gold Mastery skins from SE4, but more variety in cosmetics like the Cloth wrap or Ghillie wrap that help you blend in I'll take anytime). Character customization however is a yikes. With only being able to choose preset characters for Campaign, Survival and MP as well as only being able to choose a hat as a cosmetic is a bit of a letdown. Now I was not expecting to be able to customize like its an RPG. But being able to choose/edit your Uniform, Vest, Boots or whether or not you wanted a Ghillie suit for Campaign, especially since Axis Invaders get to use a Ghillie or try to blend in as an AI, would definitely add in an interesting or little more intense Cat and Mouse experience. When I think Character customizing, I think Rainbow Six Vegas 2.

 Axis Invasion certainly is an interesting new twist for Sniper Elite. It can definitely be jokingly compared to Dark Souls. But I still need a better understanding on how the invasion occurs. Whether it is just something that can happen at any moment, or is based on if an alarm is triggered. I would err on the side of caution and assume that it is something that can happen any moment while enabled. But what I do know is that you can gain more XP with the risk than without it. And no XP is not throttled if you choose to disable it because you can reach max level quite easily with it disabled. From what I have also seen the game-mode seems to penalize you for camping while being invaded. For balancing reasons I can understand intel-gathering for both the Target player and the Invading player. But if the AI are completely unaware and not alerted then there should be no information relayed to the Invader about the Target player until they do something to make themselves known. It would be a good idea if the invasion mode was based on your play style. Meaning if you were to be stealthy and never trigger alarms or get into prolonged active combat, you would be less likely to get invaded. And for doing so you would be rewarded even more XP for being a True Shadow, at least as an idea that would be great if they did it that way.

 Overall I enjoy the game-play. The new areas give me more variety of environment, and if I ever feel like a change of scenery I won't have to go back to previous titles unless I felt like it. I will say that most of your 1000 hours (I doubt many will spend over 500 hours, but there are those that will) will encompass collecting and completing the challenge medals for campaign if you are a completionist or perfectionist. But everyone is different when it comes to personal preference. I would recommend that if you are on the fence and not sure if it would be worth the regular price to get this, then wait for it to go on sale.

Its another Sniper Elite game. Not much has changed since 4 in the grand scheme of things. Honestly a good point in my book. The campaign seems to be well varied with both close and long range encounters, and plenty of traversal options. If you go loud the game punishes the player with smarter AI than previous games. They will spread out and flank, fall back and alert others, use suppressing fire when the player is not in direct line of sight, and much more. The Axis invasion idea was brilliant(an option you can turn on or off to allow players to invade your campaign). It is also well implemented well with a good balance for both sides(and a camping detector thank God!). However I have to go back on a little bit of what i said in the beginning. I'm honestly not sure if its trying to compete with Ghost Warrior, or just pandering to the ones who want a watered down experience. Suppressors are EVERYWHERE! One would think you could walk into your local hardware store and buy one. I've been playing since the first game, and there was so much more of an authentic challenge back then. Suppressed pistols are available from mission 2, and suppressed rifles by mission 3. The weapon attachments and their provided "upgrades" are simply comical. We are not to Tarkov levels of customization or anything, but hardly any of it is WWII period. I guess this could be chalked up to an alternate universe as we have killed Hilter in plenty of places and times. Still way over the top for WWII and a bit too much. Simplicity here is best imo. Different guns is fine, but when your putting a 6x scope, suppressor and a shoulder stock on a 1911 a line has been crossed. Now that we have the campaign out of the way lets get into multiplayer. Lets also get the disclaimers out of the way. I am a fan of hardcore(no glint, no aim assist, no empty lung zoom, ect) no cross. My opinions here are going to reflect my game play experiences on this game mode specifically. There has been a lot more work put into the framework of multiplayer compared to 4. This title seems primed to grow into a more successful multiplayer than previous titles. However there's only 2 maps.... 2. there's 4 total i believe, but only 2 for no cross. Might as well be 1 though since omg the beach map is trash. The team on the beach has NO cover. While the other side gets trenches, bunkers and plenty of options to move around the map without being seen. The beach side is just screwed. This is also a pretty small map as well. The other map is built much better. 1 side is a little more open, but you can navigate the map mostly in stealth if you traverse the buildings in the back. A little annoying, but if your not going to be patient in a sniper game why are you here lol?? Now my biggest complaint has to be the Assassins Creed style of movement. You character will literally do that annoying thing from AC where if you run up to a wall you cant climb you just run 2 steps up and jump back down killing all your momentum. Its rare, but stupid annoying when it happens. There is no button to hug the wall so the game decides when you use the wall for cover. Let me tell you this happens at the worst times. You're wanting to go around a corner, and your guy just keeps bouncing from one side of the corner to the other. Just like AC I feel this game has severe movement lag. I constantly find myself correcting my characters movements from doing something dumb and its always 1 step behind what I'm doing, and that's how you end up sticking to both sides of a corner 4 times in a row while your trying to make a break for it. It can also be a problem when your trying to hide on a box in a hall from a player. Its hard to get the character to do what you want it to do to prevent your gun from sticking out and blowing your cover. This would be so easy to fix with a simple button command. If this wasn't bad enough the game will change your characters stance on uneven terrain. Almost the entire game is uneven terrain! If the game decides your character cant "fit" into the area your trying to crawl to your character will go from prone to crouch or stand in rare cases with no warning. In a sniper game and in a multiplayer setting this is simply unacceptable as it stands. I'd rather have my character not move than be a whack a mole. Again we get into the laggy movement. I'll often times find myself panicking and pressing the button again since my character didnt do anything quickly and now he will be standing and crouching a couple times before going prone again. Also prone movement is not great. Objects like a curb will prevent the player from going sideways over it(sure it wont be comfortable, but very doable). This is a SNIPER game. If you cant navigate properly while prone something is very wrong. All my complaints aside this is a good game that has the potential to be a better game than it currently is.
